## ADR-0060: Phase-24 scoping — `envoy.filters.http.csrf` as the SECOND per-route `typed_per_filter_config` consumer (proving the phase-23 infrastructure generalizes additively), minimum-viable (decode-side modify-method origin guard; `additional_origins` via `StringMatcher`; `filter_enabled` deterministic-only); deferring `shadow_enabled` / runtime fractional gating / the route>vhost cascade / other per-route filter variants

- **Date:** 2026-06-11.
- **Status:** accepted.
- **Context:** The phase-23 state-6 close-out (commit `3b7cf1384`) left the project AWAITING NEXT PLANNING with ROADMAP rows `00`–`23` all `done`: the MVP trunk (00–08), the HTTP-filters family (09 `local_ratelimit` / 10 `rbac` / 11 `fault` / 22 `jwt_authn` / 23 `cors`), the upstream-robustness family (12–17, "complete in minimum-viable form"), and the xDS / dynamic-config filesystem-transport quartet (18 CDS / 19 LDS / 20 RDS / 21 EDS). **Phase 23 landed the per-route `typed_per_filter_config` infrastructure** — the `@type`-tagged `PerFilterConfig` enum (`crates/envoy-config/src/bootstrap.rs:787`, only the `Cors` variant registered), the HCM route-early-resolution helper (`resolve_route` at `crates/envoy-http1/src/hcm.rs:1195`, reused by H2), the `FilterPipeline::apply_route_config` → `HttpFilterInstance::apply_route_config` → per-filter threading (`crates/envoy-filter/src/{pipeline.rs:66,instance.rs:167,cors.rs:115}`), and the `PerRouteConfigForAbsentFilter` all-fatal validator (`crates/envoy-config/src/lib.rs:531`). This ADR records the phase-24 pick + scope. **The §6.3 anti-pattern (no untested infrastructure) means the per-route infra needs a SECOND consumer to prove it generalizes** — phase 23 deferred exactly this ("`typed_per_filter_config` for filters OTHER than cors: csrf/buffer + per-route fault/rbac/local_ratelimit overrides defer to their own phases"). Within the HTTP-filters family — the richest remaining §9 vein (≈11 filters undone) — **`csrf` was picked** as the second per-route consumer: it is deterministic, header-only, locally-verifiable, and reuses existing infra, and crucially the cross-cutting architectural risk that made phase 23 borderline (the HCM resolving the route AFTER the pipeline) is GONE — phase 24 is a near-pure additive plug-in. A read-only reconnaissance at the brainstorm HEAD `3b7cf1384` established the three reuse facts (SPEC §0): (1) `PerFilterConfig` exists `@type`-tagged for additive extension (the hand-rolled `Route` deserializer at `bootstrap.rs:1404-1435` already parses the `typed_per_filter_config:` map — only an enum variant is needed, no deserializer surgery); (2) the `apply_route_config` dispatch (`instance.rs:167`) is already filter-generic, with `cors.rs:115` the precedent shape; (3) the decode-side `Decision::StopAndSend` 403 short-circuit + the `PerRouteConfigForAbsentFilter` validator + the `decorate_filter_synth_response{,_h2}` helpers + the `header_ci` helper + the `04.x` `StringMatcher` are all reusable verbatim. CSRF is the lightest filter phase since the framework was completed.
- **Alternatives considered (rejected at this brainstorm):**
  - **`buffer`** (`envoy.filters.http.buffer`) — per-route too, and would also exercise the phase-23 infra, but it operates on the request **body** (buffer the full body before forwarding), requiring new body-accumulation machinery in the decode-data path that no filter has exercised to date. Higher risk; deferred to its own phase.
  - **Per-route overrides of existing filters (`fault`/`rbac`/`local_ratelimit`)** — would exercise the per-route infra by adding those filters' configs as `PerFilterConfig` variants + a route-level override merge, but the *interesting* part (the route>vhost `mostSpecificPerFilterConfig` precedence cascade) was explicitly deferred at phase 23, and a pure route-level override is lower new-surface value than a genuinely new filter. Lower leverage than a new filter that ALSO proves the infra.
  - **`compression` (gzip)** — would need a gzip dependency (a foundations-grant ADR; `flate2` is not on the D-3.2 list) AND a decompress-to-compare harness step (zlib output is not byte-exact across implementations → the differential body comparison cannot be byte-exact). Rejected at phase 23 for the same reason; still higher risk than CSRF's pure header inspection.
  - **`ext_authz` / `ext_proc`** — need an external auth service in the differential harness; `ext_proc` is gRPC (still H2-trailers-blocked, re-verified at HEAD). Large infra lift.
  - **Load-balancing family** (least_request / random / ring_hash / maglev / subset / locality / priority) — high value but differential testing is genuinely hard (non-deterministic distribution or byte-exact hash-ring/Maglev reproduction; all need distinguishable-backend harness infra). A larger, riskier first cut.
  - **Folding in the phase-23 M23-6 (token-aware `Connection: close`) + M23-7 (HTTP/1.0 implicit-close) hardening** — offered as a possible foundation slice; declined to keep phase 24 a clean, single-purpose filter phase. The M-track follow-ups stay in the phase-23 `REVIEW.md` ledger.
- **Decision:** Land **`envoy.filters.http.csrf`** as phase 24, minimum-viable, configured **per-route via the phase-23 `typed_per_filter_config` infrastructure** (the SECOND `PerFilterConfig` variant, proving the infra generalizes additively):
  1. **`CsrfPolicy` schema + the second `PerFilterConfig` variant** — add `Csrf(CsrfPolicy)` to `PerFilterConfig` (`bootstrap.rs:787`) + a near-empty filter-chain `Csrf` entry to `HttpFilterTypedConfig` (`:741`, mirroring `CorsConfig {}`); `CsrfPolicy { additional_origins: Vec<StringMatcher> (reuse 04.x), filter_enabled: Option<RuntimeFractionalPercent> (deterministic 0%/100% only) }`, all `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` (rejects `shadow_enabled`). The gating §6.2 item is the exact config shape — whether Envoy requires a chain-level `filter_enabled` or accepts a near-empty chain entry with the policy supplied purely per-route.
  2. **`CsrfFilter`** (the eighth `HttpFilterInstance` variant at `crates/envoy-filter/src/instance.rs:32`, after Router/HeaderMutation/LocalRateLimit/Rbac/Fault/JwtAuthn/Cors) — a new `crates/envoy-filter/src/csrf.rs` module, **decode-side only** (the first decode-only per-route filter): for modify methods (POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH + the non-safe set, §6.2-verified), compute the source origin (`Origin`, fallback `Referer`) vs the target origin (`Host`/`:authority`), valid if equal or matches `additional_origins` → `Decision::Continue`; invalid or missing-source → `Decision::StopAndSend` 403 + the Envoy CSRF failure body, decorated by the existing H1/phase-11-H2 filter-synth helpers (reused unchanged). The per-route policy flows in via the existing `apply_route_config` threading (the `cors.rs:115` precedent — no HCM change). Conditional `http.<stat_prefix>.csrf.{request_valid, request_invalid, missing_source_origin}` stats (namespace §6.2-verified); fixture `0032-http-filter-csrf` (H1, real upstream cluster per ADR-0058 L6; 5 deterministic header-only probes — same-origin-POST→200 / evil-origin-POST→403 / additional-allowed-POST→200 / safe-GET→200 / no-source-POST→403); an in-process backstop; a new `parse_bootstrap` fuzz seed (NO new fuzz target — CSRF reuses `StringMatcher`, introduces no new parser crate); BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT csrf rows. The existing `PerRouteConfigForAbsentFilter` validator is reused verbatim.
  3. **Defer** (each rejected by `deny_unknown_fields` or simply out of scope): `filter_enabled` runtime-keyed fractional gating (needs the unimplemented RTDS runtime — honor only deterministic 0%/100%, the phase-11 fault precedent); `shadow_enabled` shadow/observe-only mode; vhost-level `typed_per_filter_config` + the route>vhost `mostSpecificPerFilterConfig` precedence cascade (phase 23 already deferred vhost-level); `typed_per_filter_config` for filters OTHER than cors/csrf (the mechanism is general; only `Cors` [phase 23] + `Csrf` [this phase] are wired/tested — buffer + per-route fault/rbac/local_ratelimit overrides defer to their own phases); streaming/trailers + gRPC-Web CSRF.
  4. **§6.1 split:** projected single-phase (~900–1300 LoC / ~8–11 tasks — comfortably inside the gate and LIGHTER than phase 23 since the cross-cutting HCM change is already done); the split valve is held in nominal reserve as **`24.1`** (the schema + the `PerFilterConfig::Csrf`/`HttpFilterInstance::Csrf` wiring + validator — a foundation slice) + **`24.2`** (the `CsrfFilter` runtime + stats + fixture 0032 + backstop + parent-24 close), with the split ADR being **ADR-0062** — but the split is very unlikely to fire. The PLAN-writer decides AFTER the §6.2 verification.
- **Rationale:** Per the project's demonstrated preferences (deterministic · locally-verifiable · self-contained · builds on existing infra) CSRF is the standout pick: it is fully differential-testable with zero timing/crypto sensitivity (CSRF is a pure function of request method + `Origin`/`Referer` + `Host` + the policy — header-only, no body, no clock); and, decisively, it is the **second consumer of the per-route `typed_per_filter_config` infrastructure**, which the §6.3 anti-pattern demands to prove the phase-23 infra generalizes additively beyond its single `Cors` consumer. Phase 23 took on the cross-cutting HCM route-early-resolution risk; phase 24 reaps it as a near-pure additive plug-in (an enum arm + a filter module), the lightest filter phase since the framework was completed. Recording the pick + scope here (vs. only in the SPEC) honors D-3.5: a future session must understand WHY phase 24 is csrf (the second per-route consumer), WHY it is a pure plug-in (the phase-23 infra), and WHY buffer/overrides/compression/ext_authz/LB were deferred, without re-deriving the analysis. This mirrors the HTTP-filter-family / xDS-family brainstorm-ADR cadence (ADR-0048/0050/0051/0053/0055/0057).
- **Consequences:**
  - **The phase-24 SPEC (`docs/envoy-rust/phases/24-http-filter-csrf/SPEC.md`) lands at THIS commit** with the D1–D6 deliverables, the §0 reuse findings, the §4 deferral ledger, the §6.1 split projection (single-phase), and the §6.2 PLAN-write empirical-verification checklist (the config shape [verify FIRST — gates D1, the chain-vs-route `filter_enabled` question], the modify-method set, the source/target-origin computation + `Referer` fallback, the 403 failure-body bytes + `content-type` + the missing-source disposition, the stat namespace + semantics, the `filter_enabled`/`shadow_enabled` disposition, the per-route-for-absent-filter reuse). **This §6.2 runs LOCALLY** (CSRF has no virtiofs/inotify dependency).
  - **ROADMAP row `24` enters `planned`** beneath the "HTTP filters family" §9 heading (the sixth concrete row after 09/10/11/22/23). No existing row flips (invariant 4.1.2); row 24 becomes `in-progress` only when the next session's state-2 PLAN-write points STATE at it (invariant 4.1.3).
  - **ADR-0061 is reserved** for the state-2 PLAN-write §6.2 reconciliation (lands inline if any of the config shape / modify-method set / origin computation / 403 failure body / stat semantics / `filter_enabled` disposition diverges materially — the config shape [chain-vs-route `filter_enabled`] and the modify-method set are the most likely triggers). **ADR-0062 is reserved** for the §6.1 split (lands only if phase 24 splits into 24.1/24.2 — very unlikely).
  - **ADR-0014 REMAINS IN FORCE** (the YAML-native shim; CSRF does not engage the xDS protos); **ADR-0028 REMAINS OPEN** (phase 24 does not engage it). ADR-0049's all-fatal config posture is the projected default for the new csrf validators (a non-deterministic `filter_enabled`, and a `CsrfPolicy` on a route with no `csrf` filter in the chain [reusing the ADR-0058 `PerRouteConfigForAbsentFilter` all-fatal reject], are projected startup-fatal — §6.2-verified).
  - **`DECISIONS.md` ledger head: ADR-0060** (this ADR). Next available **ADR-0061** (reserved for the §6.2 reconciliation). Project-cumulative ADR count 61. The phase-24 state-1 brainstorm commit title carries `[ADR-0060]`.
- **Provenance:** the three reuse findings were established by a read-only reconnaissance at the phase-24 brainstorm HEAD `3b7cf1384`: (1) `PerFilterConfig` (the `Cors` variant) at `crates/envoy-config/src/bootstrap.rs:787`, the `typed_per_filter_config` field on `Route` at `:1213`, the hand-rolled deserializer at `:1404-1435`, `CorsPolicy` at `:798`, `CorsConfig {}` at `:821`, `HttpFilterTypedConfig` at `:741`, `StringMatcher` at `:1815` / `StringMatcherMode` at `:1821`; (2) the threading — `resolve_route` at `crates/envoy-http1/src/hcm.rs:1195`, `apply_route_config` at `crates/envoy-filter/src/pipeline.rs:66` → `instance.rs:167` → `cors.rs:115`; (3) the reuse points — `HttpFilterInstance` (variants Router/HeaderMutation/LocalRateLimit/Rbac/Fault/JwtAuthn/Cors) at `crates/envoy-filter/src/instance.rs:32`, `PerRouteConfigForAbsentFilter` at `crates/envoy-config/src/lib.rs:531` (logic at `bootstrap.rs:2605/2695`), the `header_ci` helper at `crates/envoy-filter/src/jwt_authn.rs:156` + the duplicate at `cors.rs:236` (the N=3 consolidation pressure), the latest fixture `tests/fixtures/0031-http-filter-cors` (next is 0032). The §6.2 EMPIRICAL verification against `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` is DEFERRED to the state-2 PLAN-write per the verify-at-PLAN-write discipline (it RUNS LOCALLY — no virtiofs/inotify dependency); this brainstorm ADR locks only the pick + scope, which are decisions, not empirically-discoverable wire shapes. Per D-3.5 this ADR lands at the state-1 brainstorm commit alongside the SPEC it scopes.

## ADR-0061: Phase-24 §6.2 empirical-verification reconciliation — Envoy's CSRF uses ONE `CsrfPolicy` message at BOTH the filter-chain AND per-route levels with a **REQUIRED** `filter_enabled` (the SPEC's near-empty `CsrfConfig {}` projection is WRONG); origin comparison is on **scheme-stripped `host[:port]`** (`Url::hostAndPort()`), NOT `scheme+host+port`; the chain-level policy is an always-applied **base** that a per-route policy **REPLACES** wholesale (a route without an override is still guarded by the chain policy); the 403 body is `Invalid origin` (14 bytes, no newline) `content-type: text/plain`; stats `http.<prefix>.csrf.{request_valid,request_invalid,missing_source_origin}` are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE; the modify set is `{POST,PUT,DELETE,PATCH}`

- **Date:** 2026-06-11.
- **Status:** accepted.
- **Context:** Phase-24 (ADR-0060) deferred the §6.2 empirical verification of the upstream CSRF wire shapes to the state-2 PLAN-write per the ratified verify-at-PLAN-write discipline (the phase-10 ADR-0034 / phase-22 ADR-0056 / phase-23 ADR-0058 inline-at-PLAN-write precedent). The verification ran LOCALLY against `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` (digest `sha256:56da5afd7df364350ff92de4fb49a9b09957c17295f2899f0a31cd12c28770c2`; CSRF has no virtiofs/inotify dependency — the phase-22/23 §6.2-local methodology), driving a canonical H1-listener bootstrap with the `csrf` filter in the chain + a per-route `CsrfPolicy` via `typed_per_filter_config`, proxying to a real all-method-200 backend (sidecar container on a shared Docker network, the ADR-0058 L6 real-upstream constraint). Of the seven §6.2 checklist items, **three diverged MATERIALLY from the SPEC §3 projection** (items 1/3/6) and are reconciled here; the rest CONFIRMED the SPEC and are recorded as PLAN lock-ins (PLAN "L1–L8"; full probe transcript in `phases/24-http-filter-csrf/PROGRESS.md` Task-1 preamble).
- **Findings (the PLAN lock-ins; ✗ = material divergence from SPEC, ✓ = confirmed):**
  1. **✗ DIVERGENCE — config shape (item 1, gates D1).** Envoy's CSRF filter uses a SINGLE proto message `type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.csrf.v3.CsrfPolicy` at BOTH the filter-chain `http_filters[].typed_config` AND the per-route `typed_per_filter_config[envoy.filters.http.csrf]` — there is NO separate near-empty chain config. **`filter_enabled` is a REQUIRED field** (`--mode validate` rejects its absence at BOTH levels: `CsrfPolicyValidationError.FilterEnabled: value is required`). The SPEC §3 D1 projection (a near-empty filter-chain `CsrfConfig {}` mirroring `CorsConfig {}`, plus `filter_enabled: Option<RuntimeFractionalPercent>`) is therefore WRONG. **Schema:** `CsrfPolicy { filter_enabled: RuntimeFractionalPercent (required, NOT Option), additional_origins: Vec<StringMatcher> (default empty) }`, with `RuntimeFractionalPercent { default_value: FractionalPercent (required), runtime_key: Option<String> }` — a NEW config type (the existing `FractionalPercent` at `bootstrap.rs:649` is reused as `default_value`). Both `HttpFilterTypedConfig::Csrf(CsrfPolicy)` (chain) and `PerFilterConfig::Csrf(CsrfPolicy)` (per-route) carry the SAME `CsrfPolicy` type. `additional_origins` elements are `StringMatcher` (`exact`/`suffix` verified). `deny_unknown_fields` rejects the deferred `shadow_enabled`.
  2. **✓ CONFIRMED — modify-method set (item 2).** `{POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH}` are guarded (403 on a cross-origin request); `{GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE}` pass through unconditionally (200, no stat tick). A custom/unknown method (`FOOBAR`) is rejected `400` by Envoy's HTTP layer before CSRF, so the modify set is taken as the explicit hardcoded `{POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH}`.
  3. **✗ DIVERGENCE — origin computation (item 3).** Both the source and the target origin are reduced to **scheme-stripped `host[:port]`** (Envoy `Http::Utility::Url::hostAndPort()`), NOT the full `scheme://host:port` origin the SPEC §1/§3 D2 projected. Empirically: with `Origin: http://additional.example.com`, a route `additional_origins` matcher `exact: "additional.example.com"` → **200** (allowed); `exact: "http://additional.example.com:80"` → **403**; `exact: "additional.example.com:80"` → **403**; `suffix: "additional.example.com"` → **200**. So the source origin from `Origin: http://additional.example.com` is `additional.example.com` (host only — no `:80` synthesized when the URL omits the port). The comparison: **source equals target OR an `additional_origins` `StringMatcher` matches `source`** (the scheme-stripped host[:port] string). Source = `hostAndPort(Origin)`; if `Origin` is absent, `hostAndPort(Referer)` (the Referer fallback CONFIRMED: `Referer`-only same-origin → 200, `Referer`-only evil → 403). `Origin` takes precedence over `Referer` (both present → `Origin` decides). Target = `hostAndPort(Host`/`:authority`)` — a bare `Host: localhost:10000` is not a URL, so it is used verbatim (`localhost:10000`). **envoy-rust `host_and_port(v)`:** if `v` contains `"://"`, take the authority between `"://"` and the next `/` (or end); else return `v` unchanged.
  4. **✓ CONFIRMED byte-exact — the 403 local reply (item 4).** A guarded invalid (or missing-source) modify request yields **`403 Forbidden`**, body **`Invalid origin`** (exactly **14 bytes, NO trailing newline** — `xxd`: `496e 7661 6c69 6420 6f72 6967 696e`), `content-type: text/plain`, `content-length: 14`, `server: envoy`, `date`. The existing H1 `decorate_filter_synth_response` helper (`hcm.rs:1454`) auto-adds `content-type: text/plain` for a non-empty body + stamps `content-length`/`server`/`date`, so the csrf `FilterResponse { status: 403, reason: Some("Forbidden"), headers: vec![], body: b"Invalid origin" }` reproduces Envoy's output byte-for-byte (the rbac `b"RBAC: access denied"` precedent verbatim).
  5. **✓ CONFIRMED — stat namespace + semantics (item 5).** `http.<stat_prefix>.csrf.{request_valid, request_invalid, missing_source_origin}` (HCM-prefixed, identical rooting to rbac/fault/jwt/cors). **MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE, one tick per evaluated modify request:** valid (source allowed) → `request_valid` only; present-but-disallowed source → `request_invalid` only; **no source origin (no `Origin`, no `Referer`) → `missing_source_origin` only** (it does NOT also tick `request_invalid`); safe methods touch NO stat. Empirically a controlled `{same-origin POST, evil POST, additional POST, evil GET, no-source POST}` sequence yields `request_valid: 2, request_invalid: 1, missing_source_origin: 0→0→0→0→1`.
  6. **✗ DIVERGENCE — chain-base / route-replace model (item 6).** `filter_enabled` is honored at the deterministic 0%/100% endpoints (`numerator: 0` → passthrough; `numerator: 100, denominator: HUNDRED` → enforce), the phase-11 fault precedent. **The chain-level `CsrfPolicy` is an always-applied BASE: a route with NO per-route override is STILL guarded by the chain policy** (`/plain POST evil → 403` with only a chain-level policy). **A per-route `CsrfPolicy` REPLACES the chain policy wholesale** (NOT a field-merge): chain=100% + route-override=0% → passthrough; chain=0% + route-override=100% → enforce. So the effective policy = the route's `CsrfPolicy` if present, else the chain `CsrfPolicy`; its `filter_enabled` gate decides enforce-vs-passthrough. This DIVERGES from the cors "`active_policy = None` (inert) when the route carries no config" pattern (`cors.rs:115`) — `CsrfFilter` must compile the chain policy as a base and have `apply_route_config` fall back to it. **envoy-rust disposition (the ADR-0049 all-fatal posture):** reject a non-deterministic `default_value` (`numerator ∉ {0, denominator.value()}`) at startup (a new `ConfigError`, the phase-11 `validate_fault_config` precedent); reject a present `runtime_key` at startup (envoy-rust has no RTDS runtime layer to honor it — a new `ConfigError`); reject `shadow_enabled` via `deny_unknown_fields`. These rejections apply to the `CsrfPolicy` at BOTH the chain and the route level.
  7. **✓ CONFIRMED reuse — policy-for-absent-filter (item 7).** The existing generic `PerRouteConfigForAbsentFilter` all-fatal validator (`crates/envoy-config/src/bootstrap.rs:2696`, iterating `route.typed_per_filter_config.keys()`) already covers a `csrf` per-route policy whose `csrf` filter is absent from the HCM chain — startup-fatal, reused verbatim, no new code (the ADR-0058 L7 divergence: Envoy accepts-and-ignores; envoy-rust stricter-rejects). The no-override-on-route case falls back to the chain policy (finding 6), not to passthrough.
  8. **✓ CONFIRMED reuse — fixture topology (the ADR-0058 L6 constraint).** Fixture 0032 must proxy to a REAL upstream cluster (the `http1-echo-server` helper) — a valid CSRF modify request must reach an upstream to yield a 200 (a `direct_response` route does not engage per-route filter config). The verification harness required a real all-method-200 backend to observe the 200/403 split.
- **Decision:**
  1. Model `CsrfPolicy { filter_enabled: RuntimeFractionalPercent, #[serde(default)] additional_origins: Vec<StringMatcher> }` (finding 1) used at BOTH `HttpFilterTypedConfig::Csrf(CsrfPolicy)` (chain) and `PerFilterConfig::Csrf(CsrfPolicy)` (per-route), with a new `RuntimeFractionalPercent { default_value: FractionalPercent, #[serde(default)] runtime_key: Option<String> }`, all `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`.
  2. Implement `CsrfFilter` with the **chain-base / route-replace** effective-policy model (finding 6): compile the chain `CsrfPolicy` as the base at `build_from_config`; `apply_route_config` sets the active policy to the route's `CsrfPolicy` override if present, else clones the base. The decode-side guard: passthrough if the effective `filter_enabled` is deterministic-0%; passthrough for safe methods; for `{POST,PUT,DELETE,PATCH}` compute `host_and_port` source (`Origin`, fallback `Referer`) vs target (`Host`/`:authority`) (finding 3), 403 + `Invalid origin` (finding 4) on missing-source or unmatched-source, else Continue; tick the mutually-exclusive counter (finding 5).
  3. Reject (startup-fatal, ADR-0049 all-fatal) a non-deterministic `filter_enabled.default_value` and a present `filter_enabled.runtime_key`, at both chain and route level; reject `shadow_enabled` via `deny_unknown_fields` (finding 6). Reuse `PerRouteConfigForAbsentFilter` verbatim (finding 7).
  4. Lock fixture 0032 to a REAL upstream cluster (the `http1-echo-server` helper, the 0008/0030/0031 pattern), NOT `direct_response` (finding 8). The 5 probes: `[POST same-origin→200, POST evil-origin→403+body, POST additional-allowed→200, GET evil-origin→200, POST no-source→403]`; the `additional_origins` matcher is `exact: <backend-host:port>`-shaped (scheme-stripped, finding 3) for the allowed-origin and an `exact:`-mismatching evil origin.
- **Consequences:**
  - The phase-24 `PLAN.md` + `PROGRESS.md` skeleton + Task-1 preamble land at THIS commit (the 06.2→23 standalone-PLAN cadence), carrying these lock-ins as PLAN L1–L8. **§6.1 split-gate: SINGLE PHASE** (7 tasks, refined estimate ~1000–1350 LoC — the schema grew slightly [`RuntimeFractionalPercent` + the chain-base model] but stays well under both §6.1 thresholds; the cross-cutting HCM change already landed at phase 23) — **ADR-0062 (split) does NOT fire.**
  - **ROADMAP row `24` flips `planned → in-progress`** (invariant 4.1.3 — this session's PLAN-write points STATE at it).
  - **`DECISIONS.md` ledger head: ADR-0061** (this ADR). Project-cumulative ADR count 62. Next available **ADR-0062** (reserved-but-unfired for the §6.1 split, which did not fire). ADR-0014 in force; ADR-0028 open.
  - BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md gains the csrf stat rows + the 403 status/`Invalid origin` body row + the scheme-stripped-origin note + the chain-base/route-replace note + the policy-for-absent-filter divergence note at the Task where each is first empirically exercised (the 06.x → 23 contract-cadence).
- **Provenance:** the verification ran LOCALLY on macOS Docker (Docker 28.0.4) against `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` (digest `sha256:56da5afd…`) on 2026-06-11; the probe transcript (config-shape `--mode validate` acceptance + the two required-`filter_enabled` rejections, the modify-method matrix, the origin-matcher-value isolation [4 matcher shapes], the byte-exact 403 body `xxd`, the controlled mutually-exclusive stat sequence, the chain-base/route-replace 2×2 matrix, the Referer fallback + Origin-precedence probes) is preserved in `phases/24-http-filter-csrf/PROGRESS.md` Task-1 preamble. Per ADR-0049 Provenance, the AUTHORITATIVE differential evidence remains the Linux CI run (this local verification is the §6.2 wire-shape lock-in, not the §7.5 gate evidence). Per D-3.5 this reconciliation ADR lands at the state-2 PLAN-write commit.

## ADR-0062: Phase-25 scoping — `envoy.filters.http.buffer` as the THIRD per-route `typed_per_filter_config` consumer AND the project's first body-dependent HTTP filter; minimum-viable two-part scope (Part A: close the pre-existing H1 request-body-forwarding gap [Content-Length-delimited only]; Part B: the `BufferFilter` `max_request_bytes`/413 guard + `BufferPerRoute`); the easy header-only HTTP-filter vein is exhausted, so phase 25 deliberately takes on the body path; deferring chunked/streaming bodies, the generic streaming `decode_data` framework hook, encode-side buffering, the vhost-level cascade, and all heavier HTTP filters

- **Date:** 2026-06-13.
- **Status:** accepted.
- **Context:** The phase-24 state-6 close-out (commit `7243d381f`) left the project AWAITING NEXT PLANNING with ROADMAP rows `00`–`24` all `done`: the MVP trunk (00–08), the HTTP-filters family (09 `local_ratelimit` / 10 `rbac` / 11 `fault` / 22 `jwt_authn` / 23 `cors` / 24 `csrf`), the upstream-robustness family (12–17, "complete in minimum-viable form"), and the xDS / dynamic-config filesystem-transport quartet (18 CDS / 19 LDS / 20 RDS / 21 EDS). A read-only reconnaissance at the brainstorm HEAD `7243d381f` established the decisive scoping fact (SPEC §0): **the HTTP filter framework is HEADERS-ONLY** (`HttpFilterInstance`/`FilterPipeline` expose only `decode_headers`+`encode_headers` returning `Decision { Continue, StopAndSend }`; `crates/envoy-filter/src/pipeline.rs:11-15,76-84`, `instance.rs:138`), and **all seven shipped feature filters are header-only decode-side decisions** (header_mutation/local_ratelimit/rbac/fault/jwt/cors/csrf). The easy header-only HTTP-filter vein is therefore EXHAUSTED — every remaining HTTP filter needs a body path (`buffer`, `compression`), an external service (`ext_authz`, `ext_proc`, global `ratelimit`, `oauth2`), an embedded engine (`lua`, `wasm`), or non-deterministic timing (`bandwidth_limit`, `adaptive_concurrency`, `admission_control`). Phase 25 is a genuine inflection point. The recon further established the request-body data path is asymmetric and partly ABSENT: **H1 does NOT forward request bodies upstream** — the router builds the upstream request with `body: Some(Bytes::new())` always-empty (`crates/envoy-http1/src/hcm.rs:356`, comment "Chunked-request-body forwarding is a SPEC §4 non-goal") and drains-and-discards the downstream body (`:678-697`); whereas **H2 already fully buffers the request body** into `BytesMut` before the pipeline (`crates/envoy-http2/src/hcm.rs:437-448`, exposed as `FilterRequest.body: Some(Bytes)` at `:473`) and forwards it upstream. So envoy-rust currently cannot proxy an H1 POST body at all — a pre-existing functional gap carried since phase 04.3.
- **Alternatives considered (rejected at this brainstorm):**
  - **The Load-Balancing family** (least_request / random / ring_hash / maglev / subset / locality / priority) — the highest strategic ceiling (LB is a marquee proxy capability; only round-robin exists), and a header-hashed `ring_hash`/`maglev` is deterministic → byte-exact differential. But it is the larger, riskier first cut: a new family + a new reusable distinguishable-backend harness + the hash-ring/Maglev table math; it cuts against the project's demonstrated low-differential-risk grain. Deferred to its own (likely split) phase.
  - **The Network-filters family opener** (`sni_cluster` / network `direct_response` / `echo`) — light and deterministic, but low leverage (niche filters that unlock little; the network filter chain already runs HCM + tcp_proxy). Deferred.
  - **The heavier HTTP filters** — `compression` (gzip dep [not on the D-3.2 list] + non-byte-exact bodies), `ext_authz`/`ext_proc` (external auth service in the harness; `ext_proc` is gRPC, still H2-trailers-blocked), global `ratelimit` (external RLS gRPC service), `oauth2` (external token endpoint + redirects + SDS secrets + HMAC cookies + timing), `lua`/`wasm` (embedded engines — multi-phase sub-projects), `bandwidth_limit`/`adaptive_concurrency`/`admission_control` (timing/statistical, non-deterministic). All higher-infra or non-deterministic than buffer.
  - **An H2-only buffer exploiting H2's incidental pre-buffering** (length-check the already-buffered body, no H1 change) — the lightest possible cut, but it builds NO body-path infrastructure and leaves the real H1 request-body-forwarding gap unaddressed (nearly cosmetic on H2). Rejected in favor of closing the genuine gap.
  - **A pure H1-request-body-forwarding phase with the buffer filter deferred to phase 26** — the cleanest single-purpose decomposition, but it ships a foundation with no consumer (the §6.3 anti-pattern tension), and the foundation is best motivated + exercised by its first consumer. Folded into phase 25 as Part A with the buffer filter as Part B (the §6.1 split valve splits them if the LoC warrants).
- **Decision:** Land **`envoy.filters.http.buffer`** as phase 25, minimum-viable, in a deliberate two-part scope:
  1. **Part A (foundation; projected `25.1`): close the H1 request-body-forwarding gap.** Read the Content-Length-delimited downstream request body into a `Bytes`, populate `FilterRequest.body` on H1 (today `None`), and forward it upstream (replacing `body: Some(Bytes::new())` at `hcm.rs:356`) instead of draining-and-discarding (`:678-697`). Regression-equivalence (all 32 existing Docker-gated fixtures green simultaneously) is the load-bearing invariant — the 07.1/12.1/14.1/23.1 foundation-slice pattern. Chunked/streaming request bodies remain a recorded non-goal (Content-Length only).
  2. **Part B (the filter; projected `25.2`): `BufferFilter`.** The NINTH `HttpFilterInstance` variant (`instance.rs:32`), a new `crates/envoy-filter/src/buffer.rs`, **decode-side only**: in `decode_headers`, with the full body available as `FilterRequest.body` (Part A on H1 / the codec on H2), reject `body.len() > effective_max_request_bytes` with `Decision::StopAndSend` 413 (Envoy's payload-too-large body, decorated by the existing H1/phase-11-H2 filter-synth helpers — §6.2-verified byte-exact), else Continue. Configured per-route via `BufferPerRoute` (the THIRD `PerFilterConfig` variant after `Cors`+`Csrf` — disable for a route, or override the per-route limit), threaded through the existing phase-23 `apply_route_config` hook (NO HCM change). `Buffer { max_request_bytes }` chain-level config; conditional `http.<stat_prefix>.buffer.*` stats (namespace §6.2-verified); fixture `0033-http-filter-buffer` (H1, real `http1-echo-server` upstream per ADR-0058 L6; 5 deterministic header+body probes — within-limit→200+echoed-body / over-limit→413 / per-route-disabled→200 / per-route-lowered-limit→413 / GET-no-body→200); an in-process backstop; a new `parse_bootstrap` fuzz seed (NO new fuzz target). Reuse the `PerRouteConfigForAbsentFilter` all-fatal validator verbatim.
  3. **Defer** (each rejected by `deny_unknown_fields` or simply out of scope): chunked/streaming request bodies; the generic streaming `decode_data` framework hook (not needed for whole-body buffering — deferred to the first body-transforming filter, e.g. compression); response/encode-side buffering; vhost-level `BufferPerRoute` + the route>vhost `mostSpecificPerFilterConfig` cascade; `typed_per_filter_config` for filters OTHER than cors/csrf/buffer; gRPC/trailers; per_try_timeout/retry interplay beyond existing.
  4. **§6.1 split:** projected two-part (~1300–2000 LoC / ~10–13 tasks). **The split is LIKELY to fire** (unlike phases 23/24's nominal reserve) because Part A is a genuine regression-sensitive foundation slice — into `25.1` (Part A; no new fixture; all 32 existing fixtures green) + `25.2` (Part B + fixture `0033` + parent-25 close), with the split ADR being **ADR-0064**. The PLAN-writer decides AFTER the §6.2 verification refines the estimate.
- **Rationale:** The easy header-only HTTP-filter vein is exhausted; among the body-dependent filters, `buffer` is the standout minimum-viable pick — it needs no external service, no engine, no gzip dependency, and no non-deterministic timing (it is a pure function of request method + body length + policy; header+body, no clock, no crypto → fully differential-testable byte-exact). It is the THIRD consumer of the per-route `typed_per_filter_config` infrastructure (the §6.3 anti-pattern continues to be served — the infra now has cors+csrf+buffer), and it forces the project to honestly close a real pre-existing functional gap (H1 request-body forwarding) rather than exploit H2's incidental pre-buffering for a near-cosmetic win. Recording the pick + scope here (vs only in the SPEC) honors D-3.5: a future session must understand WHY phase 25 is buffer (the lightest body-dependent filter at the HTTP-filter inflection point), WHY it has a foundation slice (H1 does not forward request bodies today), and WHY LB / network-filters / the heavier HTTP filters were deferred, without re-deriving the analysis. This mirrors the HTTP-filter-family brainstorm-ADR cadence (ADR-0048/0050/0051/0053/0055/0057/0060).
- **Consequences:**
  - **The phase-25 SPEC (`docs/envoy-rust/phases/25-http-filter-buffer/SPEC.md`) lands at THIS commit** with the §0 recon findings, the D1–D6 deliverables, the §4 deferral ledger, the §6.1 split projection (two-part, split LIKELY), and the §6.2 PLAN-write empirical-verification checklist (the 413 body bytes [verify FIRST — gates D2/§2.2], the `Buffer`/`BufferPerRoute` wire shapes, the buffer stat namespace, the no-body/GET disposition, the `==`-limit boundary, the absent-filter reuse, the real-upstream constraint). **This §6.2 runs LOCALLY** (buffer has no virtiofs/inotify dependency).
  - **ROADMAP row `25` enters `planned`** beneath the "HTTP filters family" §9 heading (the seventh concrete row after 09/10/11/22/23/24). No existing row flips (invariant 4.1.2); row 25 becomes `in-progress` only when the next session's state-2 PLAN-write points STATE at it (invariant 4.1.3).
  - **ADR-0063 is reserved** for the state-2 PLAN-write §6.2 reconciliation (lands inline if the 413 body / `Buffer` shape / `BufferPerRoute` oneof shape / stat namespace diverges materially — the 413 body bytes and the `BufferPerRoute` shape are the most likely triggers). **ADR-0064 is reserved** for the §6.1 split (LIKELY to fire — Part A is a genuine foundation slice).
  - **ADR-0014 REMAINS IN FORCE** (the YAML-native shim; buffer does not engage the xDS protos); **ADR-0028 REMAINS OPEN** (phase 25 does not engage it). ADR-0049's all-fatal config posture is the projected default for the new buffer validators (an invalid `max_request_bytes` is projected startup-fatal — §6.2-verified).
  - **`DECISIONS.md` ledger head: ADR-0062** (this ADR). Next available **ADR-0063** (reserved for the §6.2 reconciliation). Project-cumulative ADR count 63. The phase-25 state-1 brainstorm commit title carries `[ADR-0062]`.
- **Provenance:** the recon facts were established by a read-only reconnaissance at the phase-25 brainstorm HEAD `7243d381f`: the headers-only framework (`crates/envoy-filter/src/pipeline.rs:11-15,76-84`, `instance.rs:32-77,103-136,138,180-190`); the H1 always-empty upstream body + drain-and-discard (`crates/envoy-http1/src/hcm.rs:356,635,678-697`); the H2 pre-buffering (`crates/envoy-http2/src/hcm.rs:437-448,473`); the per-route plumbing (`crates/envoy-config/src/bootstrap.rs:791,1247,1413-1515,2728-2735`); the filter-synth decoration helpers (`crates/envoy-http1/src/hcm.rs:1454-1499`, `crates/envoy-http2/src/response.rs:70-110`); the body-echoing `http1-echo-server` (`tests/helpers/http1-echo-server/src/main.rs:149-244`); the latest fixture `tests/fixtures/0032-http-filter-csrf` (next is 0033). The §6.2 EMPIRICAL verification against `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` is DEFERRED to the state-2 PLAN-write per the verify-at-PLAN-write discipline (it RUNS LOCALLY); this brainstorm ADR locks only the pick + scope, which are decisions, not empirically-discoverable wire shapes. Per D-3.5 this ADR lands at the state-1 brainstorm commit alongside the SPEC it scopes.

## ADR-0063: Phase-25 §6.2 reconciliation — empirical verification of `envoy.filters.http.buffer` against `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` at the state-2 PLAN-write; the 413 over-limit local reply is `Payload Too Large` (17 bytes); the reject boundary is strictly `>` `max_request_bytes`; Envoy emits NO buffer-scoped stats (the over-limit 413 is reflected only in the generic HCM `downstream_rq_too_large`) → the SPEC §2.1 buffer-stats row is DROPPED; the `Buffer` / `BufferPerRoute` wire shapes match the ADR-0062 projection; a `BufferPerRoute` per-route config whose `buffer` filter is absent from the chain is ACCEPTED (inert) by Envoy but the generic `PerRouteConfigForAbsentFilter` validator is reused verbatim per the cors/csrf precedent

- **Date:** 2026-06-13.
- **Status:** accepted.
- **Context:** ADR-0062 §2.4 reserved ADR-0063 for the state-2 PLAN-write §6.2 empirical reconciliation, to land inline "iff the 413 body / `Buffer` shape / `BufferPerRoute` oneof shape / stat namespace diverges materially from the SPEC projection." The §6.2 verification ran LOCALLY (buffer has no virtiofs/inotify dependency) against `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` (image id `56da5afd7df3`, the ADR-0058 digest) on macOS Docker 28.0.4 on 2026-06-13, via (a) two `--mode validate` probes for the config wire shapes + a bogus-`@type` negative control, and (b) a live container (`envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` listener on `:10000`, admin on `:9901`) on a shared Docker network with a `mccutchen/go-httpbin:v2.15.0` sidecar upstream (the `project_docker_sidecar_backend_for_62_verify` methodology — `host.docker.internal` is IPv6-only on macOS Docker → 503s) driving curl probes for the data-plane dispositions + an admin `/stats` scrape. **ADR-0063 FIRES** because the stat namespace diverged materially (Envoy emits NO buffer-scoped stats — see finding 4).
- **Findings (the SPEC §6.2 8-item checklist; each gates a deliverable):**
  1. **413 over-limit local reply (gates D2/§2.2) — RESOLVED:** an over-limit POST (11 bytes > chain `max_request_bytes: 10`) yields `HTTP/1.1 413 Payload Too Large` with body bytes `Payload Too Large` (**17 bytes**, hex `50 61 79 6c 6f 61 64 20 54 6f 6f 20 4c 61 72 67 65`, **NO trailing newline**), `content-type: text/plain`, `content-length: 17`, `server: envoy`, `connection: close`. **Byte-identical at the chain level AND at a per-route `BufferPerRoute`-lowered limit.** This is Envoy's standard payload-too-large local reply; the existing `decorate_filter_synth_response{,_h2}` helpers reproduce this framing verbatim (the rbac `"RBAC: access denied"` / csrf `"Invalid origin"` byte-exact precedent).
  2. **`Buffer` config shape (gates D3) — CONFIRMED as projected:** `@type: type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.buffer.v3.Buffer`; the single field `max_request_bytes` accepts a plain integer (proto `UInt32Value`); `--mode validate` accepted `max_request_bytes: 10`.
  3. **`BufferPerRoute` shape (gates D3) — CONFIRMED as projected:** `@type: type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.buffer.v3.BufferPerRoute`; the oneof `override { disabled: bool; buffer: Buffer }` — both `disabled: true` and `buffer: { max_request_bytes: 4 }` `--mode validate`-accepted.
  4. **Buffer stat namespace (gates D5/§2.1) — MATERIAL DIVERGENCE (the ADR-0063 trigger):** Envoy v1.33.0 emits **NO `http.<stat_prefix>.buffer.*` counters at all**. The admin `/stats` scrape after a probe burst (8×2xx + 2×413) showed the over-limit rejections reflected ONLY in the **generic HCM counter `http.ingress_http.downstream_rq_too_large` (= 2)** plus `downstream_rq_4xx` (= 2) / `downstream_rq_response_before_rq_complete` (= 2) / `downstream_rq_rx_reset` (= 2). Per ADR-0062 / SPEC §2.1 ("if Envoy exposes no buffer-scoped stats, this row is dropped and the phase asserts only the data-plane 200/413 split"), **the SPEC §2.1 buffer-stats deliverable is DROPPED**: phase 25.2 wires NO buffer-scoped stats and adds NO stats-related `ConfigError`. This is differentially safe — the fixture-0032 `expectations.yaml` precedent asserts NO HCM-level stats block (stats are not compared per-probe in the HTTP-filter fixtures), so the absence of a buffer stat surface needs no fixture assertion.
  5. **No-body / GET disposition (gates D6 probe 5) — RESOLVED:** a no-body `GET /` → **200** passthrough (the filter does not tick or reject a no-body request).
  6. **`==`-limit boundary (gates D2) — RESOLVED:** the reject is **strictly `>` `max_request_bytes`**: at chain `max_request_bytes: 10`, 9 bytes → 200, exactly 10 bytes → 200, 11 bytes → 413; at per-route `max_request_bytes: 4`, 3 bytes → 200, exactly 4 bytes → 200, 5 bytes → 413. So `BufferFilter` rejects iff `body.len() > effective_max_request_bytes`.
  7. **Per-route-for-absent-filter reuse (gates D3) — NUANCE (recorded, not closed):** a `BufferPerRoute` per-route config attached to a route whose chain has NO `buffer` filter is **ACCEPTED (config OK, inert)** by Envoy v1.33.0 — `buffer` is a compiled-in extension, so Envoy parses the per-route config regardless of chain membership (the negative control — a bogus `@type` — DID fail hard with `could not find @type`, proving `--mode validate` is not merely lenient). envoy-rust's generic `PerRouteConfigForAbsentFilter` validator (`crates/envoy-config/src/bootstrap.rs:2729-2737`) instead REJECTS this all-fatally — a pre-existing project posture already shared by `cors` (phase 23) and `csrf` (phase 24). **RESOLUTION:** reuse the generic validator verbatim (it iterates `typed_per_filter_config.keys()` against the chain's `present_http_filter_names`, so `buffer` is covered with ZERO new code). The divergence is NOT differentially exercised (fixture 0033 always carries `buffer` in the chain) and is left consistent with cors/csrf rather than reopened this phase; closing it (accept-inert per Envoy) is a recorded cross-cutting M-track candidate touching all three consumers, out of phase-25 scope.
  8. **Real-upstream fixture constraint (gates D6, ADR-0058 L6) — CONFIRMED:** a within-limit POST (5 bytes < 10) reached the live `go-httpbin` upstream and the body (`hello`) was echoed in the upstream's reflected `data` field → 200. Confirms a within-limit buffered request must reach a REAL upstream to yield a body-echoing 200 (a `direct_response` route engages neither per-route filter config nor body forwarding). Fixture 0033 therefore uses a real `http1-echo-server` upstream (the 0030/0031/0032 pattern).
- **Residual (deferred to the 25.2 state-2 PLAN-write):** the disposition of an absent / `0` / malformed `max_request_bytes` was NOT probed this session (the live probes used valid limits 10 and 4). The 25.2 PLAN-write verifies it locally; the projected default is the ADR-0049 all-fatal startup-rejection posture for an unsupported value, but the empirical Envoy disposition governs.
- **Decision:** lock the §6.2-verified shapes for phase 25.2: (a) the 413 over-limit reply is `Payload Too Large` (17 bytes, no trailing newline) + `content-type: text/plain`, reproduced by the existing `decorate_filter_synth_response{,_h2}` helpers; (b) `BufferFilter` rejects iff `body.len() > effective_max_request_bytes` (strict `>`); (c) NO buffer-scoped stats (the SPEC §2.1 row is dropped); (d) `Buffer { max_request_bytes: u32 }` + `BufferPerRoute` oneof `{ disabled: bool, buffer: Buffer }` as the third `PerFilterConfig` variant; (e) reuse the generic `PerRouteConfigForAbsentFilter` validator verbatim (no buffer-specific absent-filter code).
- **Consequences:**
  - Phase 25.2's D3 schema is `Buffer { max_request_bytes }` on `HttpFilterTypedConfig` + `BufferPerRoute` oneof `{ disabled, buffer }` on `PerFilterConfig`; D5's buffer-stats sub-deliverable is ELIMINATED (no stats wiring, no stats `ConfigError`, no BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT stat row); the §2.2 BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT row records the 413 `Payload Too Large` body byte-exact.
  - Phase 25.1 (Part A) is unaffected by this ADR (it ships no filter / config / stats) EXCEPT that the over-limit case it enables in 25.2 depends on Part A reading the full body before the pipeline — confirmed compatible.
  - **`DECISIONS.md` ledger head: ADR-0063** (this ADR). Next available **ADR-0064** (the §6.1 split, below). Project-cumulative ADR count 64.
- **Provenance:** the §6.2 probe transcript (the `/tmp/buf62` `validate-ok.yaml` / `validate-absent.yaml` / `validate-bogus.yaml` config-shape probes; the live-container curl dispositions; the admin `/stats` scrape) is preserved in `docs/envoy-rust/phases/25.1-h1-request-body-forwarding/PROGRESS.md`'s Task-1 preamble. Per ADR-0049 Provenance, the AUTHORITATIVE differential evidence remains the Linux CI run (this local verification is the §6.2 wire-shape lock-in, not the §7.5 gate evidence). Per D-3.5 this reconciliation ADR lands at the state-2 PLAN-write commit.

## ADR-0064: Phase-25 §6.1 split — SPLIT `25` into `25.1` (Part A — close the H1 request-body-forwarding gap; a regression-sensitive always-active hot-path foundation slice; NO new fixture) + `25.2` (Part B — the `BufferFilter` + `BufferPerRoute` + fixture `0033` + parent-25 close), DESPITE the §6.2-refined estimate landing UNDER the §6.1 numeric gate, because Part A is an always-active change to the H1 request data path (more regression-sensitive than the inert-when-unconfigured foundation-slice precedents) that warrants an isolated green + reviewed gate before the additive filter layers on

- **Date:** 2026-06-13.
- **Status:** accepted.
- **Context:** ADR-0062 §6.1 / SPEC §6.1 projected the §6.1 split as LIKELY (the pre-§6.2 estimate was ~1300–2000 LoC / ~10–13 tasks) and reserved ADR-0064 for it, deferring the decision to AFTER the §6.2 verification refined the LoC. The §6.2 verification (ADR-0063) refined BOTH parts DOWNWARD: Part A (H1 body forwarding) is mechanically contained — `run_attempt(req: &Request, …)` (`crates/envoy-http1/src/hcm.rs:315-321`) already takes `req` by reference and builds the upstream `out_req` from it (`:349-357`), so Part A reads the Content-Length body once into a `Bytes`, populates `req.body`, and each attempt clones it into `out_req.body` (`:356`, replay-safe — mirroring the H2 side); the discard-drain already exists (`:678-697`) and is merely relocated-and-accumulated before the pipeline. Estimate ~250–400 LoC / ~3 tasks. Part B is LIGHTER than the SPEC projection because ADR-0063 DROPPED the buffer-stats deliverable (no stats wiring / no stats `ConfigError`) and the 413 reuses the existing decorate helpers verbatim and the absent-filter validator is reused verbatim — estimate ~800 LoC / ~8 tasks. Combined ~1050–1200 LoC / ~11 tasks — **UNDER the §6.1 numeric gate** (`> ~25 tasks` OR `> ~1500 LoC`).
- **Decision:** **SPLIT phase `25` into `25.1` + `25.2`** even though the numeric gate is not crossed. The §6.1 split valve is used here in its **risk-isolation** mode (not its LoC-overflow mode): Part A is an **always-active** change to the H1 request data path — after Part A, EVERY H1 request reads its Content-Length body before the pipeline and forwards it upstream, whereas today the path drains-and-discards. This is structurally MORE regression-sensitive than the inert-when-unconfigured foundation slices (`05.1`/`07.1`/`12.1`/`14.1`/`23.1`, which were transparent until their feature was configured): a subtle body-read-relocation bug (keep-alive pipelining, idle-timeout drain semantics, retry body-replay, the `bytes_consumed`/`buf.advance` accounting) could break many existing H1 fixtures at once. Isolating Part A as `25.1` — whose load-bearing acceptance is "all 32 existing Docker-gated fixtures green simultaneously" with NO new fixture — gives the hot-path change its own green + reviewed gate before the additive `BufferFilter` (`25.2`) layers on. This matches the foundation-slice precedent (`07.1`/`12.1`/`14.1`/`23.1`) and the SPEC/ADR-0062/ROADMAP "split LIKELY" framing; splitting is "cheap, expected, and encouraged" (BOOTSTRAP §6.1 / D-3.6).
- **Alternatives considered:** a SINGLE un-split phase 25 (permissible since the numeric gate is not crossed — the phase-15/16/17/22/24 single-phase precedent) was REJECTED: it would tangle the regression-sensitive always-active Part-A hot-path change with the additive Part-B filter in one review, defeating the isolation that makes a Part-A defect diagnosable. The lighter LoC does not offset Part A's always-active regression surface.
- **Consequences:**
  - **`25.1` (`25.1-h1-request-body-forwarding`; depends-on `04 07`):** Deliverable **D1** only — relocate the H1 Content-Length-delimited request-body read to BEFORE the filter pipeline (accumulate into a `Bytes` rather than discard at `hcm.rs:678-697`), populate `FilterRequest.body` (today `None` on H1 at `:635`), and forward it upstream (`out_req.body = req.body.clone()` at `:356`, replacing `Some(Bytes::new())`). Load-bearing invariant: all 32 existing Docker-gated fixtures (`0001`–`0032`) green simultaneously. NO new fixture; NO new crate; chunked/streaming request bodies remain a non-goal (the `:656` 501 rejection is preserved). A BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT note records H1 request-body forwarding (Content-Length-delimited). The body-forwarding capability is verified by an in-process capturing-upstream unit test in `25.1`; it is DIFFERENTIALLY proven by `25.2`'s fixture `0033` (within-limit → 200 + echoed body) — the foundation-slice-exercised-by-its-consumer pattern.
  - **`25.2` (`25.2-http-filter-buffer`; depends-on `23 25.1`):** Deliverables **D2–D6** — `BufferFilter` (the ninth `HttpFilterInstance` variant; decode-side-only: `body.len() > effective_max_request_bytes` → `Decision::StopAndSend` 413 `Payload Too Large` via the existing decorate helpers per ADR-0063, else `Continue`) + `Buffer { max_request_bytes: u32 }` chain config + `BufferPerRoute` oneof `{ disabled, buffer }` as the third `PerFilterConfig` variant + reuse of the generic `PerRouteConfigForAbsentFilter` validator (ADR-0063) + NO stats (ADR-0063) + fixture `0033-http-filter-buffer` (H1 → real `http1-echo-server`; the 5 probes of SPEC §1) + an `http1_probe_list` harness extension carrying a request body + an in-process backstop + a new `parse_bootstrap` fuzz seed (NO new fuzz target) + the parent-25 close.
  - **ROADMAP:** parent row `25` flips `planned → in-progress` with `sub-phases = 25.1, 25.2`; a new `25.1` row enters `in-progress` (STATE points at it and its `PLAN.md` lands at this commit); a new `25.2` row enters `planned`. Parent `25` flips `done` only after both sub-phases are `done` (the `02`/`12`/`13`/`14` parent-row schema, invariant 4.1.2).
  - **STATE:** advances to active phase `25.1`, lifecycle state-2-complete / state-3-next, next expected skill `superpowers:subagent-driven-development` (this PLAN-write session also lands `25.1`'s `PLAN.md` + `PROGRESS.md` skeleton + Task-1 preamble, per the verify-at-PLAN-write cadence and the split STOP condition — the next session BEGINS `25.1`'s subagent-driven implementation).
  - **`DECISIONS.md` ledger head: ADR-0064** (this ADR). Next available **ADR-0065**. ADR-0014 in force; ADR-0028 open. The phase-25 split commit title carries `[ADR-0063, ADR-0064]`.
- **Provenance:** the split decision follows the §6.2 verification (ADR-0063) and the read-only recon of the H1 body path (`crates/envoy-http1/src/hcm.rs:315-357,580-697`; `crates/envoy-filter/src/types.rs:28-35`) at code-HEAD `9b0e7b925`. Per D-3.5 this ADR lands at the state-2 PLAN-write / split commit.

## ADR-0065: Phase-26 scoping — PIVOT from the (exhausted) HTTP-filters family to the xDS / dynamic-config family's prime follow-up, HOT RELOAD, at its minimum-viable increment: file-based RDS hot-reload (poll-based file watch + atomic route-table swap + per-reload `rds.*` counter advancement + `RoutesConfigDump` version update + fixture `0034`); the FIRST post-construction live mutation in the project, chosen as the LEAST invasive one (the route table is already a swappable `Arc` and route matching is per-request stateless); defer CDS/LDS/EDS hot-reload, inotify-exactness/`watched_directory`, SDS/RTDS, the gRPC/ADS transport, delta xDS, and the ADR-0014 protos supersession

- **Date:** 2026-06-15.
- **Status:** accepted.
- **Context:** Parent phase `25` (`envoy.filters.http.buffer`) closed at the phase-25.2 state-6 deterministic close-out (HEAD `28e03a831`), advancing STATE to a phase-`26` placeholder at state-1-next. The phase-26 state-1 brainstorm (`superpowers:brainstorming`) had to pick + scope phase 26 from the `ROADMAP.md` §9 feature-family candidate lists, since the sequential rows END at `25.2` (no pre-numbered row `26`). The pick is a genuine fork: the **HTTP-filters family's light/deterministic vein is EXHAUSTED** — all eight shipped filters (header_mutation/local_ratelimit/rbac/fault/jwt_authn/cors/csrf/buffer) are header- or whole-body decode-side decisions, and buffer (the phase-25 pick) was explicitly chosen as "the lightest remaining body-dependent filter" (ADR-0062). Every remaining HTTP-filters candidate violates the project's deterministic-locally-verifiable-byte-exact-differential doctrine (see Options).
- **Options considered:**
  - **xDS hot-reload — file-based RDS (CHOSEN).** Every xDS phase (18/19/20/21) named file watching / hot reload "the family's prime follow-up" with explicitly-increasing ROI. RDS hot-reload is the cleanest live mutation: the HCM route table is already `route_config: Arc<RouteConfiguration>` (`crates/envoy-http1/src/hcm.rs:122`), route matching is per-request stateless, and the periodic-watch task is the FIFTH instance of an established primitive (`envoy-health::Scheduler` + the 13.x/14.2 sweepers, shared `CancellationToken` discipline). It reuses the entire phase-20 RDS load path (parser + validator + `rds.*` stats + `RoutesConfigDump`) — no new crate, no new dependency (poll-based mtime watch + a dep-free `RwLock<Arc<…>>`/`tokio::sync::watch` swap handle), no new data-plane harness driver. Deterministic via settle-then-probe (the 12.2 pattern). The one cost: the reload trigger is unobservable on macOS Docker (virtiofs) → the §6.2 verification + fixture 0034 differential are Linux-CI-authoritative (ADR-0049 Provenance; the phase-21 EDS precedent for watching-class phases).
  - **The remaining HTTP filters (REJECTED — doctrine departure).** `compression` (byte-fragile — zlib/brotli output must match Envoy byte-for-byte across versions; the ADR-0062 gzip-dep rejection stands); `ext_authz`/`ext_proc`/global `ratelimit`/`oauth2` (require an EXTERNAL service [gRPC/HTTP] + a new harness; `ext_proc` is gRPC, still H2-trailers-blocked; `oauth2` adds token endpoints + redirects + SDS secrets + HMAC + timing); `lua`/`wasm` (embedded ENGINES — multi-phase sub-projects); `bandwidth_limit`/`adaptive_concurrency`/`admission_control` (timing/statistical, non-deterministic). All are external-service, engine, or non-deterministic — each a doctrine departure for a clean next cut.
  - **The LB-family opener (REJECTED — deferred again).** Deterministic hash LB (`ring_hash`/`maglev`) or `least_request` is foundational (unblocks multi-endpoint EDS / locality / priority), but needs a NEW distinguishable-backend harness and was explicitly deferred at the phase-25 brainstorm (ADR-0062) as "larger/riskier first cut." RDS hot-reload needs at most a two-distinguishable-cluster pair (a far smaller harness step, §6.2 item 3), not a general distinguishable-backend framework.
  - **EDS / CDS / LDS hot-reload FIRST (REJECTED — harder live mutations).** EDS endpoint reload churns the connection pool + LB state; CDS cluster add/remove spawns/tears-down pools + health checkers + outlier sweepers + budgets; LDS listener add/remove binds/unbinds sockets + drains connections. All are heavier live mutations than the stateless route-table pointer swap. RDS establishes the watcher + atomic-swap primitive that these layer onto in deferred follow-ups (§4).
  - **The gRPC/ADS xDS transport (REJECTED — protos-blocked).** Requires tonic + envoy-protos/prost + the ADS state machine + the ADR-0014 protos supersession — re-verified blocked (the gRPC family is also H2-trailers-blocked). A multi-phase sub-project, not a single increment.
  - **The Network-filters opener (REJECTED — low leverage).** `echo`/`direct_response`/`sni_cluster` are light and deterministic but niche (the ADR-0062 / ADR-0064 low-leverage rejection stands).
- **Decision:** Land **file-based RDS hot-reload** as phase `26` (`26-xds-rds-hot-reload`), minimum-viable. Deliverables D1–D8 (SPEC §3): D1 migrate `HCMConfig.route_config` from an owned `Arc<RouteConfiguration>` to a shared atomically-swappable handle (dep-free `RwLock<Arc<…>>`/`tokio::sync::watch`); D2 an `RdsWatcher` — the fifth periodic-background primitive (poll mtime, `CancellationToken` discipline, `envoy-bin`-spawned beside the 12.2/13.x/14.2 tasks); D3 the reload pipeline (re-parse via the existing `rds.rs` → re-validate route→cluster refs against the immutable live cluster set → atomic swap; tick the phase-20 `rds.*` counters per reload; warm-reject keeping the last-good table on a bad reload — the one ADR-0049 startup-all-fatal carve-out, §5.5); D4 the per-reload counter increments; D5 the `RoutesConfigDump` version/`last_updated` update read through the swappable handle; D6 the one new harness capability (mid-test fixture-file rewrite + settle-then-probe); D7 fixture `0034-xds-rds-hot-reload` (two distinguishable real `http1-echo-server` clusters; three-phase pre-reload→reload→post-reload + a bad-reload probe; Linux-CI-authoritative per ADR-0049); D8 in-process backstop (the deterministic local complement via `tokio::time` — covers the negative paths + in-flight isolation) + BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT extensions. Minimum-viable hot-reload adds ZERO new config schema (Envoy's file xDS is always-watching; envoy-rust watches every `rds`-configured HCM) UNLESS §6.2 reveals Envoy needs `watched_directory` for the chosen file-change operation.
- **Rationale:** xDS hot-reload is the highest-ROI clean next phase: it has been the named prime follow-up since phase 18, it reuses the entire phase-20 RDS infrastructure + the established periodic-task primitive, and RDS is the LEAST invasive live mutation (a stateless route-table pointer swap) — making it the architecturally-correct FIRST hot-reload phase, establishing the watcher + atomic-swap pattern that CDS/LDS/EDS hot-reload reuse. The HTTP-filters family genuinely offers no light/deterministic member after buffer (every remaining filter is external-service / engine / non-deterministic / byte-fragile), and the LB opener carries a larger harness cost; pivoting to xDS hot-reload keeps the project on its deterministic-byte-exact-differential doctrine. Recording the pivot + scope here (vs only in the SPEC) honors D-3.5: a future session must understand WHY phase 26 leaves the HTTP-filters family (its light vein is exhausted), WHY RDS is the first hot-reload target (the least invasive live mutation), and WHY the harder hot-reloads / the LB opener / the gRPC transport were deferred, without re-deriving the analysis. This mirrors the xDS-family brainstorm-ADR cadence (ADR-0048/0050/0051/0053).
- **Consequences:**
  - **The phase-26 SPEC (`docs/envoy-rust/phases/26-xds-rds-hot-reload/SPEC.md`) lands at THIS commit** with the §0 findings, the D1–D8 deliverables, the §4 deferral ledger, the §5 invariants (incl. §5.2 the 0028-idle-watcher regression witness, §5.5 the reload warm-reject carve-out, §5.7 the Linux-CI-authoritative evidence), the §6.1 split projection (single-phase, NOT projected to fire), and the §6.2 PLAN-write empirical-verification checklist (which MUST run on Linux — the reload trigger is macOS-unobservable).
  - **ROADMAP gains a new row `26`** (`status: planned`) beneath the "xDS / dynamic config family" §9 heading (the family's fifth concrete row after 18/19/20/21). No existing row flips (invariant 4.1.2); row `26` becomes `in-progress` only when the next session's state-2 PLAN-write points STATE at it (invariant 4.1.3).
  - **STATE advances** to active phase `26` (`26-xds-rds-hot-reload`), lifecycle state-1-complete / state-2-next, next expected skill `superpowers:writing-plans`; the superseded phase-26-placeholder top-section blocks relocate to `STATE_HISTORY.md` (ADR-0035), and a `### Phase-26 state-1 brainstorm` Notes subsection records the pivot + rejected alternatives.
  - **ADR-0066 is reserved** for the state-2 PLAN-write §6.2 reconciliation (lands inline if §6.2 forces the `watched_directory` schema field, or the reload-counter values / bad-reload disposition / config_dump-version shape diverge materially). **ADR-0067 is reserved** for the §6.1 split (projected NOT to fire).
  - **ADR-0014 REMAINS IN FORCE** (the YAML-native shim; RDS hot-reload does not engage the xDS gRPC/protos transport); **ADR-0028 REMAINS OPEN** (phase 26 does not engage it). **ADR-0049 governs** (its all-fatal posture for STARTUP carries; §5.5 carves out reload as warm-reject per Envoy parity; its Linux-CI-authoritative Provenance rule applies to fixture 0034 per §5.7).
  - **`DECISIONS.md` ledger head: ADR-0065** (this ADR). Next available **ADR-0066** (reserved for the §6.2 reconciliation). Project-cumulative ADR count 66. The phase-26 state-1 brainstorm commit title carries `[ADR-0065]`.
- **Provenance:** the recon facts were established by a read-only reconnaissance at the phase-26 brainstorm HEAD `28e03a831`: the swappable route table (`crates/envoy-http1/src/hcm.rs:122` `route_config: Arc<RouteConfiguration>`, constructed at `:209` via `clone_route_config`, read at `:1177`); the periodic-background-task primitive (`crates/envoy-health/src/scheduler.rs` `Scheduler::spawn` + `CancellationToken`; `envoy-bin` spawns at `crates/envoy-bin/src/main.rs:91,180-194`); the phase-20 RDS load path + `rds.*` stats + `RoutesConfigDump` (the four xDS parser modules `crates/envoy-config/src/{cds,lds,rds,eds}.rs`; `load_dynamic_resources`); the no-filesystem-watch-dep baseline (no `notify`/inotify in any `Cargo.toml`); the 33-fixture baseline (`tests/fixtures/0001`…`0033`, next is `0034`; the existing RDS fixture `0028-xds-file-based-rds` is the idle-watcher regression witness). The §6.2 EMPIRICAL verification against `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` is DEFERRED to the state-2 PLAN-write per the verify-at-PLAN-write discipline — and MUST run on Linux (the reload trigger is unobservable on macOS Docker); this brainstorm ADR locks only the pivot + scope, which are decisions, not empirically-discoverable wire shapes. Per D-3.5 this ADR lands at the state-1 brainstorm commit alongside the SPEC it scopes.

## ADR-0066: Phase-26 §6.2 empirical-verification reconciliation (run on LINUX as state-3 Task 1) — Envoy's default file-watch reloads on ATOMIC-RENAME ONLY (in-place truncate-rewrite is NEVER detected; `watched_directory` does NOT change that, so NO schema field is added and Task 9 does NOT fire); the reload-counter values match the projection (`update_attempt/success/config_reload` tick +1 per successful reload); the bad-reload disposition is {malformed/IO→`update_failure`+keep, wrong `route_config_name`→`update_rejected`+keep} matching the projection, BUT {unknown-cluster route→Envoy ACCEPTS it (`update_success`+applies+serves 503/`no_cluster`), NOT rejected} — a material divergence that envoy-rust does NOT mirror (it re-validates + warm-REJECTS unknown-cluster reloads, a recorded deliberate divergence, because the request path `.expect()`s cluster existence and matching Envoy would require a new request-time missing-cluster→503 synth path out of minimum-viable scope); `RoutesConfigDump` carries NO `version_info` for file-RDS (already the phase-20 shape) and `last_updated` + the embedded `route_config` reflect the reload; the §6.1 split does NOT fire (single phase confirmed)

- **Date:** 2026-06-16.
- **Status:** accepted.
- **Context:** Phase `26` (`26-xds-rds-hot-reload`) was scoped by ADR-0065 with its §6.2 empirical verification **deferred to state-3 Task 1** and required to run on **Linux** — the RDS hot-reload trigger (a file change observed inside the Envoy container) is unobservable on macOS Docker Desktop virtiofs (SPEC §0 finding 4 / §5.7 / ADR-0049 Provenance). The state-2 PLAN-write was authored on macOS in "macOS-deferred mode": all §6.2-dependent shapes were left as `[§6.2-PENDING]` projections and **ADR-0066 was reserved-but-unfired**, to fire inline at Task 1 iff §6.2 diverged materially. The §6.2-INDEPENDENT foundation (Task 2 the route-table-handle migration; Task 3 the `RdsWatcher` skeleton) landed first. This ADR records the Task-1 empirical run and the reconciliation decisions it forces. **ADR-0066 FIRES** (P2, P5(iii), and P6 diverge materially from the projections).
- **§6.2 empirical method (Provenance):** a read-only probe rig was stood up on a Linux host against `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` (digest `sha256:56da5afd7df364350ff92de4fb49a9b09957c17295f2899f0a31cd12c28770c2`), an `rds`-configured H1 HCM (`stat_prefix: ingress_http`, `route_config_name: local_route`, `path_config_source.path`) + two STATIC clusters `backend_a`/`backend_b` (distinguished by `cluster.<name>.upstream_rq_total`) + admin `/stats` + `/config_dump`. **Host caveat (REINFORCES §5.7 / ADR-0049):** the Linux host runs Docker Desktop (a VM); host **bind-mounts do NOT deliver inotify into the container** (virtiofs — the same limitation as macOS). The probe achieved real reloads only by placing the RDS file in a Docker **volume** and editing it **inside the container via `docker exec`** (writes on the container's real ext4). Consequence carried to Task 8: fixture `0034`'s differential reload remains **Linux-CI-authoritative on a NATIVE-Linux runner** (real bind-mount inotify) — it is NOT locally observable under Docker Desktop. The full probe transcript is preserved in `PROGRESS.md` Task 1.
- **Findings (the SPEC §6.2 7-item checklist, P1–P7):**
  - **P1 (reload happens + readiness) — MATCHES.** Editing the RDS file under a running Envoy re-routes live traffic WITHOUT a restart; settle latency **~50 ms** (observed range 6–60 ms); the listener stays up (zero connection drops / no port close across all reloads, verified under 60 concurrent probes). Informs the Task-7 harness wait bound (a bounded wait-for-convergence, not a fixed sleep).
  - **P2 (file-change operation — THE load-bearing item) — DIVERGES.** Under Envoy's DEFAULT file-watch (no `watched_directory`): **in-place truncate-rewrite is NEVER detected** (confirmed 3× via `cat >`, `python open('w')`, truncate-append — `update_attempt`/`update_success` never moved); **atomic-rename (write-temp-then-`mv`-into-path) reliably reloads every time** (3/3, detected in ~6–60 ms). Adding `watched_directory` (which lives under `path_config_source`, NOT directly under `config_source` — the latter fails boot) does **NOT** rescue the in-place case (still 0/3). The projection (in-place rewrite triggers the default watch) is **WRONG**. **`watched_directory` is therefore NOT required** for the atomic-rename trigger — it only matters when the watched target is a symlinked directory (k8s ConfigMap swaps). **Consequence: Task 9 (the `ConfigSource.watched_directory` schema field + fuzz seed) does NOT fire — NO config-schema change this phase; the Task-7 harness must rewrite the fixture file via ATOMIC-RENAME** so BOTH proxies reload deterministically. envoy-rust's own watcher is poll-based on `std::fs::metadata().modified()` (mtime), which detects an atomic-rename (the moved-in inode carries a fresh mtime) — so the landed Task-3 skeleton needs NO change for P2.
  - **P3 (distinguishable backends) — MATCHES.** Two single-endpoint clusters are cleanly discriminated by `cluster.backend_a.upstream_rq_total` vs `cluster.backend_b.upstream_rq_total`; a single STATIC endpoint per cluster suffices (both may even point at the same backend — only the route target, hence the per-cluster counter, differs).
  - **P4 (reload counter values) — MATCHES.** `http.ingress_http.rds.local_route.{update_attempt, update_success, update_failure, update_rejected, config_reload}` = **`1/1/0/0/1`** (boot) → **`2/2/0/0/2`** (after reload #1) → **`3/3/0/0/3`** (after reload #2). `update_attempt`, `update_success`, and `config_reload` each tick **exactly +1 per successful reload**; `update_failure`/`update_rejected` stay 0 on success. (Other Envoy-only `rds.local_route.*` names observed — `version` [a 64-bit content hash], `version_text: ""`, `update_time`, `config_reload_time_ms`, `update_duration`, `update_empty: 0`, `init_fetch_timeout: 0` — remain unasserted per the phase-20 Envoy-only enumeration.)
  - **P5 (bad-reload disposition) — PARTIALLY DIVERGES.** With Envoy serving the last-good table, applied via atomic-rename: (i) **malformed YAML / garbage bytes → `update_failure` +1, last-good KEPT** (routes unchanged, no dropped traffic) — MATCHES; (ii) **wrong/renamed `route_config_name` (the named RouteConfiguration absent from the envelope) → `update_rejected` +1, last-good KEPT** — MATCHES; (iii) **route referencing an UNKNOWN cluster → `update_success` +1 + `config_reload` +1 (Envoy ACCEPTS the update and APPLIES the broken table); the route then serves `503` with `http.ingress_http.no_cluster` incrementing; last-good is NOT kept** — **DIVERGES** from the projection (which expected `update_rejected` + last-good kept). Envoy validates the RouteConfiguration in isolation and does **not** cross-check cluster existence on a filesystem-RDS update (no CDS/RDS consistency check without ADS).
  - **P6 (config_dump on reload) — MINOR DIVERGENCE.** The `dynamic_route_configs[]` entry carries keys `[@type, route_config, last_updated]` only. **`version_info` is ABSENT** (not "changes" — it is simply never populated for file-based RDS), which is **already the phase-20 envoy-rust `RoutesConfigDump` shape** (`crates/envoy-admin/src/endpoint.rs` — "NO `version_info` key"). `last_updated` **changes** (RFC3339 ms `…Z` timestamp); the embedded `route_config` **reflects the NEW route table** (backend_a → backend_b). Fixtures 0026/0027 `configs[]` indices are unaffected.
  - **P7 (in-flight isolation) — MATCHES (resolved).** A request that began under the old table (against a 5 s-delaying backend) completed under the OLD route table (served by the old cluster, full 5 s, 200) when a reload landed mid-flight; the swap retargets only NEW requests. Confirms the §5.4 read-once-per-request invariant.
- **Decision:**
  1. **NO config-schema change; Task 9 does NOT fire.** envoy-rust's poll-based mtime watcher already detects the atomic-rename trigger; `watched_directory` is not added. Record "Task 9 N/A — atomic-rename triggers the reload; `watched_directory` not required" in PROGRESS.
  2. **The Task-7 harness rewrites the mounted RDS file via ATOMIC-RENAME** (render new contents to a temp file on the same mount, then `rename`/`mv` over the path) — the ONLY operation that triggers BOTH proxies. In-place truncate-rewrite is forbidden for the harness reload step (Envoy would miss it). Fixture `0034`'s differential reload evidence is **Linux-CI-authoritative on a native-Linux runner** (NOT locally observable under Docker Desktop virtiofs — §5.7).
  3. **The phase-26 reload bad-reload taxonomy (Task 4 / D3 / §5.5 warm-reject):** {file unreadable / IO error / malformed YAML / parse error → tick `update_attempt`+`update_failure`, KEEP last-good}; {`route_config_name` not present in the reloaded envelope → tick `update_attempt`+`update_rejected`, KEEP last-good}; {a reloaded route references an unknown cluster → tick `update_attempt`+`update_rejected`, KEEP last-good — a **DELIBERATE RECORDED DIVERGENCE** from Envoy (which accepts + applies + serves 503/`no_cluster`)}. envoy-rust **re-validates route→cluster references against the immutable live cluster set on every reload and warm-rejects an unresolved reference**, because the H1/H2 request path resolves the route's cluster via `config.cluster_mgr.get(&cluster_name).expect("validator ensures cluster present")` (`crates/envoy-http1/src/hcm.rs:818`) — installing an unknown-cluster route would PANIC the proxy (catastrophically worse than Envoy's 503). Matching Envoy's accept-and-503 would require adding a request-time missing-cluster→503 synth path on BOTH codecs, which is out of phase-26 minimum-viable scope; the divergence is unobservable in fixture `0034` (which exercises only the malformed → `update_failure` bad-reload, where both proxies agree) and surfaces only in the envoy-rust-only in-process backstop. Justified by D-3.3 (the differential contract — fixture `0034` — does not assert the unknown-cluster reload case, so the safer non-panicking divergence is permitted and recorded).
  4. **Task 6 (`RoutesConfigDump` on reload) shrinks:** `version_info` is already absent (phase-20 shape — no change); `last_updated` is already render-time `now()` (already changes); the only Task-6 work is to render `route_config` **through the swappable handle** (`current_route_config()`) so a post-reload `/config_dump` reflects the new table.
  5. **The §6.1 split does NOT fire — single phase confirmed (ADR-0067 stays UNFIRED).** Task 9 is dropped (no schema change), Task 4's unknown-cluster handling is the SPEC's already-planned re-validate-and-reject (no extra request-time code), and Task 6 shrinks — so the refined surface is at or under the ADR-0065 / SPEC §6.1 projection (~1200–1600 LoC / ~10–13 tasks), below the ~1500-LoC / ~25-task gate.
- **Rationale:** P2 is the most consequential finding and it inverts the projection: Envoy's default file-watch is rename/move-triggered, not content-triggered, so the harness MUST atomic-rename — but because envoy-rust polls mtime (which catches both rename and in-place), no envoy-rust behavior change and no `watched_directory` schema field are needed, keeping the phase dep-free and schema-stable as ADR-0065 intended. P5(iii) is the substantive design divergence: Envoy's RDS does not validate cluster references, but envoy-rust's request path assumes the load-time cluster-existence invariant, so envoy-rust must keep re-validating and warm-rejecting on reload — preserving safety (never panics, never installs a broken table) at the cost of a recorded divergence that the differential contract does not exercise. P6 turned out already-correct in envoy-rust's phase-20 code. Recording all three here (vs only in the PLAN) honors D-3.5: a future session must understand WHY the harness atomic-renames, WHY there is no `watched_directory` field, and WHY envoy-rust rejects (rather than Envoy-faithfully accepts) an unknown-cluster reload, without re-running the §6.2 probe.
- **Consequences:**
  - **`PLAN.md` is updated at the Task-1 commit:** every `[§6.2-PENDING]` projection (P1–P7) is replaced with the verified facts above; the STATUS-DEFERRED banner is resolved; Task 4 carries the P5 taxonomy + the unknown-cluster recorded divergence; Task 6 is narrowed (read-through-handle only); Task 7 carries the atomic-rename operation; Task 9 is marked N/A (does-not-fire); the §6.1 re-evaluation confirms single-phase.
  - **`BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md` gains:** (a) a "RDS reload semantics" extension to the phase-20 `http.<prefix>.rds.<name>.*` Stat-name-mapping rows (the counters advance per reload — `2/2/0/0/2` after one successful reload — vs the phase-20 initial-load-only `1/1/0/0/1`); and (b) a **hot-reload subsection** under "xDS wire state machine → Filesystem transport (`path_config_source`)" recording the atomic-rename trigger (+ envoy-rust's mtime-poll mechanism divergence), the warm-reject taxonomy (incl. the unknown-cluster recorded divergence), the `RoutesConfigDump` `last_updated`/route-reflects-new shape (no `version_info`), and the in-flight read-once isolation guarantee.
  - **DECISIONS.md ledger head: ADR-0066** (this ADR). Project-cumulative ADR count 67. **ADR-0067 (the §6.1 split) is reserved-but-UNFIRED** (single phase confirmed). The Task-1 docs commit title carries `[ADR-0066]`.
  - **ADR-0014 REMAINS IN FORCE** (no protos/gRPC transport engaged). **ADR-0028 REMAINS OPEN.** **ADR-0049 governs** (its all-fatal STARTUP posture carries; phase 26's RELOAD is the §5.5 warm-reject carve-out, whose exact taxonomy this ADR locks; its Linux-CI-authoritative Provenance rule applies to fixture `0034` per §5.7, reinforced by the Docker-Desktop-virtiofs caveat above).
  - **ADR-0065 is NOT superseded** — this ADR resolves the §6.2 reconciliation ADR-0065 reserved as ADR-0066, within the scope ADR-0065 set.
