## ADR-0067: Phase-27 scoping — CONTINUE the xDS / dynamic-config family with the first of the ADR-0065-deferred CDS/LDS/EDS hot-reload layers: file-based EDS endpoint hot-reload (`eds_cluster_config.eds_config.path_config_source.path` re-read on atomic-rename + atomic endpoint-set swap + per-reload `cluster.<name>.update_*` advancement + `EndpointsConfigDump` update + fixture `0035`), chosen as the LEAST invasive of the three (an endpoint address-`Vec` swap within an already-existing cluster; the round-robin LB is per-request stateless; the cluster lifecycle stays immutable); reuses phase-26's watcher + atomic-swap + mid-test-atomic-rename harness primitives wholesale; minimum-viable scope = PLAIN clusters only (no active HC / no outlier detection — the endpoint-index-aligned health/outlier array rebuild defers); defer CDS/LDS hot-reload, the EDS+HC/OD aligned-array rebuild, LB-policy/weight/locality/priority reload, SDS/RTDS, the gRPC/ADS transport, delta xDS, and the ADR-0014 protos supersession

- **Date:** 2026-06-18.
- **Status:** accepted.
- **Context:** Phase `26` (`26-xds-rds-hot-reload`, file-based RDS hot-reload) closed at its state-6 deterministic close-out (HEAD `b01e7eb`), advancing STATE to a phase-`27` placeholder at state-1-next. The phase-27 state-1 brainstorm (`superpowers:brainstorming`) had to pick + scope phase 27 from the `ROADMAP.md` §9 feature-family candidate lists, since the sequential rows END at `26` (no pre-numbered row `27`). Unlike the phase-26 pick (a genuine cross-family fork — ADR-0065), phase 27's pick is a **continuation**: ADR-0065 explicitly named **CDS/LDS/EDS hot-reload the cleanly-deferred next layers that "build on THIS phase's [phase 26's] watcher primitive + atomic-swap pattern,"** and STATE recorded the xDS / dynamic-config family as "the natural continuation now that phase 26 built the watcher + atomic-swap primitive." The fork that REMAINS is *which* of CDS/LDS/EDS goes first, weighed against the still-deferred LB-family opener / network-filters opener / the protos-blocked gRPC transport.
- **Options considered:**
  - **EDS hot-reload — file-based endpoint assignments (CHOSEN).** Among the three ADR-0065-deferred hot-reload layers, EDS is the LEAST invasive: an EDS reload mutates ONLY a cluster's endpoint (host) `Vec<SocketAddr>` (`crates/envoy-cluster/src/cluster.rs:80`, built once at `from_bootstrap` `:741-803`, read every request by the round-robin LB `pick()` `:274` via an `AtomicUsize` cursor — per-request stateless, the closest analog to phase-26's stateless route-table swap). The cluster lifecycle (pools keyed by `(cluster,endpoint)`, health checkers, outlier sweepers, budgets, listeners) stays immutable. It REUSES phase-26's entire infrastructure — the periodic poll-watch primitive (`crates/envoy-http1/src/rds_watcher.rs`), the atomic-swap-handle pattern, the warm-reject reload pipeline, and the **mid-test atomic-rename file-rewrite + settle-then-probe harness capability** — so it needs no new crate, no new dependency (poll-based mtime watch + a dep-free `RwLock<Arc<…>>`/`tokio::sync::watch` swap handle), and no new reload/settle harness machinery, only the endpoint-handle migration + the EDS reparse/validate/swap pipeline + ONE genuinely-new harness capability (a second distinguishable backend — see Decision). Two costs: (i) the differential observability is harder than RDS — an endpoint swap WITHIN one cluster is invisible through a single echo backend (`cluster.<name>.membership_total` is not emitted `cluster.rs:963`, `membership_healthy` is HC-gated, no per-endpoint request counters), so the fixture needs two distinguishable single-endpoint backends (the minimal seed of the deferred LB distinguishable-backend harness); (ii) the reload trigger is unobservable under virtiofs → Linux-CI-authoritative (ADR-0049 / ADR-0066 Provenance).
  - **CDS hot-reload FIRST (REJECTED — heavier live mutation).** A CDS cluster add/remove/update spawns/tears-down the per-cluster connection pools (`H1PoolManager`/`H2PoolManager`), active health checkers (`envoy-health::Scheduler`), outlier ejection sweepers, and budget primitives, and needs a swappable `ClusterManager` handle (vs phase-26's per-HCM route handle / phase-27's per-cluster endpoint handle). A heavier live mutation that layers onto EDS's + RDS's atomic-swap primitive in a later increment.
  - **LDS hot-reload FIRST (REJECTED — heaviest live mutation).** A listener add/remove/update binds/unbinds sockets, churns the accept-loop task, and drains in-flight connections. The heaviest of the three; deferred furthest.
  - **The LB-family opener (REJECTED — still deferred, but phase 27 lays its seed).** Deterministic hash LB (`ring_hash`/`maglev`) / `least_request` / locality-weighted LB needs a GENERAL distinguishable-backend harness (N backends, weights, locality, hash-distribution observability) — deferred at the phase-25/26 brainstorms (ADR-0062/0065) as "larger/riskier." Phase 27 builds only the MINIMAL version (a two-single-endpoint-backend pair to observe an `A→B` endpoint swap), which becomes that harness's seed — exactly as ADR-0065 framed RDS needing "a two-distinguishable-cluster pair, not a general framework."
  - **The gRPC/ADS xDS transport (REJECTED — protos-blocked).** Requires tonic + envoy-protos/prost + the ADS state machine + the ADR-0014 protos supersession — re-verified blocked (the gRPC family is also H2-trailers-blocked). A multi-phase sub-project, not a single increment.
  - **The Network-filters opener (REJECTED — low leverage).** `echo`/`direct_response`/`sni_cluster` are light and deterministic but niche (the ADR-0062 / ADR-0064 / ADR-0065 low-leverage rejection stands).
- **Decision:** Land **file-based EDS endpoint hot-reload** as phase `27` (`27-xds-eds-hot-reload`), minimum-viable. Deliverables D1–D8 (SPEC §3): D1 migrate `Cluster.endpoints` from an owned `Vec<SocketAddr>` to a shared atomically-swappable handle (dep-free `RwLock<Arc<…>>`/`tokio::sync::watch`; the LB `pick()` reads through it; cursor-bounds-safe on a shrinking set); D2 the EDS file watcher — GENERALIZE the phase-26 `RdsWatcher` (or a sibling `EdsWatcher`; likely relocated to a shared crate since EDS concerns `envoy-cluster`, not the HCM in `envoy-http1` — a PLAN-write call weighing the §6.11 watcher-generalization pressure); D3 the reload pipeline (re-parse via the existing `eds.rs` → re-validate the assignment against the phase-21 gate → atomic swap; tick the phase-21 `cluster.<name>.update_*` counters per reload; warm-reject keeping the last-good set on a bad reload — reusing the phase-26 §5.5 carve-out); D4 the per-reload counter increments; D5 the `EndpointsConfigDump` `last_updated`/assignment update read through the swappable handle; D6 the one new harness capability (a second distinguishable single-endpoint backend so the endpoint re-targeting is observable on the wire — the mid-test atomic-rename rewrite + settle is REUSED from phase-26 D6); D7 fixture `0035-xds-eds-hot-reload` (two distinguishable real `http1-echo-server` backends; one `type: EDS` cluster `eds_backend` with NO HC / NO OD; three-phase pre-reload→reload→post-reload + a bad-reload probe; native-Linux-CI-authoritative per ADR-0049/0066); D8 in-process backstop (the deterministic local complement via `tokio::time` — covers the negative paths + in-flight isolation + cursor-bounds) + BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT extensions. **Minimum-viable scope = PLAIN clusters only (no active HC / no outlier detection):** the endpoint-index-aligned `endpoint_health`/`outlier_detection` arrays + the per-`(cluster,endpoint)` health-probe tasks would need spawn/drain/rebuild on a count-changing reload — the same per-endpoint lifecycle churn that defers CDS — so the EDS+HC/OD aligned-array rebuild defers (the §6.2/PLAN-write disposition of an EDS+HC/OD cluster — reject-loud vs no-watcher — is recorded; ADR-0068 reserved if it diverges). Minimum-viable EDS hot-reload adds ZERO new config schema (Envoy's file xDS is always-watching; envoy-rust watches every `eds`-configured cluster; ADR-0066 P2's atomic-rename-triggers-without-`watched_directory` finding carries).
- **Rationale:** EDS hot-reload is the highest-ROI clean next phase: it is the explicit ADR-0065-named continuation of the xDS hot-reload arc, it reuses phase-26's entire infrastructure (watcher + atomic-swap + warm-reject + mid-test-atomic-rename harness) + the phase-21 EDS load path (parser + validator + `cluster.<name>.update_*` stats + `EndpointsConfigDump`), and EDS is the LEAST invasive of the three deferred live mutations (a stateless endpoint-`Vec` pointer swap) — making it the architecturally-correct SECOND hot-reload phase, establishing the cluster-endpoint-swap pattern before CDS's heavier cluster-lifecycle mutation. The MVP plain-clusters-only boundary keeps it a pure data swap (the HC/OD aligned-array rebuild is genuinely the CDS-class hard part and is honestly deferred, NOT silently under-implemented — an EDS+HC/OD cluster's disposition is resolved at §6.2). Recording the continuation + scope here (vs only in the SPEC) honors D-3.5: a future session must understand WHY EDS is the first of the three deferred hot-reloads (the least invasive), WHY the MVP excludes HC/OD clusters (the aligned-array rebuild is CDS-class lifecycle churn), and WHY a second distinguishable backend is needed (an intra-cluster endpoint swap is invisible through one backend), without re-deriving the analysis. This mirrors the xDS-family brainstorm-ADR cadence (ADR-0048/0050/0051/0053/0065).
- **Consequences:**
  - **The phase-27 SPEC (`docs/envoy-rust/phases/27-xds-eds-hot-reload/SPEC.md`) lands at THIS commit** with the §0 findings, the D1–D8 deliverables, the §4 deferral ledger, the §5 invariants (incl. §5.2 the 0029-idle-watcher regression witness, §5.3 the plain-cluster-only boundary, §5.5 the reused warm-reject carve-out, §5.7 the Linux-CI-authoritative evidence), the §6.1 split projection (single-phase, NOT projected to fire; ~900–1300 LoC, below phase 26), and the §6.2 PLAN-write empirical-verification checklist (which MUST run on native Linux — the reload trigger is virtiofs-unobservable).
  - **ROADMAP gains a new row `27`** (`status: planned`) beneath the "xDS / dynamic config family" §9 heading (the family's sixth concrete row after 18/19/20/21/26). No existing row flips (invariant 4.1.2); row `27` becomes `in-progress` only when the next session's state-2 PLAN-write points STATE at it (invariant 4.1.3).
  - **STATE advances** to active phase `27` (`27-xds-eds-hot-reload`), lifecycle state-1-complete / state-2-next, next expected skill `superpowers:writing-plans`; the superseded phase-27-placeholder top-section blocks relocate to `STATE_HISTORY.md` (ADR-0035), and a `### Phase-27 state-1 brainstorm` Notes subsection records the continuation + rejected alternatives.
  - **ADR-0068 is reserved** for the state-2 PLAN-write §6.2 reconciliation (lands inline if §6.2 changes the harness observability shape, or the reload-counter/membership values / the empty-assignment bad-reload disposition + its Envoy-applies-vs-rejects divergence / config_dump shape / the EDS+HC/OD disposition diverge materially). **ADR-0069 is reserved** for the §6.1 split (projected NOT to fire).
  - **ADR-0014 REMAINS IN FORCE** (the YAML-native shim; EDS hot-reload does not engage the xDS gRPC/protos transport); **ADR-0028 REMAINS OPEN** (phase 27 does not engage it). **ADR-0049 governs** (its all-fatal posture for STARTUP carries; §5.5 reuses the phase-26 reload-as-warm-reject carve-out; its Linux-CI-authoritative Provenance rule, reinforced by ADR-0066's Docker-Desktop-virtiofs caveat, applies to fixture 0035 per §5.7). **ADR-0066 governs** the reused atomic-rename trigger + mtime-poll mechanism.
  - **`DECISIONS.md` ledger head: ADR-0067** (this ADR). Next available **ADR-0068** (reserved for the §6.2 reconciliation). Project-cumulative ADR count 68. The phase-27 state-1 brainstorm commit title carries `[ADR-0067]`.
- **Provenance:** the recon facts were established by a read-only reconnaissance at the phase-27 brainstorm HEAD `b01e7eb`: the cluster endpoint model (`crates/envoy-cluster/src/cluster.rs:80` `endpoints: Vec<SocketAddr>`, constructed at `:741-803`, read by the round-robin LB `pick()` at `:274`); the endpoint-index-aligned `endpoint_health: Option<Vec<Arc<EndpointHealth>>>` / `outlier_detection: Option<OutlierDetectionState>` (the §0-finding-3 HC/OD-lifecycle boundary); the EDS load path + the `cluster.<name>.update_attempt/update_success/update_empty` registration (`cluster.rs:974-977`, `update_failure`/`update_rejected` at `:1097`) + the `membership_total`-not-emitted note (`cluster.rs:963`); the `EndpointsConfigDump` renderer (`crates/envoy-admin/src/endpoint.rs`); the reusable phase-26 primitives (`crates/envoy-http1/src/rds_watcher.rs` watcher; the `tests/differential/src/lib.rs` mid-test atomic-rename rewrite + wait-for-convergence); the 34-fixture baseline (`tests/fixtures/0001`…`0034`, next is `0035`; the existing EDS fixture `0029-xds-file-based-eds` is the idle-watcher regression witness). The §6.2 EMPIRICAL verification against `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` is DEFERRED to the state-2 PLAN-write per the verify-at-PLAN-write discipline — and MUST run on native Linux (the reload trigger is virtiofs-unobservable); this brainstorm ADR locks only the continuation + scope, which are decisions, not empirically-discoverable wire shapes. Per D-3.5 this ADR lands at the state-1 brainstorm commit alongside the SPEC it scopes.

## ADR-0068: Phase-27 §6.2 empirical-verification reconciliation (run on this host at the state-2 PLAN-write, via the ADR-0066 Docker-Desktop methodology — container-internal EDS file edited by `docker exec` atomic-rename) — the reload happens (~8 ms settle, zero 503 gap), the `cluster.<name>.update_*` values match (`1/1→2/2→3/3`), the second-distinguishable-backend observable is confirmed over the liveness-flip alternative, AND the `EndpointsConfigDump` reflects the new assignment — BUT the empty-assignment disposition DIVERGES from the SPEC's warm-reject projection: Envoy APPLIES an empty endpoint list (CLA present, `endpoints: []` → 0 hosts → `update_success` → 503 "no healthy upstream"), and envoy-rust faithfully MIRRORS this (NOT a recorded divergence — turns a projected divergence into a MATCH — because `pick()` already returns `None` on an empty set with no panic [unlike phase-26's `.expect()` cluster lookup] and the `synth_no_healthy_upstream` 503 path already exists), while a truly-empty envelope (`resources: []`, no CLA) is the no-op `update_empty` path; the `EndpointsConfigDump` carries NO `last_updated` and NO `version_info` (the SPEC's "`last_updated` changes" projection is WRONG — there is no such field; already the phase-21 shape) → D5 shrinks to read-through-handle only; `membership_*` stays Envoy-only; the EDS+HC/OD cluster gets NO watcher (endpoints frozen at initial load, a recorded deferred non-goal); the §6.1 split does NOT fire (single phase confirmed; ADR-0069 stays UNFIRED)

- **Date:** 2026-06-18.
- **Status:** accepted.
- **Context:** Phase `27` (`27-xds-eds-hot-reload`, file-based EDS endpoint hot-reload) was scoped by ADR-0067, which **reserved ADR-0068** for the state-2 PLAN-write §6.2 empirical-verification reconciliation. Unlike phase 26 (whose §6.2 was deferred to state-3 Task 1 because the PLAN-write ran on macOS), phase 27's §6.2 verification was run **at the state-2 PLAN-write** (this commit) against `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` (digest `sha256:56da5afd7df364350ff92de4fb49a9b09957c17295f2899f0a31cd12c28770c2`). The verifier ran on this dev host, which is **Docker Desktop 4.41.2** (a linuxkit VM — host bind-mounts deliver no inotify, per the `host-docker-desktop-virtiofs-no-inotify` finding + ADR-0066). Real reloads were obtained via the **ADR-0066 methodology**: the EDS file lives on the Envoy container's OWN overlayfs (written by an entrypoint shell script, NO host bind-mount) and is reloaded by `docker exec` write-temp-then-`mv` (atomic-rename) inside the container, where inotify works. Two distinguishable single-endpoint `hashicorp/http-echo` backends (`BACKEND_ONE`/`BACKEND_TWO`) on a user-defined docker network reachable by numeric IP. **ADR-0068 FIRES** (the empty-assignment disposition + the config_dump `last_updated` projection diverge from the SPEC; the reconciliation also LOCKS the bad-reload taxonomy + the observability shape the downstream tasks consume). The full probe transcript is preserved in `PROGRESS.md` (the state-2 §6.2 entry).
- **§6.2 empirical method (Provenance):** docker network `eds-probe-net`; `backend1`/`backend2` = `hashicorp/http-echo -text=BACKEND_ONE|BACKEND_TWO` (port 5678, single endpoint each), discovered by numeric IP; `envoy-probe` = `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` on the same network, `--entrypoint /bin/sh` writing `/tmp/bootstrap.yaml` + the initial `/tmp/eds/eds.yaml` (CLA `eds_backend` → backend1 IP) then `exec envoy`; admin `:9901`, H1 listener `:10000` (`stat_prefix: ingress_http`, route `/`→`eds_backend`, `type: EDS` cluster with `eds_cluster_config.eds_config.path_config_source.path: /tmp/eds/eds.yaml`, router-only chain, NO HC / NO OD). Reloads via `docker exec ... 'cat > /tmp/eds/eds.new <<EDS … EDS; mv /tmp/eds/eds.new /tmp/eds/eds.yaml'`. Host left clean (all containers + network removed).
- **Findings (the SPEC §6.2 6-item checklist):**
  - **Item 1 (reload happens + readiness) — MATCHES.** Atomic-rename `[backend1]→[backend2]` re-targets live traffic with **no restart**; the `/probe` body flips `BACKEND_ONE`→`BACKEND_TWO` on the first 50 ms poll; measured `mv`→effective **settle ~7–8 ms** (a later recovery flip ~6.7 ms). **Zero 503 gap** — a 400-request hammer loop across a live swap saw zero non-200s; the cluster stays up (no membership drop, no pool teardown). → harness wait bound = poll on a 50 ms grid with a ~2 s ceiling (generous margin; the phase-26 pattern).
  - **Item 2 (observability shape — D6 is built to it) — second backend CONFIRMED over liveness-flip.** Body markers `BACKEND_ONE`/`BACKEND_TWO` cleanly distinguish the backends on the wire; the swap re-targets observably. The **liveness-flip** alternative (point `eds_backend` at an unreachable `127.0.0.1:1` → `/probe` 503 in ~55 ms) IS observable but NOISIER: the 503 is a request-time connection-refused (membership stays `1/1`, the `update_*` counters tick normally — it does NOT exercise membership/update the way an empty-assignment does), it does not prove the NEW endpoint serves, and its latency/reliability depend on connect-failure timing. **Decision: D6 uses the second-distinguishable-backend body-marker swap** as the primary differential observable (positive, instant, deterministic, zero-503-gap); the liveness/503 signal is reserved as the EXPECTED result of the empty-assignment case only.
  - **Item 3 (`cluster.<name>.update_*` values) — MATCHES.** `update_attempt`/`update_success` = `1/1` (boot) → `2/2` (one reload) → `3/3` (two); `update_failure`/`update_rejected`/`update_empty` = 0 across good reloads. `update_attempt`+`update_success` each tick +1 per successful reload. Fixture 0035 asserts `2/2` after its one successful reload. **Membership signal:** Envoy DOES emit `cluster.<name>.membership_total`/`membership_healthy`/`membership_change` (`membership_change` ticks on every endpoint-set change, even a same-count address swap; `membership_total` tracks host count → drops to 0 on empty-apply), but **envoy-rust does NOT emit `membership_total`** (`cluster.rs:963`) and gates `membership_healthy` on `health_checks` (absent on a plain cluster). → assert ONLY `update_*` (portable); `membership_*` stays Envoy-only/informational (the phase-21 narrowing carries).
  - **Item 4 (bad-reload disposition — locks §5.5 + D3) — ONE MATERIAL DIVERGENCE (empty-assignment), reconciled to a MATCH by mirroring.** From a clean last-good (serving a live backend), each bad reload via atomic-rename:
    - **(a) malformed YAML / garbage bytes** → Envoy `update_failure` +1, last-good KEPT (200). (`Filesystem config update failure: ... yaml-cpp: error ...`.) **envoy-rust mirrors:** file-read/parse error → `update_attempt`+`update_failure`, KEEP last-good.
    - **(b) wrong/absent `cluster_name`** (the envelope carries a CLA, but named `NOT_eds_backend`, not the target) → Envoy `update_rejected` +1, last-good KEPT (200). (`Filesystem config update rejected: Unexpected EDS cluster (expecting eds_backend): NOT_eds_backend`.) **envoy-rust mirrors:** no CLA matches the target name (envelope non-empty) → `update_attempt`+`update_rejected`, KEEP last-good.
    - **(c) unparseable endpoint address** (`address: not-an-ip`) → Envoy `update_rejected` +1, last-good KEPT. (`Filesystem config update rejected: malformed IP address: not-an-ip`.) **envoy-rust mirrors:** the phase-21 numeric-IP validator rejects → `update_attempt`+`update_rejected`, KEEP last-good.
    - **(d) EMPTY endpoint list** (CLA PRESENT for `eds_backend`, but `endpoints: []`) → **Envoy APPLIES it**: `update_success` +1, `membership_total` 1→0, subsequent `/probe` → **503 "no healthy upstream"**; last-good NOT kept. This **DIVERGES** from the SPEC §0-finding-3 / §5.5 / §6.2-item-4 projection (which expected envoy-rust to warm-REJECT an empty assignment to avoid an empty-LB panic). **RECONCILIATION — envoy-rust MIRRORS Envoy (applies the empty set → `update_success` → 503), turning the projected divergence into a MATCH**, because (unlike phase-26's unknown-cluster case which `.expect()`ed cluster existence and would PANIC) envoy-rust's `pick()` already returns `None` on an empty endpoint set with NO panic (`crates/envoy-cluster/src/cluster.rs:275` `if self.endpoints.is_empty() { return None }`) and the request path already maps that `None` to a byte-exact `synth_no_healthy_upstream` 503 (`crates/envoy-http1/src/hcm.rs:392,1489` — body `no healthy upstream`, matching Envoy's empty-cluster 503 body). D-3.3 (differential correctness beats internal fidelity) therefore PREFERS mirroring: it is safe (no panic), cheap (the 503 path exists; mirroring is actually LESS code than a warm-reject empty-check), and faithful. **The SPEC's warm-reject-empty projection is CORRECTED to apply-empty.**
    - **(e) truly-empty envelope** (`resources: []`, NO CLA for the cluster at all) → Envoy `update_empty` +1, last-good KEPT (200), `membership_total` stays 1. **envoy-rust mirrors:** parsed envelope yields zero CLAs → `update_attempt`+`update_empty`, KEEP last-good (no-op). Envoy DISTINGUISHES (e) `resources: []` → `update_empty`+no-op from (d) CLA-present-but-`endpoints: []` → `update_success`+apply-0-hosts — envoy-rust mirrors that distinction.
  - **Item 5 (`/config_dump` `EndpointsConfigDump` on reload) — MATCHES the wire shape, but the SPEC's `last_updated` projection is WRONG.** EDS appears ONLY under `?include_eds` (plain `/config_dump` omits it), classified under `static_endpoint_configs[]` (the phase-21 ADR-0054 shape). The embedded assignment **reflects the NEW endpoints** after a reload. **There is NO `last_updated` and NO `version_info`** on the `EndpointsConfigDump` entry — the SPEC §1/§2.2/D5/§6.2-item-5 projection that "`last_updated` changes on reload" is WRONG (the EndpointsConfigDump has no such field; this is ALREADY the phase-21 envoy-rust shape — `crates/envoy-admin/src/endpoint.rs` `Endpoints { static_endpoint_configs }`, no `last_updated` key). **Consequence: D5 SHRINKS to ONE thing — render the assignment THROUGH the swappable endpoint handle** (D1) so a post-reload `/config_dump?include_eds` reflects the new endpoints; NO timestamp/version plumbing (parallels ADR-0066 P6, where `RoutesConfigDump.version_info` was already absent). Post-reload subtree: `{"@type":"…EndpointsConfigDump","static_endpoint_configs":[{"endpoint_config":{"@type":"…ClusterLoadAssignment","cluster_name":"eds_backend","endpoints":[…new address…],"policy":{"overprovisioning_factor":140}}}]}`.
  - **Item 6 (in-flight isolation) — MATCHES.** A request begun pre-reload (against a 3 s-sleep backend) completed against the OLD endpoint; a request issued immediately after the reload hit the NEW endpoint. The swap re-targets only subsequent LB picks — confirms the §5.4 read-once-per-selection invariant. (Cursor-bounds on a SHRINKING set is a pure envoy-rust-side concern — `pick()`'s `i % total` over the read-once snapshot, with the empty case short-circuited — covered by the D8 backstop, not the differential.)
- **Decision:**
  1. **Observability (D6): the second-distinguishable-backend body-marker swap** is the differential observable (not the liveness-flip). D6 ships two single-endpoint backends distinguishable by a per-backend body marker; the mid-test atomic-rename + settle-then-probe is reused from phase-26 D6.
  2. **The EDS reload bad-reload taxonomy (D3 / §5.5 warm-reject) — envoy-rust MIRRORS Envoy in all five classes:** {file unreadable / IO / malformed YAML / parse error → `update_attempt`+`update_failure`, KEEP last-good}; {envelope non-empty but no CLA matches the target `cluster_name` → `update_attempt`+`update_rejected`, KEEP last-good}; {a matched CLA has an unparseable/non-numeric endpoint address → `update_attempt`+`update_rejected`, KEEP last-good}; {a matched CLA has `endpoints: []` → `update_attempt`+`update_success`, APPLY the empty set (0 hosts → `pick()` None → `synth_no_healthy_upstream` 503); last-good NOT kept — the mirror that REPLACES the SPEC's warm-reject projection}; {truly-empty envelope `resources: []` (zero CLAs) → `update_attempt`+`update_empty`, KEEP last-good (no-op)}. The reparse/revalidate runs OUTSIDE the write lock; a single `store_endpoints` applies on success (the phase-26 carve-out discipline). This is the §5.5 warm-reject carve-out for the IO/parse/reject/empty-envelope classes (ADR-0049's all-fatal posture governs STARTUP, where `from_bootstrap` STILL rejects an empty cluster — `cluster.rs:804`; the reload path deliberately applies-empty to mirror Envoy, the recorded reload-vs-startup asymmetry).
  3. **D4 must REGISTER `update_rejected` for `eds`-configured clusters** — the phase-21 registration (`cluster.rs:974-977`) registers `update_attempt`/`update_success`/`update_failure`/`update_empty` but NOT `update_rejected` (phase-21 treated it Envoy-only, since the all-fatal initial load never rejects). Phase 27's reload reject paths (taxonomy (b)/(c)) tick `update_rejected`, so it is promoted from Envoy-only to emitted. The four phase-21 handles + the new `update_rejected` handle are captured as `Arc<Counter>` and threaded to the watcher target (the 06.x shared-handle idiom; per-reload increments live in the reload pipeline).
  4. **D5 shrinks to read-through-handle** (no `last_updated`/`version_info` — already the phase-21 shape).
  5. **The EDS+HC/OD cluster disposition (the SPEC §0-finding-3 reserved call): NO watcher.** A `type: EDS` cluster that ALSO configures active HC or outlier detection gets NO endpoint watcher — its endpoints stay frozen at initial load (phase-21 initial-load-only behavior, non-breaking). This is the safe, non-rejecting choice: such a cluster is VALID config (rejecting it would be wrong), and the endpoint-index-aligned `endpoint_health`/`outlier_detection` arrays would need spawn/drain/rebuild on a count-changing reload — the CDS-class per-endpoint lifecycle churn that is the SPEC §4 deferred non-goal. The watcher is spawned ONLY for PLAIN (no-HC/no-OD) EDS clusters, which GUARANTEES the D1 endpoint-handle swap never desynchronizes an index-aligned array (those arrays are `None` on a plain cluster). Envoy WOULD hot-reload an EDS+HC/OD cluster, so this is a recorded deferred non-goal (no fixture exercises it; the differential does not catch it).
  6. **The §6.1 split does NOT fire — single phase confirmed (ADR-0069 stays UNFIRED).** D5 shrank, the empty-assignment mirror is LESS code than a warm-reject special-case, the observability is the projected second backend, and no new schema/dep emerged — so the refined surface is at or under the SPEC §6.1 projection (~900–1300 LoC / ~9 tasks), below the ~1500-LoC / ~25-task gate.
- **Rationale:** The headline reconciliation is the empty-assignment case (Item 4d). The SPEC projected a warm-reject divergence by analogy to ADR-0066's unknown-cluster divergence (P5(iii)) — but that analogy does NOT hold: phase-26's divergence was forced because the request path `.expect()`ed cluster existence (mirroring Envoy would PANIC or require new request-time 503 code); phase-27's empty-endpoint case is already gracefully handled by `pick()`'s `is_empty()` guard + the existing `synth_no_healthy_upstream` 503, so mirroring Envoy is safe, cheap, and strictly MORE differential-faithful (D-3.3). Eliminating a projected divergence is a better outcome than recording one. The config_dump `last_updated` projection was simply wrong (the EndpointsConfigDump never had that field — a SPEC carry-over assumption from RDS's `RoutesConfigDump`, which DOES carry `last_updated`; EDS does not). Recording all of this here (vs only in the PLAN) honors D-3.5: a future session must understand WHY envoy-rust applies (not rejects) an empty EDS assignment, WHY the EndpointsConfigDump has no `last_updated`, WHY `update_rejected` is now registered for EDS clusters, and WHY an EDS+HC/OD cluster is not watched — without re-running the §6.2 probe.
- **Consequences:**
  - **`PLAN.md` lands at THIS state-2 commit** with the §6.2-VERIFIED facts inline (no `[§6.2-PENDING]` projections — phase 27 verified at PLAN-write): D3 carries the five-class mirror taxonomy (incl. apply-empty); D4 registers `update_rejected`; D5 is narrowed (read-through-handle, no `last_updated`); D6 uses the second-backend observable; the EDS+HC/OD-no-watcher boundary is in the watcher-target build; the §6.1 single-phase confirmation stands.
  - **`BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md` gains:** (a) a "EDS reload semantics" extension to the phase-21 `cluster.<name>.update_*` Stat-name-mapping rows (the counters advance per reload — `2/2` after one successful reload — and `update_rejected` is now emitted by envoy-rust; the apply-empty → `update_success`+503 and empty-envelope → `update_empty` dispositions); and (b) an **EDS row** under the "xDS wire state machine → Filesystem transport (`path_config_source`)" hot-reload subsection (the atomic-rename trigger + envoy-rust's mtime-poll mechanism; the five-class warm-reject/mirror taxonomy incl. apply-empty→503; the `EndpointsConfigDump` reflects-new-assignment / no-`last_updated` shape; the in-flight read-once isolation; the MVP plain-cluster-only scope note + the EDS+HC/OD-no-watcher deferred non-goal).
  - **DECISIONS.md ledger head: ADR-0068** (this ADR). Project-cumulative ADR count 69. **ADR-0069 (the §6.1 split) is reserved-but-UNFIRED** (single phase confirmed). The state-2 PLAN-write commit title carries `[ADR-0068]`.
  - **ADR-0014 REMAINS IN FORCE** (no protos/gRPC transport engaged). **ADR-0028 REMAINS OPEN.** **ADR-0049 governs** (all-fatal STARTUP; the reload is the §5.5 warm-reject carve-out, whose EDS taxonomy this ADR locks — with the deliberate apply-empty reload-vs-startup asymmetry; the Linux-CI-authoritative Provenance applies to fixture 0035 per §5.7). **ADR-0066 governs** the reused atomic-rename trigger + mtime-poll mechanism + the Docker-Desktop-volume/`docker exec` verification methodology this ADR reused. **ADR-0067 is NOT superseded** — this ADR resolves the §6.2 reconciliation ADR-0067 reserved as ADR-0068, within the scope ADR-0067 set (correcting two of its empirically-discoverable projections: empty-assignment disposition and config_dump `last_updated`).

## ADR-0069: Phase-28 pick + scope — OPEN the Load-balancing family with the `RING_HASH` consistent-hashing load balancer (route `hash_policy` on a request header; XX_HASH ring; differentially proven LOCALLY by same-key→same-backend selection across two distinguishable backends); defer CDS/LDS hot-reload, maglev, least_request/random, cookie/source-IP hash

- **Date:** 2026-06-19.
- **Status:** accepted.
- **Context:** Phase `27` (`27-xds-eds-hot-reload`) CLOSED at its state-6 close-out; the sequential ROADMAP rows ended at `27` and STATE pointed at a phase-28 placeholder at lifecycle state-1-next. This ADR records the phase-28 state-1 brainstorm (`superpowers:brainstorming`) pick + scope. The project had run SIX consecutive xDS / dynamic-config phases (18 CDS / 19 LDS / 20 RDS / 21 EDS / 26 RDS-hot-reload / 27 EDS-hot-reload). The fork was: continue the xDS arc (CDS or LDS hot-reload — the ADR-0065/0067-named "next layers") vs open a different ROADMAP family. **Decision: open the Load-balancing family** (`§9` heading `least_request, random, ring_hash, maglev, subset LB, locality-weighted LB, priority load balancing, panic thresholds`) **with `RING_HASH`.** Phase `02` shipped the only LB policy to date — `ROUND_ROBIN` (`crates/envoy-cluster/src/cluster.rs:322` `pick()`; config `LbPolicy { RoundRobin }` at `crates/envoy-config/src/bootstrap.rs:290`, the lone variant; `LEAST_REQUEST` is currently parse-REJECTED at `bootstrap.rs:4319`). The LB family is foundational (subset LB / locality-weighted / priority all layer onto a real policy-dispatch + a request-hash plumbing this phase builds) and was the phase-25 brainstorm's "larger/riskier — needs a NEW distinguishable-backend harness" deferral — **a deferral phase 27 just retired** by building the two-distinguishable-backend harness seed (`spawn_with_marker` + `{{HTTP1_BACKEND_1_PORT}}`/`{{_2_PORT}}` + per-backend `--body-marker`, `tests/differential/src/lib.rs:3019-3041`).
- **Why `RING_HASH` specifically (the only DIFFERENTIABLE LB opener):** the differential contract (D-3.3 / §7.2) requires byte-exact response equivalence for deterministic handlers. With two distinguishable backends in ONE cluster, a request's chosen backend is observable on the wire (body marker) — so a NEW LB policy's SELECTION is differentially provable **only if it is deterministic**: both proxies must pick the SAME backend for the same input. Among the family's policies, ONLY the consistent-hashing ones (`ring_hash`, `maglev`) are deterministic (a request hash key → a fixed host); `random` and `least_request` (P2C random) are NON-deterministic → their selection cannot be byte-exact-differentiated (they would require an ADR relaxing the contract to statistical/consistency checks — a WEAKER differential than this project accepts as a family opener). **`ring_hash` over `maglev`:** ketama-style ring_hash (a sorted ring of host-key hashes + next-clockwise lookup) is the gentler, more-standard opener; maglev requires replicating Envoy's exact permutation-table construction (prime table size 65537, per-host permutation) — strictly more algorithm to match byte-for-byte. Maglev defers.
- **Why NOT continue xDS (CDS/LDS hot-reload) now — deferred AGAIN (not abandoned):**
  - **CDS hot-reload is heavy + split-prone + CI-only-differential.** The `ClusterManager` is `{ clusters: HashMap<String, Arc<Cluster>> }` built-once-immutable (`cluster.rs:745`); hot-reload requires making it a swappable handle AND preserving per-cluster identity across swaps — unchanged clusters must KEEP their connection pools (keyed by cluster-name+endpoint in the H1/H2 pool managers), round-robin cursor, health-check tasks, outlier state, and circuit-breaker budget, while added clusters spin those up and removed clusters tear them down + drain. That is precisely the per-cluster-lifecycle churn ADR-0067 cited when it chose EDS over CDS as "least invasive"; it projects ~1500-2000 LoC and is LIKELY to hit the §6.1 split gate. And like RDS/EDS-reload its differential is reload-triggered → **native-Linux-CI-authoritative** (virtiofs-unobservable on this Docker-Desktop host — the repeatedly-paid CI-iteration tax, memories `host-docker-desktop-virtiofs-no-inotify` + `envoy-rust-state4-ci-first-execution`). LDS hot-reload is heavier still (socket bind/unbind + connection drain). Both remain the named next xDS layers; they are deferred, not dropped.
  - **`ring_hash` is the better-bounded, LOCALLY-verifiable single phase.** Its differential is a NORMAL request/response (send N hash-keyed requests → assert each routes to the same backend on both proxies) — **fully observable on this dev host**, no reload trigger, no Linux-CI-only gate, faster + higher-confidence iteration. It is self-contained in the cluster/LB + route-config layers (no manager-wide swap, no pool lifecycle), reuses the fresh phase-27 two-backend harness, and is a foundational family-opener. Healthy variety after six consecutive xDS phases.
- **Scope (minimum-viable — the SPEC §2 boundary; per §6.3 every item is in-phase-and-tested or an explicit deferred non-goal):**
  - **IN:** a second `LbPolicy::RingHash` variant + a `RingHashLbConfig` (Envoy `Cluster.ring_hash_lb_config`: `minimum_ring_size`/`maximum_ring_size`, `hash_function` accept-XX_HASH-only); a route-level `hash_policy` carrying a single **header** hash source (`hash_policy: [{ header: { header_name } }]`) on `RouteAction_Route` (which today has only `cluster` + `retry_policy`, `bootstrap.rs:1303`); an **xxHash64 (XX_HASH, seed 0) implemented from scratch** (D-3.2: LB algorithms written from scratch; no hashing crate exists or is permitted); the ring construction + next-clockwise lookup; `pick()`/`pick_endpoint()` gain an optional request hash key threaded from the H1 + H2 request paths (the two `pick_endpoint()` call sites, `hcm.rs:392` H1 / `hcm.rs:184` H2); per-cluster LB stats if §6.2 shows any; fixture 0036 (one `RING_HASH` cluster, two distinguishable backends, a header `hash_policy`, a sweep of hash-key values asserting same-key→same-backend bilaterally) + an in-process backstop (ring determinism, empty-ring/no-hash-key fallback, cursor/host-set edge cases) + a BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT "LB selection" extension + a `parse_bootstrap` fuzz seed (the new config surface).
  - **DEFERRED NON-GOALS (explicit):** `maglev`; `least_request`/`random` (non-deterministic — not byte-exact-differentiable); MURMUR_HASH_2 (XX_HASH only); cookie / source-IP / query-parameter / filter-state hash sources (header only); `hash_policy.terminal`, multi-policy hash combination, and `regex_rewrite` on the header hash; weighted hosts in the ring (`LbEndpoint.load_balancing_weight` → unequal ring replicas — phase 27's plain endpoints are weight-1); `RingHashLbConfig.use_hostname_for_hashing`; subset LB / locality-weighted / priority / panic-threshold-for-hashing; CDS/LDS hot-reload (the deferred xDS layers); the gRPC/ADS transport (still ADR-0014/H2-trailers-blocked).
  - **HASH-POLICY ABSENT case:** a `RING_HASH` cluster whose matched route has NO `hash_policy` (or where the named header is absent on the request) — Envoy's documented fallback is to pick a random host. The §6.2 PLAN-write reconnaissance MUST verify envoy-rust's faithful equivalent (likely: fall back to the existing round-robin/`pick()` no-hash path, which is deterministic-enough for a fixture that always supplies the header; the no-header case is a backstop concern, not a differential one). Reserved as a §6.2 reconciliation item.
- **The differential-equivalence question (the core PLAN-write risk, resolved by §6.2 empirical lock-in):** for the fixture to be GREEN, envoy-rust must select the **same backend as Envoy** for each hash key — which requires replicating Envoy's EXACT ring (hash function + the per-host ring-key string format + the replica count derived from `minimum_ring_size`) AND Envoy's exact header-hash. This is the same Envoy-precision bar the project has met for stats names and config_dump bytes. **The §6.2 reconnaissance at the state-2 PLAN-write** (run on THIS Docker-Desktop host — ring_hash is locally observable, no virtiofs/inotify dependency) MUST: stand up `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` with one `RING_HASH` cluster + two distinguishable backends + a header `hash_policy`, sweep a set of header values, RECORD which backend each maps to, and reverse-engineer Envoy's ring construction (hash fn, key format, replica math) precisely enough to replicate it. **If exact cross-proxy selection-identity proves achievable → the STRONG differential** (assert same-key→same-backend bilaterally). **If a residual mismatch proves intractable → the fallback** is a reconciliation ADR defining LB-selection equivalence for consistent-hashing as **same-key-stability** (each proxy maps a key to a FIXED backend across requests, internally consistent) + distribution sanity, rather than cross-proxy identical selection — a documented, weaker-but-honest contract (the xDS-wire-state-machine-equivalence precedent). The SPEC scopes for the STRONG target and names the fallback.
- **Decision:**
  1. **Phase 28 = `28-lb-ring-hash`**, the Load-balancing family opener: the `RING_HASH` consistent-hashing LB with a header `hash_policy`, differentially proven locally.
  2. Scope as above (header-hash + XX_HASH + ring_hash only; the listed deferred non-goals).
  3. **ADR-0070 is reserved** for the state-2 PLAN-write §6.2 reconciliation (lands inline if §6.2 changes the ring/hash construction, the hash-policy-absent fallback, the LB-stat namespace, the config wire shapes, OR forces the same-key-stability equivalence fallback). **ADR-0071 is reserved** for the §6.1 split (PLAUSIBLE this phase — xxHash-from-scratch + ring + route hash_policy config + the pick() threading is a meaty surface; the split valve is held in nominal reserve, e.g. 28.1 [config + hash_policy + xxHash + the pick() threading, a foundation slice] / 28.2 [the ring LB + fixture 0036 + close], decided at the PLAN-write per §6.1).
  4. `SPEC.md` lands at `docs/envoy-rust/phases/28-lb-ring-hash/SPEC.md` at this brainstorm commit; `PLAN.md` is the NEXT session's state-2 step.
- **Rationale:** `ring_hash` is the only LB-family opener that is BOTH foundational AND byte-exact-differentiable, and uniquely it is **locally** differentiable (no reload trigger) — retiring the CI-only-iteration tax that RDS/EDS-reload paid and that CDS/LDS-reload would pay again. It is better-bounded for a single phase than CDS hot-reload (which needs a swappable ClusterManager + per-cluster lifecycle churn and is split-prone), reuses the freshly-built two-backend harness, and opens a family the upstream-robustness / subset-LB / priority work all build on. Deferring CDS/LDS hot-reload is a sequencing choice, not an abandonment — the watcher + atomic-swap + warm-reject primitive (phases 26/27) waits for them. Recording the differentiability reasoning here (why ring_hash not random/least_request; why the same-key→same-backend differential needs exact-Envoy-ring replication; the §6.2 lock-in + the same-key-stability fallback) honors D-3.5: a future session must understand WHY the LB family opens with consistent hashing and WHAT the differential equivalence target is, without re-deriving it.
- **Consequences:**
  - `ROADMAP.md` gains a rows table under the **Load balancing family** heading with row `28` (`status = in-progress`, `depends-on = 02 04 06 21`), the FIRST concrete LB-family row.
  - `STATE.md` advances from the phase-28 placeholder to the real phase-28 identity at lifecycle **state-1-complete / state-2-next** (next skill `superpowers:writing-plans`); the superseded placeholder narrative relocates to `STATE_HISTORY.md` per ADR-0035.
  - The state-2 PLAN-write runs the §6.2 ring/hash reconnaissance (LOCAL Docker, no virtiofs dependency) and authors `PLAN.md` with the empirically-locked ring construction + hash-policy-absent fallback + the §6.1 split decision; ADR-0070 fires inline if material reconciliations emerge.
  - **DECISIONS.md ledger head: ADR-0069** (this ADR). Project-cumulative ADR count 70. **ADR-0070** (the §6.2 reconciliation) and **ADR-0071** (the §6.1 split) are reserved. The phase-28 state-1 brainstorm commit title carries `[ADR-0069]`.
  - **ADR-0014 REMAINS IN FORCE** (ring_hash engages no protos/gRPC). **ADR-0028 REMAINS OPEN.** **ADR-0049 governs** config validity (an invalid `ring_hash_lb_config`/`hash_policy` is a startup-fatal parse error per the all-fatal posture; no reload path this phase). The phases-26/27 reload primitives are NOT engaged (ring_hash is not a hot-reload phase).
- **Provenance:** the recon facts were established by a read-only reconnaissance at this brainstorm HEAD `119df36`: the LB `pick()` (`crates/envoy-cluster/src/cluster.rs:322-373`, round-robin cursor `:122`, health/outlier slow path, takes no per-request context) + `pick_endpoint()` (`:549`); the lone `LbPolicy { RoundRobin }` (`crates/envoy-config/src/bootstrap.rs:290`) + cluster `lb_policy` field (`:195`) + the `LEAST_REQUEST`-rejected validator (`:4319`); the ABSENCE of any route `hash_policy` (`RouteAction_Route { cluster, retry_policy }`, `bootstrap.rs:1303` — no hash field) and the ABSENCE of any hash function in the tree; the two per-request `pick_endpoint()` call sites (H1 `crates/envoy-http1/src/hcm.rs:392`, H2 `crates/envoy-http2/src/hcm.rs:184`); the `ClusterManager { clusters: HashMap<String, Arc<Cluster>> }` built-once shape (`cluster.rs:745`) that makes CDS-hot-reload heavy; the phase-27 two-distinguishable-backend harness (`spawn_with_marker`, `{{HTTP1_BACKEND_1_PORT}}`/`{{_2_PORT}}`, `tests/differential/src/lib.rs:3019-3041`); the 35-fixture baseline (`tests/fixtures/0001`…`0035`; next is `0036`). The §6.2 EMPIRICAL verification against `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` is DEFERRED to the state-2 PLAN-write per the verify-at-PLAN-write discipline (and runs LOCALLY — ring_hash selection is observable without a file-watch/reload trigger, unlike phases 26/27); this brainstorm ADR locks only the pick + scope, which are decisions, not empirically-discoverable wire shapes. Per D-3.5 this ADR lands at the state-1 brainstorm commit alongside the SPEC it scopes.

## ADR-0070: Phase-28 §6.2 empirical-verification reconciliation (run LOCALLY at the state-2 PLAN-write against `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` — one `RING_HASH` cluster, two distinguishable backends, a route header `hash_policy`) — the ring algorithm was CRACKED and EXACTLY VALIDATED (36/36 keys against live Envoy), so the **STRONG differential target FIRES** (cross-proxy byte-identical backend selection): hash = **xxHash64 seed 0**; per-host ring key = **`"<ip:port>_<i>"`** for `i` in `0..(minimum_ring_size / num_hosts)`; ring = sorted `(hash, host)`; request hash = `xxHash64(header_value_bytes, seed 0)`; lookup = first ring entry with `hash ≥ request_hash`, wrapping (`bisect_left` semantics). `ring_hash_lb_config` is OPTIONAL (default `minimum_ring_size` 1024); the empty-header-VALUE is HASHED (not the random fallback — only an ABSENT hash key falls back to a random host); `hash_function: MURMUR_HASH_2` parses-and-accepts in Envoy but is OUT of phase-28 scope (XX_HASH only); a bogus enum is parse-rejected and `minimum_ring_size > maximum_ring_size` is init-rejected. NO material divergence from the SPEC — this ADR LOCKS the open §3 PLAN-write calls.

- **Date:** 2026-06-19.
- **Status:** accepted.
- **Context:** Phase `28` (`28-lb-ring-hash`, the Load-balancing-family opener — the `RING_HASH` consistent-hashing LB) was scoped by ADR-0069, which **reserved ADR-0070** for the state-2 PLAN-write §6.2 empirical-verification reconciliation. Per the phase-27 verify-at-PLAN-write discipline, §6.2 ran **at the state-2 PLAN-write** (this commit) against `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` (digest `sha256:56da5afd7df364350ff92de4fb49a9b09957c17295f2899f0a31cd12c28770c2`). Because ring_hash selection is a NORMAL request/response (no file-watch/reload trigger), the recon ran **LOCALLY** on this Docker-Desktop host — the differentiating advantage of this phase over the phase-26/27 reload phases. **ADR-0070 FIRES to LOCK the empirically-validated ring algorithm** (a load-bearing implementation fact future sessions must not re-derive, D-3.5) and to RECORD the STRONG-target decision; it records NO divergence from the SPEC (the recon CONFIRMED the SPEC's projections and resolved its open §3 calls). The full probe transcript is preserved in `PROGRESS.md` (the state-2 §6.2 entry).
- **§6.2 empirical method (Provenance):** docker network `p28recon-net`; `b1`/`b2` = `hashicorp/http-echo -text=BACKEND_ONE|BACKEND_TWO -listen=:5678` (single endpoint each), discovered by numeric IP (`172.22.0.2:5678` / `172.22.0.3:5678`); `envoy` = `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` on the same network, admin `:9901`, H1 listener `:10000` (`stat_prefix: ingress_http`, route `/` → cluster `ring_cluster` with a route `hash_policy: [{ header: { header_name: "x-hash-key" } }]`, `ring_cluster` = `type: STATIC`, `lb_policy: RING_HASH`, two equal-weight `lb_endpoints`, NO HC / NO OD). A 27-key sweep recorded the backend per `x-hash-key` value; an independent xxHash64-from-scratch replica (validated on known vectors `""`→`0xEF46DB3751D8E999`, `"abc"`→`0x44BC2CF5AD770999`) reproduced ALL keys. Host left clean (all `p28recon-*` containers + network removed).
- **Findings (the SPEC §6.2 checklist):**
  - **Hash function — XX_HASH (xxHash64, seed 0) CONFIRMED** (Envoy's documented `RING_HASH` default; the recon's from-scratch xxHash64 passed the canonical vectors and reproduced Envoy's selection).
  - **The EXACT ring algorithm (the implementation MUST use this — the locked §3.1 call):**
    1. **Ring keys:** for each host, add `replicas = minimum_ring_size / num_hosts` entries (equal weight; 1024/2 = 512 per host in the 2-backend fixture). Entry `i`'s ring hash = `xxHash64( "<address>_<i>", seed=0 )` where `<address>` is the host's `ip:port` string (e.g. `172.22.0.2:5678`) and `<i>` is the decimal index `0..replicas-1`. **The `_` separator is load-bearing** — the recon tested `"<addr><i>"`, `"<addr>:<i>"`, `"<addr>_<i>_"` and they matched only 11–14/27; `"<addr>_<i>"` matched 36/36.
    2. **Ring:** collect all `(hash, host)` entries, **sort ascending by hash**.
    3. **Request hash:** `xxHash64( header_value_bytes, seed=0 )` — the raw `x-hash-key` value bytes.
    4. **Lookup:** the first ring entry whose `hash ≥ request_hash`; if none (request hash > max ring hash), **wrap to ring index 0** (`bisect_left` / first-clockwise semantics).
  - **Determinism + stability — MATCHES** (5 keys × 10 calls each, identical every time). **Spread — MATCHES** (the 27-key sweep split 14 ONE / 13 TWO — the ring distributes; not stuck on one host).
  - **Config wire shapes — MATCH the SPEC §2.1 projection:** the cluster needs `lb_policy: RING_HASH`; `ring_hash_lb_config` is OPTIONAL (omitted → defaults; `minimum_ring_size` default 1024, confirmed identical selections to an explicit `1024`); accepted fields `minimum_ring_size` / `maximum_ring_size` / `hash_function` (enum `XX_HASH` default | `MURMUR_HASH_2`); the route `hash_policy: [{ header: { header_name } }]` shape is accepted and echoed in `/config_dump`.
  - **Hash-policy-absent fallback — MATCHES (with a refinement):** a request with **NO `x-hash-key` header** → Envoy falls back to a **per-request random host** (10 requests = a both-backends mix, not stuck). **REFINEMENT (a new finding, not a divergence):** an **EMPTY header VALUE** (`x-hash-key:` present-but-empty) is **HASHED like any value** (`xxHash64("")` → deterministic backend), NOT the random fallback — only an ABSENT hash result triggers fallback. envoy-rust must mirror this: present-header (even empty) → hash; absent-header (no `hash_policy` match) → the no-hash path.
  - **Invalid-config dispositions — MATCH the ADR-0049 all-fatal posture (two distinct classes):** `hash_function: MURMUR_HASH_2` ACCEPTED (valid enum — but OUT of phase-28 scope, XX_HASH only); a bogus enum (`BOGUS_HASH`) → **proto parse-reject** (`unknown enum value`, exit 1, config-LOAD class); `minimum_ring_size (2048) > maximum_ring_size (1024)` → **semantic init-reject** (`ring hash: minimum_ring_size > maximum_ring_size`, exit 1, post-parse VALIDATION class).
- **Decision:**
  1. **Differential target = STRONG (cross-proxy byte-identical backend selection).** Fixture 0036 asserts, per `x-hash-key` value, that envoy-rust selects the SAME backend as upstream Envoy (proven by the body marker). The same-key-stability FALLBACK that ADR-0069 reserved is **NOT taken** — exact replication is achieved + validated (36/36).
  2. **The implementation MUST use the locked algorithm above** (xxHash64 seed 0; ring key `"<ip:port>_<i>"`; replicas `min_ring_size/num_hosts`; sorted ring; `bisect_left` wrap). xxHash64 is **written from scratch** (D-3.2; no hashing crate is permitted/present) and unit-tested against the canonical vectors before the ring is built on top of it.
  3. **`RingHashLbConfig`** parses `minimum_ring_size` (default 1024) / `maximum_ring_size` (default 8M — confirm the exact default at impl) / `hash_function` (accept **`XX_HASH` only**; `MURMUR_HASH_2` → all-fatal config error, the deliberate phase-28 scope narrowing vs Envoy-accepts; a bogus enum → parse error; `minimum_ring_size > maximum_ring_size` → validation error — all ADR-0049 all-fatal).
  4. **The hash-policy / hash-key plumbing:** present `x-hash-key` (incl. empty value) → `xxHash64(value)` → ring lookup; ABSENT (no `hash_policy` match / header missing) → the no-hash fallback. Fixture 0036 always supplies a non-empty header (the differential exercises the ring); the empty-value-is-hashed + absent-is-fallback distinction is a backstop concern.
  5. **The §6.1 split does NOT fire — single phase confirmed (ADR-0071 stays UNFIRED).** With the algorithm locked + validated, the surface is bounded (xxHash64-from-scratch + the ring + the two config structs + the request-hash threading + fixture 0036 + backstop ≈ ~1000–1300 LoC / ~9 tasks) — at/under the SPEC §6.1 projection, below the ~1500-LoC / ~25-task gate.
- **Rationale:** the recon's headline is that the STRONG target is ACHIEVABLE — the ring algorithm reproduced Envoy's selection on 36/36 keys, so the differential can assert cross-proxy identical selection (the strongest, most-faithful contract; D-3.3) rather than the weaker same-key-stability fallback. Locking the EXACT algorithm here (vs only in PLAN.md, which is consumed/superseded) honors D-3.5: a future session must be able to reproduce the ring (the `_`-separated `ip:port_i` key, the `min/num_hosts` replica count, the seed-0 xxHash64, the `bisect_left` wrap) WITHOUT re-running the probe — these are load-bearing, non-obvious, and a one-character change (the separator) breaks the differential. The empty-header-is-hashed refinement and the two invalid-config rejection classes are recorded so the implementation mirrors them precisely. No SPEC projection was wrong — the recon CONFIRMED them and resolved the open §3 calls — so this is a confirming/locking reconciliation, not a corrective one (contrast ADR-0066/0068, which corrected wrong projections).
- **Consequences:**
  - **`PLAN.md` lands at THIS state-2 commit** with the §6.2-LOCKED algorithm inline (no `[§6.2-PENDING]` projections): the xxHash64-from-scratch task carries the canonical vectors; the ring task carries the exact key format + replica math + `bisect_left` wrap; the config task carries the XX_HASH-only narrowing + the two rejection classes; the request-hash task carries the present-empty-vs-absent distinction; fixture 0036 carries the STRONG cross-proxy-identical-selection assertion over a key sweep.
  - **`BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md` gains** an "LB selection" subsection: `RING_HASH` selection is deterministic + byte-identical to Envoy (the locked algorithm); the no-`hash_policy`-match → random-host fallback (NOT differentially asserted — non-deterministic); the empty-header-value-is-hashed refinement.
  - **DECISIONS.md ledger head: ADR-0070** (this ADR). Project-cumulative ADR count 71. **ADR-0071 (the §6.1 split) is reserved-but-UNFIRED** (single phase confirmed). The state-2 PLAN-write commit title carries `[ADR-0070]`.
  - **ADR-0014 REMAINS IN FORCE** (ring_hash engages no protos/gRPC). **ADR-0028 REMAINS OPEN.** **ADR-0049 governs** the invalid-config all-fatal rejections (the two classes above). **ADR-0069 is NOT superseded** — this ADR resolves the §6.2 reconciliation ADR-0069 reserved as ADR-0070, within the scope ADR-0069 set (confirming its projections + locking its open §3 calls; no projection corrected).

## ADR-0071: Phase-29 pick + scope — CONTINUE the Load-balancing family with the `MAGLEV` consistent-hashing load balancer (the same route header `hash_policy` + XX_HASH as phase 28; the Maglev permutation table replaces the ring; differentially proven LOCALLY by same-key→same-backend selection across two distinguishable backends); consume the phase-28 M28-3 discriminator refactor; defer least_request/random, subset/locality/priority LB, CDS/LDS hot-reload

- **Date:** 2026-06-19.
- **Status:** accepted.
- **Context:** Phase `28` (`28-lb-ring-hash`) CLOSED at its state-6 close-out; the sequential ROADMAP rows ended at `28` and STATE pointed at a phase-29 placeholder at lifecycle state-1-next. This ADR records the phase-29 state-1 brainstorm (`superpowers:brainstorming`) pick + scope. Phase 28 OPENED the Load-balancing family with `RING_HASH`, building the foundational LB machinery: xxHash64 (seed 0) from scratch (`crates/envoy-cluster/src/xxhash.rs`), the route-level `hash_policy` header config + validator (`crates/envoy-config/src/bootstrap.rs`), the `pick()`/`pick_endpoint()` `Option<u64>` request-hash threading + the H1/H2 HCM extraction, the `LbPolicy`/`RingHashLbConfig`/`HashFunction` config surface, and the two-distinguishable-backend differential harness (fixture `0036-lb-ring-hash` + `discover_host_lan_ip`/`{{BACKEND_IP}}`). The fork was: continue the LB family (the next deterministic policy `maglev`; or the non-deterministic `least_request`/`random`; or the higher-level subset/locality/priority LB) vs return to the deferred xDS arc (CDS/LDS hot-reload) vs another family. **Decision: continue the Load-balancing family with `MAGLEV`** — the SECOND (and last) deterministic, byte-exact-differentiable LB policy, explicitly named in the phase-28 SPEC §2.2 as "the LB family's next LB-opener candidate."
- **Why `MAGLEV` specifically (the only remaining DIFFERENTIABLE LB policy + maximal reuse):** the differential contract (D-3.3 / §7.2) requires byte-exact response equivalence for deterministic handlers; among the LB family ONLY the consistent-hashing policies (`ring_hash` done, `maglev`) are deterministic (a request hash key → a fixed host). `random`/`least_request` (P2C-random) are NON-deterministic → their selection cannot be byte-exact-differentiated without a contract-relaxation ADR (a weaker, statistical/consistency-based differential — deferred). **`MAGLEV` is the maximal-reuse next step:** its REQUEST side is IDENTICAL to `RING_HASH` (the same route `hash_policy` header → xxHash64 → `Option<u64>` key threaded through `pick()`), so the entire phase-28 request-hash plumbing + config pattern + xxHash64 + the two-backend fixture harness are reused; only the TABLE-BUILD strategy differs (Google's Maglev permutation table replaces the ketama ring). And like `RING_HASH` the differential is a NORMAL request/response → **LOCALLY observable on this Docker-Desktop host** (no file-watch/reload trigger), retiring the Linux-CI-only-iteration tax that CDS/LDS hot-reload would pay.
- **Why this is the right time for the M28-3 discriminator refactor:** phase 28 used `ring.is_some()` on `Cluster` as the single source of truth for "this cluster is RING_HASH" (`crates/envoy-cluster/src/cluster.rs:209`), with a prominent Maglev-footgun guard comment at the `from_bootstrap` build site warning that a SECOND consistent-hash policy would misclassify and that the discriminator must then become explicit (recorded as the phase-28 REVIEW **M28-3** carry-forward). MAGLEV is exactly that second policy — so this phase consumes M28-3: the `ring: Option<HashRing>` discriminator becomes an explicit hash-LB dispatch (e.g. `hash_lb: Option<HashLb>` with `HashLb { Ring(HashRing), Maglev(MaglevTable) }`), and `pick()` dispatches on the variant. The refactor is load-bearing and must keep BOTH the round-robin path (key inert) AND the existing RING_HASH path (fixture 0036) behavior-identical.
- **Why NOT continue xDS (CDS/LDS hot-reload) now — deferred AGAIN (not abandoned):** unchanged from ADR-0069's reasoning — CDS hot-reload needs a swappable `ClusterManager` + per-cluster pool/HC/OD/budget lifecycle churn on add/remove (split-prone, ~1500-2000 LoC) and its reload-differential is **native-Linux-CI-authoritative** (virtiofs-unobservable on this host). LDS is heavier still. Both remain the named next xDS layers (the phase-26/27 watcher+swap+warm-reject primitive waits for them); MAGLEV is the better-bounded, LOCALLY-verifiable single phase that finishes the deterministic-LB pair while the LB machinery is fresh.
- **Scope (minimum-viable — the SPEC §2 boundary; per §6.3 every item is in-phase-and-tested or an explicit deferred non-goal):**
  - **IN:** a third `LbPolicy::Maglev` variant + a `MaglevLbConfig` (Envoy `Cluster.maglev_lb_config`: `table_size`, default 65537, prime, max 5000011) + validators (non-prime / over-max / config-on-non-MAGLEV-cluster → all-fatal per ADR-0049); a new `crates/envoy-cluster/src/maglev.rs` implementing Envoy's Maglev permutation-table build (per-host `offset`/`skip` from host-key hashes; round-robin populate) + lookup (`table[request_hash % table_size]`), reusing the phase-28 xxHash64; the **M28-3 discriminator refactor** (`ring.is_some()` → an explicit hash-LB dispatch); the route `hash_policy` + the request-hash threading REUSED AS-IS; fixture `0037-lb-maglev` (clone of 0036's shape — two distinguishable backends, the `{{BACKEND_IP}}`/`discover_host_lan_ip` shared-address mechanism, a hash-key sweep asserting same-key→same-backend bilaterally + spread) + an in-process backstop (table determinism / same-key→same-host / spread / no-hash fallback / single-host / the round-robin + RING_HASH regression witnesses) + a `parse_bootstrap` fuzz seed + a BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT "LB selection" extension (a MAGLEV row + the phase-28 M28-1 `maximum_ring_size`-is-parse-validation-only doc clarification folded in).
  - **DEFERRED NON-GOALS (explicit):** `least_request`/`random` (non-deterministic — not byte-exact-differentiable); MURMUR_HASH_2 (XX_HASH only); non-header hash sources + `terminal`/multi-policy/`regex_rewrite` (deferred at phase 28, unchanged); weighted Maglev (`LbEndpoint.load_balancing_weight`); MAGLEV+EDS-hot-reload re-table; MAGLEV+HC/OD as a *differential* (backstop-only); subset LB / locality-weighted / priority / panic-threshold-for-hashing; CDS/LDS hot-reload; the gRPC/ADS transport (still ADR-0014/H2-trailers-blocked).
- **The differential-equivalence question (the core PLAN-write risk, resolved by §6.2 empirical lock-in):** for fixture 0037 to be GREEN, envoy-rust must select the **same backend as Envoy** for each hash key — which requires replicating Envoy's EXACT Maglev table (the host-key hash inputs, the `offset`/`skip` derivation, the prime `table_size` handling, the populate order) AND Envoy's exact header-hash (already matched at phase 28). **The §6.2 reconnaissance at the state-2 PLAN-write** (run on THIS Docker-Desktop host — maglev is locally observable, no virtiofs/inotify dependency) MUST: stand up `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` with one `MAGLEV` cluster + two distinguishable backends + a header `hash_policy`, sweep header values, RECORD which backend each maps to, and reverse-engineer Envoy's table construction precisely enough to replicate it. **If exact cross-proxy selection-identity is achievable → the STRONG differential** (assert same-key→same-backend bilaterally, as phase 28 achieved). **If a residual mismatch proves intractable → the fallback** is a reconciliation ADR (ADR-0072) defining LB-selection equivalence for maglev as **same-key-stability** + distribution sanity, rather than cross-proxy identical selection. The SPEC scopes for the STRONG target and names the fallback.
- **Decision:**
  1. **Phase 29 = `29-lb-maglev`**, the Load-balancing family's second deterministic LB: the `MAGLEV` consistent-hashing LB with the phase-28 header `hash_policy`, differentially proven locally.
  2. Scope as above (header-hash + XX_HASH + maglev-table only; the M28-3 refactor; the listed deferred non-goals).
  3. **ADR-0072 is reserved** for the state-2 PLAN-write §6.2 reconciliation (lands inline if §6.2 changes the Maglev table construction, the table-build hash, the hash-policy-absent fallback, the LB-stat namespace, the config wire shapes, OR forces the same-key-stability equivalence fallback). **ADR-0073 is reserved** for the §6.1 split (projected NOT to fire — the surface is smaller than phase 28's because the request-hash plumbing + xxHash64 + the fixture harness already exist; ~700–1000 LoC / ~8 tasks).
  4. `SPEC.md` lands at `docs/envoy-rust/phases/29-lb-maglev/SPEC.md` at this brainstorm commit; `PLAN.md` is the NEXT session's state-2 step.
- **Rationale:** `maglev` is the only LB-family policy left that is BOTH deterministic (byte-exact-differentiable) AND locally differentiable, and it maximally reuses the phase-28 machinery (the request side is identical — only the table-build differs), making it a well-bounded single phase that completes the deterministic consistent-hashing pair while the LB code is fresh in the codebase. It is the natural M28-3 consumer (the second consistent-hash policy the footgun guard anticipated). Deferring CDS/LDS hot-reload again is a sequencing choice, not abandonment. Recording the differentiability reasoning + the maximal-reuse + the M28-3-consumption here honors D-3.5: a future session must understand WHY the LB family's second phase is maglev (not least_request/random or a return to xDS) and WHAT the differential target is, without re-deriving it.
- **Consequences:**
  - `ROADMAP.md` gains row `29` under the **Load balancing family** heading (`status = planned`, `depends-on = 02 04 06 21 28`), the SECOND concrete LB-family row.
  - `STATE.md` advances from the phase-29 placeholder to the real phase-29 identity at lifecycle **state-1-complete / state-2-next** (next skill `superpowers:writing-plans`); the superseded placeholder narrative relocates to `STATE_HISTORY.md` per ADR-0035.
  - The state-2 PLAN-write runs the §6.2 maglev/table reconnaissance (LOCAL Docker, no virtiofs dependency) and authors `PLAN.md` with the empirically-locked table construction + the M28-3 discriminator-refactor shape + the §6.1 split decision; ADR-0072 fires inline if material reconciliations emerge.
  - **The 3 phase-28 `REVIEW.md` Minors (M28-1..M28-3) are addressed by this phase:** M28-3 (the discriminator refactor) is a load-bearing IN-scope item; M28-1 (the `maximum_ring_size`-parse-validation-only doc clarification) folds into the BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT extension; M28-2 (the cursor-vs-random absent-key fallback) is reused/characterized as-is (the §6.2 fallback verification item).
  - **DECISIONS.md ledger head: ADR-0071** (this ADR). Project-cumulative count 72 (next-available ADR-0072). **ADR-0072** (the §6.2 reconciliation) and **ADR-0073** (the §6.1 split) are reserved.
  - **ADR-0014 REMAINS IN FORCE** (maglev engages no protos/gRPC). **ADR-0028 REMAINS OPEN.** **ADR-0049 governs** config validity (an invalid `maglev_lb_config` is a startup-fatal parse error; no reload path this phase). The phases-26/27 reload primitives are NOT engaged (maglev is not a hot-reload phase).
- **Provenance:** the recon facts were established by a read-only reconnaissance at this brainstorm HEAD `c8423fa`: the phase-28 LB machinery — the `LbPolicy { RoundRobin, RingHash }` enum + `RingHashLbConfig` + `HashFunction` (`crates/envoy-config/src/bootstrap.rs:297`/`:313`/`:338`), the route `hash_policy: Vec<HashPolicy>` + `validate_hash_policy` (`:1369`/`:1419`), the `pick(key_hash: Option<u64>)` dispatch + the `ring: Option<HashRing>` discriminator + the Maglev-footgun guard comment (`crates/envoy-cluster/src/cluster.rs:199-376`), the `xxhash.rs` + `ring_hash.rs` modules; the 36-fixture baseline (`tests/fixtures/0001`…`0036`; next is `0037`) + the fixture-0036 key-sweep differential driver + `discover_host_lan_ip`/`{{BACKEND_IP}}` in `tests/differential/src/lib.rs`. The §6.2 EMPIRICAL verification against `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` is DEFERRED to the state-2 PLAN-write per the verify-at-PLAN-write discipline (and runs LOCALLY — maglev selection is observable without a file-watch/reload trigger, unlike phases 26/27); this brainstorm ADR locks only the pick + scope, which are decisions, not empirically-discoverable wire shapes. Per D-3.5 this ADR lands at the state-1 brainstorm commit alongside the SPEC it scopes.

## ADR-0072: Phase-29 §6.2 empirical-verification reconciliation (run LOCALLY at the state-2 PLAN-write against `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` — one `MAGLEV` cluster, two distinguishable backends, a route header `hash_policy`) — the Maglev table algorithm was CRACKED and EXACTLY VALIDATED (a from-scratch replica reproduced the live-Envoy oracle **80/80** at the default `table_size`, **64/64** at M=17), so the **STRONG differential target FIRES** (cross-proxy byte-identical backend selection, as phase 28 achieved — NOT the same-key-stability fallback): per-host permutation from TWO xxHash64 invocations of the host `ip:port` string (NO `_i` suffix) — `offset = xxHash64(key, seed 0) % M`, `skip = xxHash64(key, seed 1) % (M-1) + 1` (**seed 1** is the cracked unknown; high/low-32-bit and same-hash hypotheses scored ~chance), `permutation[j] = (offset + j·skip) % M`, populate by the round-robin claim loop in config order (earlier host wins contention), lookup = `table[xxHash64(header_value, seed 0) % M]`; `table_size` default 65537, prime, max 5000011. NO material divergence from the SPEC on the load-bearing axes — this ADR LOCKS the open §3 PLAN-write calls; the one disposition correction (config-on-wrong-policy: SPEC projected fatal, Envoy + the phase-28 ring precedent are accept-and-ignore → envoy-rust matches them) is recorded below.

- **Date:** 2026-06-19.
- **Status:** accepted. Supersedes nothing; reconciles the open §3 PLAN-write calls in `phases/29-lb-maglev/SPEC.md` against empirical reality (the ADR-0070 precedent for phase 28). Reserved at ADR-0071 §Decision 3; now FIRED.
- **Context:** Phase-29 (`29-lb-maglev`) state-2 PLAN-write (`superpowers:writing-plans`). ADR-0071 locked the pick + scope but deliberately left the exact Maglev table construction, the differential-equivalence target (STRONG vs fallback), the hash-policy-absent fallback, the LB-stat namespace, the config wire shapes, and the invalid-config dispositions OPEN to the §6.2 reconnaissance (the verify-at-PLAN-write discipline — D-3.3 forbids reading Envoy source to define equivalence; the contract is cracked empirically). The recon stood up `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` with one `MAGLEV` STATIC cluster (two distinguishable `ip:port` backends, host 0 = `172.31.0.2:5678`, host 1 = `172.31.0.3:5678`) + an H1 route header `hash_policy` (`x-hash-key`), swept ≥64 keys to RECORD the key→backend oracle, then hypothesis-tested a from-scratch replica (Python `xxhash` 3.7.0, the project's reference version) until it reproduced the oracle exactly.
- **What was CRACKED (the §6.2-LOCKED algorithm — `crates/envoy-cluster/src/maglev.rs` MUST reproduce it byte-for-byte; full statement in `PLAN.md §A`):**
  - **Host-key string** = the host address `asString()` = the **`ip:port`** string (e.g. `172.31.0.2:5678`), IPv4. **NO `_i` replica suffix** (unlike the ring's `{address}_{i}` — the suffix is ring-only).
  - **Per-host derivation:** `offset = xxHash64(key, seed 0) % M`; `skip = xxHash64(key, seed 1) % (M − 1) + 1`. The **seed-1 second invocation** for `skip` was the central unknown; rejected hypotheses (all ~32–44/80, i.e. chance): `skip` from the high 32 bits of a single seed-0 hash, the low/high split, and `skip` from the same seed-0 hash. Both invocations reuse the phase-28 from-scratch xxHash64 (now generalized to a seeded `xxh64_seed`).
  - **Permutation + populate:** `permutation[j] = (offset + j·skip) % M`; populate `table[0..M]` of host indices by the round-robin claim loop iterating hosts in **config / endpoint-list order**; on a slot collision the **earlier-config-order host wins** (disambiguated at M=17: config order 64/64 vs reversed 60/64).
  - **`table_size` M:** default **65537**; must be prime; max **5000011**. **Request lookup:** `table[xxHash64(header_value, seed 0) % M]` — the SAME request hash as phase-28 RING_HASH (the existing `hash_request_key`/`xxh64` seed-0 path; an empty-but-present value hashes `xxh64(b"")` — NOT a fallback).
- **REPLICA MATCH:** **80/80** (64 `key-N` + 16 misc) at the default M=65537 — the STRONG bar (≥64/64) is met; **64/64** independently at M=17 (used to disambiguate populate order). Full-table distribution at M=65537: host0 = 32769 slots, host1 = 32768 (near-perfect). Same-key stability confirmed (a key ×5 → same backend). The §A oracle table (24 representative `key → host` pairs) is the pinned `maglev.rs` unit-test ground truth.
- **Config dispositions (§6.2-verified):**
  - **non-prime `table_size`** (e.g. 100) → upstream **startup-fatal** (`"The table size of maglev must be prime number"`); envoy-rust mirrors with startup-fatal `ConfigError::MaglevTableSizeNotPrime` (ADR-0049 all-fatal).
  - **`table_size` > 5000011** → upstream **startup-fatal** (PGV `value must be less than or equal to 5000011`); 5000011 boots. envoy-rust mirrors with `ConfigError::MaglevTableSizeTooLarge`; over-max is checked BEFORE the bounded `is_prime` trial loop.
  - **`maglev_lb_config` on a non-MAGLEV cluster** → upstream **silently accepted-and-ignored** (boots, runs round-robin). **This CORRECTS the SPEC §2.1 projection** (which wanted it fatal): envoy-rust **accept-and-ignores** it (validation GATED to MAGLEV clusters), MATCHING both upstream Envoy AND the phase-28 `ring_hash_lb_config`-on-non-RING_HASH precedent (`bootstrap.rs:2629` + test `accepts_ring_hash_lb_config_on_non_ring_hash_cluster`). Parity wins over the projected stricter-than-Envoy posture for the wrong-policy case; the non-prime / over-max checks remain all-fatal (those ARE fatal in Envoy).
- **Fallback / stats (§6.2-verified):** header-ABSENT → non-deterministic cursor/round-robin path (matches phase-28 **M28-2** — a characterization, NOT a differential assertion); header-PRESENT-but-EMPTY → deterministic (hashes `xxh64(b"")`), preserving the phase-28 present-empty-vs-absent `.map()` distinction. **LB stats: NONE portable** (only generic `cluster.<name>.lb_*`; no maglev-table namespace) → emit no LB stat (the phase-21/24/28 discipline).
- **Decision:**
  1. **STRONG differential target FIRES** — fixture `0037-lb-maglev` asserts cross-proxy byte-identical backend selection per hash key (the same-key-stability fallback ADR-0071 reserved is NOT needed; exact table replication is achieved).
  2. **`maglev.rs` implements the §6.2-LOCKED algorithm above**, byte-for-byte; the pinned §A oracle is the regression gate.
  3. **Config validation is MAGLEV-gated**: non-prime → `MaglevTableSizeNotPrime`, over-max → `MaglevTableSizeTooLarge` (both startup-fatal); `maglev_lb_config` on a non-MAGLEV cluster is accept-and-ignored (Envoy parity + the ring precedent — the SPEC's fatal projection is overridden).
  4. **The M28-3 discriminator refactor** replaces `ring: Option<HashRing>` with `hash_lb: Option<HashLb>` (`HashLb { Ring(HashRing), Maglev(MaglevTable) }`); the RING_HASH path stays byte-identical (fixture 0036), the round-robin path a no-op.
  5. The phase-28 **xxHash64 is generalized** to a seeded `xxh64_seed(data, seed)` (seed 0 byte-identical to the existing `xxh64`; seed 1 drives the maglev `skip`).
- **§6.1 split: does NOT fire** — the PLAN is **8 tasks / est. ~450–550 net LoC**, well under the ~25-task / ~1500-LoC gate (xxHash64, the route-`hash_policy` request plumbing, the `LbPolicy`/`*LbConfig` config pattern, and the two-backend fixture harness all pre-exist). **ADR-0073 remains UNFIRED** (reserved).
- **Consequences:**
  - `PLAN.md` lands with the empirically-locked table construction inline (§A — no `[§6.2-PENDING]` projections); `PROGRESS.md` skeleton + the 8-task breakdown; `ROADMAP.md` row `29` flips `planned → in-progress`; `STATE.md` advances to state-2-complete / state-3-next (next skill `superpowers:subagent-driven-development`), with the superseded state-1 narrative relocated to `STATE_HISTORY.md` per ADR-0035.
  - **DECISIONS.md ledger head: ADR-0072** (this ADR). Project-cumulative count 73 (next-available ADR-0073). **ADR-0073** (the §6.1 split) remains reserved (unfired this phase).
  - **ADR-0014 REMAINS IN FORCE** (maglev engages no protos/gRPC). **ADR-0028 REMAINS OPEN.** **ADR-0049 governs** config validity (invalid `maglev_lb_config` is startup-fatal; no reload path). **ADR-0070** (the phase-28 ring §6.2 lock) is the precedent this ADR mirrors; **ADR-0071** is the phase-29 scope this reconciles.
- **Provenance:** the recon ran at the phase-29 state-2 PLAN-write against `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` on this Docker-Desktop host (maglev selection is locally observable — no file-watch/reload trigger, unlike phases 26/27); the from-scratch replica (Python `xxhash` 3.7.0) reproduced the live oracle 80/80 (default M) and 64/64 (M=17). All scratch work was in `/tmp` (no repo mutation); containers + network cleaned up. Per D-3.5 this ADR lands at the state-2 PLAN-write commit alongside the `PLAN.md` it locks.
