## ADR-0083: Phase-34 pick + scope — land the **request-driven dynamic-metadata emitter** that consumes phase-33's infrastructure unchanged: the `envoy.filters.http.header_to_metadata` HTTP filter (the 12th `HttpFilterInstance` variant, decode-side, `Continue`-only) which evaluates configured `request_rules` against the request headers and merges the extracted **string** value into `req.dynamic_metadata` under a `metadata_namespace`→`key` (on_header_present: the header value or a static `value` override; on_header_missing: a static fallback) + fixture `0042` — a byte-exact, DETERMINISTIC, LOCALLY-observable differential (the probe controls the header value, so the `%DYNAMIC_METADATA(ns:key)%` render of the extracted value is byte-identical cross-proxy); the **thin reuse-slice MVP** (request_rules only, string-only, NO header-removal/typed-values/base64/regex/response_rules); choose `header_to_metadata` over a metadata CONSUMER (jwt_authn `payload_in_metadata` / rbac dynamic-metadata) and over `json_format` and the non-string-Value generalization; REUSE the phase-33 store + `%DYNAMIC_METADATA%` operator + H1/H2 threading UNCHANGED (no new infrastructure)

**Status:** Accepted (phase-34 state-1 brainstorm; `superpowers:brainstorming`). Scope-locks phase `34-header-to-metadata`. Supersedes nothing. **ADR-0084 reserved** for the §6.2 empirical-verification reconciliation (the exact `header_to_metadata` config wire shape + the default `metadata_namespace` + the on_header_present value-vs-override precedence + the on_header_missing semantics + the config-validity disposition, locked LOCALLY at the state-2 PLAN-write); the §6.1 split is projected NOT to fire (no separate reserved ADR — if it fires, ADR-0084 covers it, and the §6.2 reconciliation takes the next-available number).

**Context.** Phase 33 (`set-metadata-dynamic-metadata`, the dynamic-metadata critical-path unlock) CLOSED 2026-06-23; ROADMAP rows `00`–`33` are all `done`. Phase 33 built the per-request **dynamic-metadata store** (`dynamic_metadata` on `FilterRequest` + `AccessLogRecord`, threaded at both H1 + H2 record-build sites), the `envoy.filters.http.set_metadata` filter (a STATIC-value emitter — the 11th `HttpFilterInstance` variant), and the `%DYNAMIC_METADATA(namespace:key)%` access-log command-operator. The phase-33 SPEC §2.2 + ADR-0080 explicitly named `header_to_metadata` as **"the natural next pick after phase 33"** — the pure-additive request-header-driven follow-up that reuses this store + operator UNCHANGED. The candidate picks weighed at this brainstorm (differential leverage × reuse × locality): (i) `header_to_metadata` [THIS pick]; (ii) a metadata CONSUMER (jwt_authn `payload_in_metadata` / rbac dynamic-metadata permission/principal conditions); (iii) `json_format`/`typed_json_format`; (iv) non-string metadata Values + nested-path `%DYNAMIC_METADATA(ns:key:sub)%`.

**Decision.** Land the **smallest request-driven dynamic-metadata producer** that is differentially testable, the **thin reuse-slice**: the **`envoy.filters.http.header_to_metadata` filter** — the 12th `HttpFilterInstance` variant (`crates/envoy-filter/src/header_to_metadata.rs`), decode-side, which on `decode_headers` evaluates each configured `request_rule` and merges the extracted **string** value into `req.dynamic_metadata` under `metadata_namespace`→`key` (returning `Decision::Continue`, NEVER `StopAndSend`; encode-side inert), following the `set_metadata`/`cdn_loop` add-a-decode-side-filter pattern. Per-rule (string-only MVP): **on_header_present** writes the matched header's value (or the rule's static `value` override) when the header is present; **on_header_missing** writes a static fallback `value` when the header is absent. Config: a `HeaderToMetadataConfig { request_rules: Vec<Rule> }` + `Rule { header, on_header_present, on_header_missing }` + `KeyValuePair { metadata_namespace (default `envoy.lb`, §6.2-VERIFY), key, value }` in `crates/envoy-config/src/bootstrap.rs` + a `HttpFilterTypedConfig::HeaderToMetadata` variant (`@type …header_to_metadata.v3.Config`) + a `validate_http_filters` arm (boot-fatal on a malformed rule, ADR-0049). Fixture `0042` drives a custom `log_format` with `%DYNAMIC_METADATA(ns:key)%` over an H1 listener carrying a `[header_to_metadata, router]` chain — a byte-identical access-log line cross-proxy (header-present + header-missing probes). The store, the `%DYNAMIC_METADATA%` operator, and the H1/H2 capture-before-drop threading are REUSED UNCHANGED from phase 33 (no new infrastructure).

**Why this is the recommendation (reuse + locality + the natural-next-pick leverage, the D-3.3 doctrine):**
- **MAXIMAL reuse / least new infrastructure.** Phase 33 built the store + operator + the dual H1/H2 threading; `header_to_metadata` writes to `req.dynamic_metadata` exactly as `set_metadata` does, so it adds NO store/operator/threading work — only the filter's header-extraction logic + a config schema. The smallest possible phase that still lands a STRONGER differential.
- **STRONGER request-driven differential, still DETERMINISTIC + byte-exact + LOCALLY observable.** Unlike `set_metadata`'s static literal, the value is derived from the request the harness controls (the header value) — a more meaningful exercise of the store — yet still a pure function of the (fixed) probe + static config, so the `%DYNAMIC_METADATA(ns:key)%` render is byte-identical on both proxies, observable via a file scrape on a normal request/response (NOT Linux-CI-only).
- **The explicitly-named natural next pick.** Both ADR-0080 and the phase-33 SPEC §2.2 elevated `header_to_metadata` as the pure-additive follow-up; this discharges it.
- **Thin reuse-slice over the wider MVP (minimum-viable filter risk).** `request_rules` + string-only `on_header_present`/`on_header_missing` is the trivial-est request-driven emitter, focusing the phase on the extraction logic; `response_rules`, typed (NUMBER/PROTOBUF) values, `encode: BASE64`, `regex_value_rewrite`, and the `remove` header-mutation are each pure-additive §2.2 increments (the latter two would pull in the non-string Value-enum and an echo-server backend fixture respectively).

**The differential-risk axis (the extracted-value byte-form + the config wire shape) is handled by §6.2:** the key risks are the `request_rules`/`Rule`/`KeyValuePair` wire shape v1.33.0 accepts, the default `metadata_namespace`, the on_header_present value-vs-static-`value` precedence, the on_header_missing semantics, and the malformed-config disposition — all **§6.2-VERIFY**, locked LOCALLY at the state-2 PLAN-write against `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` (**ADR-0084 FIRES** on any material divergence). The extracted scalar-string value byte form is projected raw-unquoted (the phase-33 §A3 ground truth for the operator render is unchanged — the operator is reused verbatim).

**Rejected alternatives** (weighed at this brainstorm against reuse + leverage + locality):
- **(ii) A metadata CONSUMER (jwt_authn `payload_in_metadata` / rbac dynamic-metadata conditions)** — reads the store rather than writing it; higher complexity (jwt payload extraction / rbac condition evaluation against metadata) and better served once a RICHER, request-driven PRODUCER exists to give consumers varied metadata to read. A future phase after the producer side is complete.
- **(iii) `json_format`/`typed_json_format` access-log encoding** — a self-contained Observability LEAF that reuses the phase-32 engine but exercises NONE of the new metadata machinery and unlocks no filter-family follow-up. Lower leverage; its own future phase.
- **(iv) Non-string metadata Values + nested-path `%DYNAMIC_METADATA(ns:key:sub)%`** — a Value-enum type-system increment (the phase-33 §2.2 deferral) with no new filter; better deferred until a consumer needs typed metadata. Larger blast radius (touches the store type + the operator render) for no new differential surface.

**Scope (minimum-viable, see SPEC §2).** IN: the `header_to_metadata` filter (12th variant, decode-side `Continue`-only, request_rules only, string-only on_header_present [header value or static override] + on_header_missing [static fallback]) + its config schema/variant/validator (+ a `ConfigError` disposition §6.2-disposed); the operator + store + H1/H2 threading REUSED UNCHANGED; fixture `0042` (header-present + header-missing, ≥2 probes, byte-exact cross-proxy) + an in-process backstop (present/missing/override/multi-rule + the H2 thread) + a `parse_bootstrap` seed + a BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT extension. DEFERRED (each a §2.2 named future home): `response_rules` (encode-side); typed (NUMBER/PROTOBUF_VALUE) values; `encode: BASE64`; `regex_value_rewrite`; the `remove` header-mutation; per-route `typed_per_filter_config`; metadata consumers (jwt_authn/rbac/ext_authz); `json_format`/`typed_json_format`/gRPC-ALS/OTLP/tracing/stats-sink/tap.

**§6.1 split** projected NOT to fire (~600–900 LoC / ~7–9 tasks — one trivial decode-side filter + one config variant/validator + one fixture, ADDING NO infrastructure since the store/operator/threading are reused; smaller than phase 33, comparable to `cdn_loop`/`csrf`); the natural seam if forced is `34.1` (the filter + config + validator + variant — a foundation slice, no new fixture, proven by all 41 existing fixtures staying green) / `34.2` (fixture `0042` + BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT + fuzz/seed + close).

**Consequences.** `crates/envoy-filter/` gains a `header_to_metadata` filter (12th `HttpFilterInstance` variant); `crates/envoy-config/` gains a `HeaderToMetadataConfig` + a `HttpFilterTypedConfig::HeaderToMetadata` variant + a `validate_http_filters` arm (+ a `ConfigError` disposition §6.2-disposed); `crates/envoy-accesslog/` is UNCHANGED (the `%DYNAMIC_METADATA%` operator + store are reused verbatim); the H1/H2 HCM threading is UNCHANGED (it already carries any `req.dynamic_metadata`). No new crate, no new dependency, no new fuzz target projected (the existing `parse_bootstrap` covers the new config). `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` holds. The pick continues the HTTP-filters family (the request-driven metadata producer) and consumes phase-33's infrastructure. **DECISIONS.md ledger head: ADR-0083** (this ADR; project-cumulative count 82 [ADR-0082 reserved-but-UNFIRED for the phase-33 §6.1 split that did not fire]; next-available **ADR-0084**). **ADR-0084** reserved (§6.2 reconciliation). **ADR-0014 REMAINS IN FORCE; ADR-0028 REMAINS OPEN; ADR-0049 governs** the config-validity all-fatal posture. The state-2 PLAN-write is the next session (`superpowers:writing-plans`), which runs the §6.2 reconnaissance and fires ADR-0084.

## ADR-0084: Phase-34 §6.2 empirical-verification reconciliation (run LOCALLY at the state-2 PLAN-write against `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` — an H1 `direct_response` listener + a `header_to_metadata` filter + a file access logger with a `%DYNAMIC_METADATA%`-bearing custom `log_format`, request probes with/without headers, bytes via `od -c`, config round-tripped through `/config_dump`) — TWO MATERIAL divergences from the SPEC projection (the default `metadata_namespace` is `envoy.filters.http.header_to_metadata` NOT `envoy.lb`; when both a static `value` and a present header exist the static `value` WINS, the header value is discarded), plus the headline confirmations (the `@type …v3.Config`; the `request_rules`/`KeyValuePair` wire shape; the RAW unquoted scalar value byte form; the on_header_missing-requires-value + present-but-empty→unset + absent→`-` semantics; the boot-fatal config-validity, ADR-0049) so the **STRONG differential target FIRES** (cross-proxy byte-identical custom-format access-log line for the header-derived value); this ADR LOCKS the open SPEC §3 PLAN-write calls

**Status:** Accepted (phase-34 state-2 PLAN-write; `superpowers:writing-plans`). Reconciles SPEC §3 / §6.2 for phase `34-header-to-metadata`. Supersedes nothing. Builds on ADR-0083 (the pick + scope).

**Method.** A read-only subagent stood up live `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` (Docker) with an H1 `direct_response` listener, a `[header_to_metadata, router]` chain, and a file access logger whose `log_format.text_format_source.inline_string` carried `%DYNAMIC_METADATA(...)%` operators; drove `curl` probes with/without request headers; captured EXACT bytes with `od -c` and the booted config via `GET /config_dump`; cleaned up all containers. The phase-33 `%DYNAMIC_METADATA%` operator + dynamic-metadata store were NOT re-verified (reused unchanged; their byte form is the ADR-0081 ground truth).

**LOCKED FACTS (the ground truth `PLAN.md §A` carries inline; the task encodings derive from these — do NOT re-derive):**
1. **Config wire shape (§A1) — CONFIRMED.** `@type = type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.header_to_metadata.v3.Config`; top-level `request_rules` list; each rule `{ header, on_header_present, on_header_missing, cookie?, remove? }`; each action a `KeyValuePair { metadata_namespace, key, value, type, encode }`. Unknown fields boot-fatal. Phase-34 models the request-side string-only subset (`cookie`/`remove`/`encode`/non-`STRING` `type` §2.2-deferred → `deny_unknown_fields`/the `MetadataType`-only-`String` enum rejects them boot-fatal, envoy-rust stricter; documented; not differentially exercised).
2. **Default `metadata_namespace` (§A2) — MATERIAL DIVERGENCE.** When `metadata_namespace` is OMITTED, Envoy defaults it to **`envoy.filters.http.header_to_metadata`** (the filter's canonical name), NOT the SPEC-projected `envoy.lb`. PROVEN by a render-back (`%DYNAMIC_METADATA(envoy.filters.http.header_to_metadata:tier)%` → `prod`; `%DYNAMIC_METADATA(envoy.lb:tier)%` → `-`). The MVP serde default for `metadata_namespace` is `"envoy.filters.http.header_to_metadata"`.
3. **on_header_present precedence + byte form (§A3) — MATERIAL DIVERGENCE + CONFIRMED bytes.** A present header writes the RAW header value, UNQUOTED (`od -c` → `p r o d`). **DIVERGENCE: a static `value` configured on `on_header_present` WINS over the present header's value** (the header value is discarded) — so `on_header_present` writes `value` if set, ELSE the header value. `type` defaults to STRING; `type: NUMBER` with a non-numeric header silently drops the key (out of MVP scope — the MVP models only STRING).
4. **on_header_missing semantics (§A4) — CONFIRMED.** `on_header_missing` REQUIRES a `value` (boot-fatal without). Header absent + `on_header_missing` → renders the static `value` (raw). Present-but-EMPTY header → key UNSET (Envoy treats empty as neither present nor missing → `-`). Header absent + no `on_header_missing` → key unset → `-`.
5. **Config-validity (§A5) — CONFIRMED boot-fatal (exit 1).** All five malformed cases fail boot with specific errors: empty `header`, empty `key` (PGV length ≥ 1), no-action rule, `on_header_missing` with no `value`, unknown field. envoy-rust matches via a new `ConfigError::HeaderToMetadataInvalidRule` (cases a-d, checked in `validate_http_filters`) + serde `deny_unknown_fields` (case e).
6. **Determinism (§A6) — STRONG target FIRES.** 50 identical requests → exactly one unique access-log render line (a pure function of request + static config; no host/clock terms), so both proxies emit a byte-identical line. The cross-proxy whole-line byte-exact differential (`Driver::Http1AccessLogByteExact`, reused verbatim) is the STRONG target — no fallback. (Note: the file logger buffers ~1s → the fixture/harness flushes via the existing 0040/0041 file-scrape path.)

**Disposition of the SPEC §3 open PLAN-write calls (now LOCKED in `PLAN.md §A`):** §3.1 → `@type …v3.Config`, `request_rules` + `KeyValuePair { metadata_namespace, key, value, type }` request-side string-only subset, default namespace `envoy.filters.http.header_to_metadata`; §3.2 → static `value` wins, raw unquoted bytes; §3.3 → on_header_missing requires `value`, present-but-empty → unset, absent → `-`; §3.4 → boot-fatal, ONE new `ConfigError::HeaderToMetadataInvalidRule` + reuse `UnsupportedHttpFilter` (name) + `deny_unknown_fields`; §3.5/§3.6 → `direct_response`, header-present + header-missing probes via `AccessLogByteExactProbe.extra_headers`; §3.7 → harness reused verbatim; §3.8 → existing `parse_bootstrap` covers it, NO new target + a seed; §3.9 → split NOT fired (~7 tasks).

**Material divergences from the SPEC:** TWO — (i) the default `metadata_namespace` is `envoy.filters.http.header_to_metadata`, not `envoy.lb`; (ii) the on_header_present static-`value` precedence (static wins over the header value). Both are encoded in `PLAN.md §A` (A2, A3) and the Task-1/Task-3 code. Neither changes the §6.1 split projection (still NOT fired) nor the strong differential target (still FIRES).

**Consequences.** `PLAN.md` lands with these facts inline (no `[§6.2-PENDING]`) + 7 TDD tasks (config schema+variant / validator+ConfigError / the filter / instance wiring / H1+H2 backstops / fixture 0042 / BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT+seed). The `envoy-accesslog` crate is UNTOUCHED (the `%DYNAMIC_METADATA%` operator + store reused verbatim). No new crate, no new dependency, no new fuzz target. `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` holds. **DECISIONS.md ledger head: ADR-0084** (this ADR; project-cumulative count 84; next-available **ADR-0085**). **ADR-0014 REMAINS IN FORCE; ADR-0028 REMAINS OPEN; ADR-0049 governs** the config-validity all-fatal posture. The state-3 implementation is the next session (`superpowers:subagent-driven-development`).

## ADR-0085: Phase-35 pick + scope — land the **FIRST dynamic-metadata CONSUMER**, closing the produce→consume loop the phase-33/34 metadata arc teed up: extend the EXISTING `envoy.filters.http.rbac` filter (phase 10) with a **`metadata` Permission/Principal condition** (a string-only `MetadataMatcher` that reads `req.dynamic_metadata` written earlier in the same decode pass by an upstream producer filter, e.g. phase-34 `header_to_metadata`) + fixture `0043` — a byte-exact, DETERMINISTIC, LOCALLY-observable differential (the probe controls the request header → the metadata value → the RBAC verdict, so the `200`+`direct_response`-body vs `403`+`RBAC: access denied` response is byte-identical cross-proxy); the **thin reuse-slice MVP** (single-segment `path`, `string_match` ValueMatcher only, NO non-string Values / nested path / `invert` / shadow_rules / per-route override); choose the rbac metadata-consumer over `header_to_metadata` `response_rules` (another producer, lights up no new vein, needs new encode-side metadata-capture plumbing), over jwt_authn `payload_in_metadata` (another producer), over `json_format` (a self-contained Observability leaf), and over the non-string-Value generalization; ADDS NO new `HttpFilterInstance` variant (RBAC is the existing phase-10 variant) and NO new infrastructure (the store + producers + `%DYNAMIC_METADATA%` operator + the decode-pipeline shared-`&mut FilterRequest` threading are all reused UNCHANGED)

**Status:** Accepted (phase-35 state-1 brainstorm; `superpowers:brainstorming`). Scope-locks phase `35-rbac-dynamic-metadata`. Supersedes nothing. **ADR-0086 reserved** for the §6.2 empirical-verification reconciliation (the exact `MetadataMatcher`/`ValueMatcher` wire shape + the `filter`→namespace correspondence + the present/absent match semantics + the StringMatcher modes accepted + the config-validity disposition, locked LOCALLY at the state-2 PLAN-write); the §6.1 split is projected NOT to fire (no separate reserved ADR — if it fires, ADR-0086 covers it, and the §6.2 reconciliation takes the next-available number).

**Context.** Phase 34 (`header-to-metadata`, the request-driven dynamic-metadata emitter) CLOSED 2026-06-24; ROADMAP rows `00`–`34` are all `done`; `34` is the highest defined row → STATE.md is "awaiting next planning". The metadata arc so far (phases 32→33→34) built the entire PRODUCER side: the access-log command-operator engine (32), the per-request dynamic-metadata store + the `set_metadata` static emitter + the `%DYNAMIC_METADATA(namespace:key)%` operator (33), and the request-header-driven `header_to_metadata` emitter (34). Every metadata SINK so far is the access log. The phase-33 SPEC §2.2 + ADR-0080 + the phase-34 SPEC §2.2 + ADR-0083 all explicitly named **"rbac dynamic-metadata conditions"** (and jwt_authn `payload_in_metadata` / ext_authz) as the consumers that "become reachable once metadata is emittable + loggable". The candidate picks weighed at this brainstorm (differential leverage × reuse × locality): (i) the rbac metadata-CONSUMER [THIS pick]; (ii) `header_to_metadata` `response_rules` (the encode-side producer increment); (iii) jwt_authn `payload_in_metadata` (a producer); (iv) `json_format`/`typed_json_format`; (v) non-string metadata Values + nested-path resolution.

**The pivotal feasibility fact (verified at this brainstorm).** The decode pipeline threads ONE `&mut FilterRequest` through every filter in chain order (`crates/envoy-filter/src/pipeline.rs:76` — `decode_headers` iterates `self.filters.iter_mut()`, first `StopAndSend` short-circuits), so a filter placed AFTER `header_to_metadata` reads the `req.dynamic_metadata` that `header_to_metadata` wrote IN THE SAME PASS. This makes a metadata CONSUMER a thin reuse-slice (no new threading) — confirmed by reading `pipeline.rs` + `rbac.rs` (the `eval_permission`/`eval_principal(p, &FilterRequest)` evaluators already receive the `dynamic_metadata`-carrying request).

**Decision.** Land the **smallest dynamic-metadata CONSUMER** that is differentially testable, the **thin reuse-slice**: extend the EXISTING phase-10 `envoy.filters.http.rbac` filter with a **`metadata` condition** on both Permission and Principal. Config: add a `Metadata(MetadataMatcher)` variant to the `Permission` and `Principal` enums (`crates/envoy-config/src/bootstrap.rs`, via the existing hand-rolled "exactly one map key" `Deserialize` visitors — a new `"metadata"` arm on each) + a `MetadataMatcher { filter, path: Vec<MetadataPathSegment>, value: ValueMatcher }` + `MetadataPathSegment { key }` + a string-only `ValueMatcher` whose only MVP variant is `StringMatch(StringMatcher)` (reusing the 04.x `StringMatcher` verbatim); all `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`. Runtime: add `RuntimePermission::Metadata`/`RuntimePrincipal::Metadata` (`crates/envoy-filter/src/rbac.rs`), lowered by the existing `lower_permission`/`lower_principal`, plus an `eval` arm reading `req.dynamic_metadata.get(filter)?.get(path[0].key)` and applying the StringMatcher (absent namespace/key → no match). The RBAC decision matrix + the `403` + `b"RBAC: access denied"` local reply are UNCHANGED (phase 10). Fixture `0043` carries a `[header_to_metadata, rbac, router]` H1 chain over a `direct_response` route (projected): `X-Tier: prod` → metadata `tier=prod` → the metadata condition matches → ALLOW → `200` + body; `X-Tier: dev`/absent → no match → DENY → `403` + body — both byte-identical cross-proxy. The store, the producers, the `%DYNAMIC_METADATA%` operator, and the decode threading are REUSED UNCHANGED (no new infrastructure; no new `HttpFilterInstance` variant).

**Why this is the recommendation (the loop-closing leverage + maximal reuse + locality, the D-3.3 doctrine):**
- **Closes the produce→consume loop — the highest leverage.** Phases 33/34 made metadata emittable + loggable; this proves it is a routing-DECISION input (allow/deny), not just a logging artifact. It is the explicitly-named payoff of the whole metadata arc and the gateway to the metadata-consumer pattern (the largest remaining HTTP-filters vein).
- **MAXIMAL reuse / least new code.** It adds NO `HttpFilterInstance` variant (RBAC exists since phase 10) and NO infrastructure — only one matcher type on the RBAC config + one arm on the recursive evaluator. Reuses the phase-10 RBAC engine, the 04.x `StringMatcher`, the phase-33 store, the phase-34 producer, and the decode-pipeline threading verbatim. The thinnest possible consumer.
- **STRONG, DETERMINISTIC, byte-exact, LOCALLY observable differential.** The probe controls the header → the metadata → the verdict, so the `200`/`403` + body is a pure function of the (fixed) probe + static config, byte-identical on both proxies, observable on a normal request/response (NO reload trigger — NOT Linux-CI-only, unlike phases 26/27). The same strong differential class as phases 10/22.
- **Thin reuse-slice over the wider MVP.** Single-segment `path` + `string_match`-only `ValueMatcher` is the trivial-est consumer; non-string Values, multi-segment/nested paths, `invert`, `present_match`, shadow_rules, and per-route override are each pure-additive §2.2 increments (the non-string/nested ones ride the shared phase-33/34 Value-enum generalization).

**The differential-risk axis (the matcher wire shape + the match semantics) is handled by §6.2:** the key risks are the `MetadataMatcher`/`ValueMatcher` wire shape v1.33.0 accepts (`filter` / `path: [{ key }]` / `value: { string_match }`), the `filter`→namespace correspondence (vs `header_to_metadata`'s `metadata_namespace`, default `envoy.filters.http.header_to_metadata` per ADR-0084), the present-but-empty / absent-key / absent-namespace match dispositions, the StringMatcher modes accepted, and the malformed-config disposition — all **§6.2-VERIFY**, locked LOCALLY at the state-2 PLAN-write against `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` (**ADR-0086 FIRES** on any material divergence). The `200`/`403` + `RBAC: access denied` (19-byte) verdict bytes are the phase-10 ground truth, reused.

**Rejected alternatives** (weighed at this brainstorm against reuse + leverage + locality):
- **(ii) `header_to_metadata` `response_rules`** — the encode-side, response-header-driven companion to phase 34's `request_rules`. Thinner-looking but lower leverage: it is ANOTHER producer that exercises the same machinery and lights up no new vein, AND it actually needs NEW encode-side metadata-capture plumbing (phases 33/34 thread only the decode-side `req.dynamic_metadata` to the record). A future pure-additive increment once a consumer justifies richer producers.
- **(iii) jwt_authn `payload_in_metadata`** — would make the phase-22 jwt_authn filter write the JWT payload into dynamic metadata; another PRODUCER, crypto-heavy, and best landed AFTER a consumer exists to read varied metadata (it then becomes a strong jwt→rbac-metadata-principal showcase). A future phase.
- **(iv) `json_format`/`typed_json_format`** — a self-contained Observability LEAF reusing the phase-32 engine but exercising NONE of the consumer machinery and unlocking no filter-family follow-up. Lower leverage; its own future phase.
- **(v) Non-string metadata Values + nested-path `%DYNAMIC_METADATA(ns:key:sub)%`** — a Value-enum type-system increment (the phase-33/34 §2.2 deferral) touching the store type + the operator render for no new differential surface until a consumer needs typed/nested metadata; deferred (the rbac `metadata` MVP reads string values, single-segment path).

**Scope (minimum-viable, see SPEC §2).** IN: the RBAC `metadata` Permission + Principal condition (config: a `Metadata(MetadataMatcher)` variant on each enum + `MetadataMatcher`/`MetadataPathSegment`/`ValueMatcher` structs, single-segment path, `string_match`-only, `deny_unknown_fields`, a `ConfigError` disposition §6.2-disposed; runtime: the two runtime variants + eval arms + lowering arms; the decision matrix + local reply UNCHANGED); the store + producers + operator + decode threading REUSED UNCHANGED; fixture `0043` (`X-Tier: prod`→200 + `X-Tier: dev`/absent→403, ≥2 probes, byte-exact cross-proxy) + an in-process backstop (present-match / absent-namespace / absent-key / value-mismatch / and_rules-or_rules-not_rule compose / Principal / DENY-inversion / mid-chain producer→consumer thread) + a `parse_bootstrap` seed + a BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT extension. DEFERRED (each a §2.2 named future home): non-string `ValueMatcher` variants (null/double/bool/present/list/or_match — `present_match` the cheapest follow-up); multi-segment/nested `path`; `MetadataMatcher.invert`; the other not-yet-shipped RBAC condition types (IP/port/url_path/SNI/etc.); `shadow_rules`; per-route `typed_per_filter_config`; other producers/consumers (jwt_authn `payload_in_metadata`, ext_authz/ext_proc [gRPC-blocked]); `json_format`/`typed_json_format`/gRPC-ALS/OTLP/tracing/stats-sink/tap.

**§6.1 split** projected NOT to fire (~500–900 LoC / ~7–9 tasks — one matcher type on an EXISTING filter, ADDING NO infrastructure; comparable to `header_to_metadata`/`cdn_loop`/`csrf`); the natural seam if forced is `35.1` (the config schema + the two visitor arms + the runtime variant/eval/lowering — a foundation slice, no new fixture, proven by all 42 existing fixtures staying green) / `35.2` (fixture `0043` + BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT + fuzz/seed + close).

**Consequences.** `crates/envoy-config/` gains a `MetadataMatcher`/`MetadataPathSegment`/`ValueMatcher` trio + a `"metadata"` arm on the `Permission` and `Principal` `Deserialize` visitors (+ a `ConfigError` disposition §6.2-disposed); `crates/envoy-filter/src/rbac.rs` gains `RuntimePermission::Metadata`/`RuntimePrincipal::Metadata` + the eval/lowering arms; the RBAC decision matrix, local reply, stats, and pipeline are UNCHANGED; `crates/envoy-accesslog/` is UNCHANGED (the store + operator are reused verbatim, and even the fixture's `%DYNAMIC_METADATA%` log line is optional). NO new `HttpFilterInstance` variant, NO new crate, NO new dependency, NO new fuzz target projected (the existing `parse_bootstrap` covers the new config). `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` holds. The pick OPENS the metadata-consumer vein in the HTTP-filters family. **DECISIONS.md ledger head: ADR-0085** (this ADR; project-cumulative count 85; next-available **ADR-0086**). **ADR-0086** reserved (§6.2 reconciliation). **ADR-0014 REMAINS IN FORCE; ADR-0028 REMAINS OPEN; ADR-0049 governs** the config-validity all-fatal posture. The state-2 PLAN-write is the next session (`superpowers:writing-plans`), which runs the §6.2 reconnaissance and fires ADR-0086.

## ADR-0086: Phase-35 §6.2 empirical-verification reconciliation (run LOCALLY at the state-2 PLAN-write against `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` — an H1 `direct_response` listener + a `[header_to_metadata, rbac, router]` chain with an `action: ALLOW` single-policy `metadata` Permission/Principal, `curl` probes with/without `X-Tier`, bytes via `od -c`, config round-tripped through `/config_dump`, malformed variants via `--mode validate`) — THREE MATERIAL divergences from the SPEC projection (the `rbac.v3.Permission.metadata` / `Principal.metadata` fields are DEPRECATED-but-functional at the pin — a non-differential boot warning; a MULTI-SEGMENT `path` is ACCEPTED by Envoy, NOT boot-fatal — envoy-rust is stricter and rejects it; a NON-`string_match` `value` [e.g. `present_match`] is ACCEPTED by Envoy — envoy-rust's string-only `ValueMatcher` rejects it), plus the headline confirmations (the `metadata: { filter, path: [{ key }], value: { string_match } }` wire shape round-trips verbatim through `/config_dump`; accepted under BOTH `permissions` and `principals`; `filter`→namespace correspondence holds for the default `envoy.filters.http.header_to_metadata` AND a custom namespace; producer-before-consumer chain order REQUIRED; the full 04.x `StringMatcher` modes flow through; `X-Tier: prod`→`200`+`ok\n` / `dev`/absent/present-empty→`403`+`RBAC: access denied` 19B byte-exact; empty `filter` / empty `path` / missing `value` boot-fatal, ADR-0049) so the **STRONG differential target FIRES** (cross-proxy byte-identical `200`/`403`+body verdict for the in-scope metadata-driven decision); this ADR LOCKS the open SPEC §3 PLAN-write calls

**Status:** Accepted (phase-35 state-2 PLAN-write; `superpowers:writing-plans`). Reconciles SPEC §3 / §6.2 for phase `35-rbac-dynamic-metadata`. Supersedes nothing. Builds on ADR-0085 (the pick + scope) + ADR-0084 (the producer's default namespace) + ADR-0034 (the 19-byte `RBAC: access denied` body) + the phase-10 RBAC ground truth.

**Method.** Stood up live `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` (Docker, the ENVOY_TARGET pin `sha256:56da5afd…`) with an H1 `direct_response` listener whose `http_filters` chain is `[header_to_metadata, rbac, router]`: `header_to_metadata` extracts `x-tier`→`tier` (default namespace), RBAC has one `action: ALLOW` policy `tier_prod` whose Permission is `metadata: { filter: envoy.filters.http.header_to_metadata, path: [{ key: tier }], value: { string_match: { exact: prod } } }`. Drove `curl` probes (`X-Tier: prod` / `X-Tier: dev` / absent / present-but-empty `X-Tier;`); captured EXACT bytes with `od -c`; round-tripped the booted config via `GET /config_dump`; tested the Principal placement, a custom `metadata_namespace`, a reversed `[rbac, header_to_metadata]` chain, and a `prefix` StringMatcher with live request probes; tested malformed variants (empty/missing `filter`, empty `path: []`, multi-segment `path`, `present_match` value, missing `value`) via `--mode validate`; cleaned up all containers. The phase-33 store, the phase-34 `header_to_metadata` producer, the `%DYNAMIC_METADATA%` operator, and the decode-pipeline threading were NOT re-verified (reused unchanged; their byte form is the ADR-0081/ADR-0084 ground truth).

**LOCKED FACTS (the ground truth `PLAN.md §A` carries inline; the task encodings derive from these — do NOT re-derive):**
1. **Wire shape (§A1) — CONFIRMED.** A `metadata` Permission/Principal entry is `{ metadata: { filter: <string>, path: [{ key: <string> }, …], value: { string_match: <StringMatcher> } } }`. Field names `filter` / `path` / `key` / `value` / `string_match` round-trip VERBATIM through `/config_dump` (snake_case). Accepted under BOTH `permissions[]` and `principals[]` (identical shape; `prod`→200 / `dev`→403 under each placement). `value` is REQUIRED (missing → boot-fatal, §A4). MVP models `MetadataMatcher { filter: String, path: Vec<MetadataPathSegment{ key: String }>, value: ValueMatcher }` + a string-only `ValueMatcher` enum (only variant `StringMatch(StringMatcher)`, reusing the 04.x `StringMatcher` verbatim), all `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`; the `Permission`/`Principal` hand-rolled visitors each gain a `"metadata"` arm.
2. **`filter`→namespace correspondence (§A2) — CONFIRMED.** `MetadataMatcher.filter` is matched against the dynamic-metadata namespace key (the store's outer `BTreeMap` key). The phase-34 default producer namespace `envoy.filters.http.header_to_metadata` (ADR-0084) is matchable; a custom `metadata_namespace` (tested `my.custom.ns`) is matchable by an equal `filter`. **Producer-before-consumer chain order is REQUIRED:** a reversed `[rbac, header_to_metadata, router]` chain evaluates RBAC against EMPTY metadata → `X-Tier: prod` gets `403` (no match under ALLOW). Fixture 0043 MUST order `[header_to_metadata, rbac, router]`.
3. **Match semantics + verdicts (§A3) — CONFIRMED byte-exact (= phase-10/ADR-0034 ground truth).** `X-Tier: prod` → store `tier=prod` → match → ALLOW → `200` + `ok\n` (3 bytes, the `direct_response` body). `X-Tier: dev` → `tier=dev` → no match → DENY → `403` + `RBAC: access denied` (19 bytes, no trailing newline, `od -c` confirmed). Absent header → key UNSET → no match → `403`+19B. Present-but-empty header (`X-Tier;`) → `header_to_metadata` writes nothing (§A4 phase-34) → key UNSET → no match → `403`+19B. **StringMatcher modes:** the FULL 04.x set flows through (`exact` AND `prefix` both confirmed live: `prefix: pro` → `prod` 200 / `dev` 403) — REUSE the `StringMatcher` verbatim, do NOT restrict the MVP to `exact`. Runtime eval: `req.dynamic_metadata.get(&m.filter).and_then(|ns| ns.get(&m.path[0].key)).is_some_and(|v| m.value.matches(v))` (absent namespace OR absent key → `false`).
4. **Config-validity (§A4) — CONFIRMED boot-fatal where Envoy rejects (exit 1, ADR-0049):** empty `filter: ""` → `MetadataMatcherValidationError.Filter: value length must be at least 1 characters`; missing `filter` → same; empty `path: []` → `MetadataMatcherValidationError.Path: value must contain at least 1 item(s)`; missing `value` → `MetadataMatcherValidationError.Value: value is required`. envoy-rust matches via ONE new `ConfigError::RbacMetadataMatcherInvalid { listener, policy_name, path, detail }` (empty `filter` + the §A5 multi-segment-path reject, checked in the `validate_permission_tree`/`validate_principal_tree` `Metadata` arm) + serde (`value` is a required non-`Option` field → missing → serde error; `deny_unknown_fields` on the structs).
5. **MATERIAL DIVERGENCE — multi-segment `path` (§A5).** Envoy ACCEPTS a multi-segment `path: [{ key: tier }, { key: sub }]` (SPEC projected boot-fatal). The flat string-only store (`BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>`) cannot resolve a nested path, so envoy-rust MVP is **STRICTER**: a `path` whose length ≠ 1 is BOOT-FATAL (`ConfigError::RbacMetadataMatcherInvalid`, detail `"metadata matcher path must have exactly one segment"`) — a documented stricter-than-Envoy divergence (the phase-34 `cookie`/typed-values precedent). The nested path is the §2.2 deferral (rides the future structured-Value generalization).
6. **MATERIAL DIVERGENCE — non-`string_match` `value` (§A6).** Envoy ACCEPTS the full `ValueMatcher` oneof (`present_match`, `null_match`, `double_match`, `bool_match`, `list_match`, `or_match`) — tested `present_match: true` → accepted. The string-only MVP `ValueMatcher` rejects any non-`string_match` key BOOT-FATAL via its hand-rolled "exactly one key" visitor (`unknown_field` → serde error) — a documented stricter-than-Envoy divergence (the phase-34 non-`STRING` `type` precedent). `present_match` is the cheapest §2.2 additive follow-up.
7. **MATERIAL DIVERGENCE — deprecation (§A7).** `envoy.config.rbac.v3.Permission.metadata` AND `.Principal.metadata` are DEPRECATED in v1.33.0 — Envoy boots with a `warning` ("Using deprecated option … will be removed from Envoy soon") but the fields are FULLY FUNCTIONAL and accepted at the pin (both verdicts correct). The warning is stderr-only → **NON-DIFFERENTIAL** (no response / access-log / stats impact; envoy-rust simply does not emit it). Disposition: land the matcher as-is at the pin; flag for the future pin-refresh phase (D-3.7) that a later Envoy may remove the field (the modern replacement is the unified `matcher`/CEL condition, out of scope).

**Disposition of the SPEC §3 open PLAN-write calls (now LOCKED in `PLAN.md §A`):** §3.1 → the `metadata: { filter, path: [{ key }], value: { string_match } }` wire shape, `value` required, accepted under both `permissions`/`principals`; §3.2 → `filter`=namespace, default `envoy.filters.http.header_to_metadata` + custom both matchable, producer-before-consumer REQUIRED; §3.3 → full StringMatcher modes (NOT exact-only), absent ns/key → no match, `200`/`403`+19B byte-exact; §3.4 → boot-fatal, ONE new `ConfigError::RbacMetadataMatcherInvalid` (empty `filter` + path-length≠1) + serde (`value` required + `deny_unknown_fields` rejects non-`string_match` value); §3.5 → fixture 0043 `direct_response` + `header_to_metadata` producer + `action: ALLOW` single-policy metadata Permission + `X-Tier: prod`→200 / `dev`→403 ≥2 probes (the optional `%DYNAMIC_METADATA%` `log_format` is dropped — the `200`/`403`+body differential is self-sufficient, NOT added); §3.6 → reuse the fixture-`0017` status+body comparator + the `extra_headers` probe; §3.7 → existing `parse_bootstrap` covers it, NO new target + a seed; §3.8 → split NOT fired (~8 tasks).

**Material divergences from the SPEC:** THREE — (i) multi-segment `path` accepted by Envoy → envoy-rust stricter (boot-fatal); (ii) non-`string_match` `value` accepted by Envoy → envoy-rust stricter (boot-fatal); (iii) the `metadata` Permission/Principal fields are deprecated-but-functional (non-differential). All three are encoded in `PLAN.md §A` (A5/A6/A7) and the Task code. None changes the §6.1 split projection (still NOT fired, ~8 tasks) nor the strong differential target (still FIRES — the in-scope fixture config exercises none of the divergent surfaces).

**Consequences.** `PLAN.md` lands with these facts inline (no `[§6.2-PENDING]`) + ~8 TDD tasks (config schema trio + the two visitor `"metadata"` arms / validator + `ConfigError::RbacMetadataMatcherInvalid` / runtime variants + eval + lowering / in-process backstop / fixture 0043 / `parse_bootstrap` seed / BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT extension). The `envoy-accesslog` crate is UNTOUCHED (store + operator + producer reused verbatim). No new `HttpFilterInstance` variant, no new crate, no new dependency, no new fuzz target. `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` holds. **DECISIONS.md ledger head: ADR-0086** (this ADR; project-cumulative count 86; next-available **ADR-0087**). **ADR-0014 REMAINS IN FORCE; ADR-0028 REMAINS OPEN; ADR-0049 governs** the config-validity all-fatal posture. The state-3 implementation is the next session (`superpowers:subagent-driven-development`).

## ADR-0087: Phase-36 pick + scope — **enrich the RBAC matcher VALUE surface**, extending the dynamic-metadata-consumer vein phase 35 just opened and folding the freshest carry-forward (M35-1): (F1) add the **`present_match` `ValueMatcher` variant** to the phase-35 RBAC `metadata` Permission/Principal condition (match on KEY PRESENCE, not value content — ADR-0086 §A6 named it "the cheapest §2.2 additive follow-up" and empirically confirmed Envoy accepts it) + (F2) compile **`safe_regex` `StringMatcher` on the RBAC path (BOTH `header` and `metadata` values)** at `rbac.rs` lowering time, **closing carry-forward M35-1** — a LATENT RUNTIME PANIC where `StringMatcher::matches` (`crates/envoy-config/src/matcher.rs:90`) does `sr.compiled.as_ref().expect(...)` but the immutable-borrow RBAC validation path never compiled `SafeRegex::compiled` (the documented NOTE at `crates/envoy-config/src/bootstrap.rs:4040-4044`), so a `safe_regex` value in ANY RBAC matcher panics on the first matching request (fixture 0043 used `exact`, so it never fired) + fixture `0044` — a byte-exact, DETERMINISTIC, LOCALLY-observable differential (the probe controls the request header → the metadata value → the RBAC verdict, so `200`+`direct_response`-body vs `403`+`RBAC: access denied` 19B is byte-identical cross-proxy); the **thin reuse-slice MVP** (NO new `HttpFilterInstance` variant, NO new infrastructure — reuses the phase-10 RBAC engine + decision matrix + local reply, the 04.x `StringMatcher`/`SafeRegex` + the `regex` foundation (ADR-0021), the phase-33 store, the phase-34 `header_to_metadata` producer, and the decode-pipeline shared-`&mut FilterRequest` threading UNCHANGED); choose this RBAC matcher-value enrichment over the rejected alternatives below

**Status:** Accepted (phase-36 state-1 brainstorm; `superpowers:brainstorming`). Locks the pick + minimum-viable scope for phase `36-rbac-matcher-value-enrichment`. Supersedes nothing. Builds on ADR-0085/0086 (the phase-35 pick + the §6.2 ground truth — §A6 confirmed `present_match` is Envoy-accepted; the M35-1 SafeRegex limitation note), ADR-0034 (the 19-byte `RBAC: access denied` body), ADR-0021 (`regex` permitted foundation), ADR-0084 (the producer's default namespace), ADR-0049 (config-validity all-fatal).

**Context.** Phase 35 closed the dynamic-metadata produce→consume loop with the FIRST consumer — the RBAC `metadata` condition — but its MVP supported exactly ONE `ValueMatcher` variant (`string_match`) and left two threads dangling: (1) `present_match` (ADR-0086 §A6 named it the cheapest follow-up), and (2) M35-1 — `safe_regex` is config-accepted on the RBAC path but NOT compiled (the RBAC validator is an immutable borrow), so it would PANIC at runtime. ROADMAP rows `00`–`35` are all `done`; `35` was the highest defined row; the next family headings (`Runtime + hot restart`, `WASM host`, `Deprecated/edge`) are headings-only with no concrete pending row → this is a free new-phase pick. The standing instruction (next-prompt §11 / STATE.md `## Next expected skill`) is to fold carry-forward Minors into whichever surface the next phase touches; M35-1's fix home IS this surface.

**Options considered (the pick rationale + rejected alternatives):**
- **(CHOSEN) RBAC matcher-value enrichment — `present_match` (F1) + RBAC `safe_regex` compilation / M35-1 (F2).** Cheapest-strong pick that EXTENDS the just-opened metadata-consumer vein AND folds the freshest carry-forward. Two byte-exact, deterministic, locally-observable differentials; NO new crate/dependency/`HttpFilterInstance` variant. F2 additionally closes a real latent PANIC (correctness, not just a feature) and covers BOTH RBAC matcher families that carry a `SafeRegex` (header + metadata). ~400–800 LoC / ~6–9 tasks.
- **(rejected) `json_format` / `typed_json_format` access log** — a self-contained Observability leaf that reuses the phase-32 command-operator engine, but BIGGER (~700–1100 LoC), carries a real §6.2 risk (JSON key-ordering + numeric-vs-string typing must match Envoy byte-for-byte), opens no filter-family follow-up, and folds NO carry-forward. A fine FUTURE Observability pick; not the cheapest-strong increment now.
- **(rejected) other not-yet-shipped RBAC condition types** (source/destination IP & port, URL path, SNI, requested-server-name) — each needs new request-context plumbing (connection addresses / SNI) NOT yet on `FilterRequest`, and none continues the metadata vein; deferred (phase-10 deferrals).
- **(rejected) jwt_authn `payload_in_metadata`** — another metadata PRODUCER (would feed an RBAC `metadata` principal with JWT claims), not a consumer increment; a natural strong follow-up once it exists, but it lights up no NEW consumer capability this phase and adds producer plumbing.
- **(rejected) the remaining non-string `ValueMatcher` variants** (`null_match`/`double_match`/`bool_match`/`list_match`/`or_match`) — a type-system increment requiring the shared non-string-Value generalization of the flat string-only store; best deferred until a consumer needs a typed value. `present_match` is carved out as the ONLY non-`string_match` variant this phase because it needs NO typed value (just presence).

**Decision.** Land F1 + F2 as a single phase `36-rbac-matcher-value-enrichment` per the SPEC at `docs/envoy-rust/phases/36-rbac-matcher-value-enrichment/SPEC.md`. F1: a `PresentMatch(bool)` variant on the `ValueMatcher` enum (config `Deserialize`/`Serialize` + `KEYS`) + an `eval_metadata` restructure so presence is compared against the bool (`present_match` CANNOT route through `ValueMatcher::matches(value: &str)`, which only runs when a value is present). F2: compile every RBAC-reachable `SafeRegex` into `SafeRegex::compiled` at `rbac.rs` lowering (`lower_permission`/`lower_principal`), mirroring the route-config `validate_header_matcher` compiler, covering the `Header` `safe_regex_match` AND the `metadata` `string_match.safe_regex`; a malformed RBAC regex becomes boot-fatal (not a first-request panic). Fixture `0044` exercises both with probe pairs (present/absent for F1; regex-match/miss for F2); the in-process backstop carries the richer cases incl. a panic-regression guard for the header-`safe_regex_match` path. Minimum-viable per §2 — defers the remaining non-string Values, multi-segment/nested path (`path.len() == 1` validator UNCHANGED), `MetadataMatcher.invert`, the other RBAC condition types, `shadow_rules`, per-route `typed_per_filter_config`, and the rest of the Observability family.

**Rationale.** It is the cheapest pick that simultaneously (a) extends the freshly-opened metadata-consumer vein, (b) folds the freshest carry-forward M35-1 — a latent panic with a clean fix home exactly on this surface, (c) adds `present_match`, the ADR-0086-confirmed Envoy-accepted cheapest follow-up, (d) is byte-exact + deterministic + locally observable, (e) needs no new crate/dependency/`HttpFilterInstance` variant, reusing the entire RBAC engine + the fixture-0043 harness. Two strong differentials + a closed latent panic for ~6–9 tasks.

**Consequences.** The state-2 PLAN-write (`superpowers:writing-plans`) runs the §6.2 LOCAL reconnaissance against live `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` (the `present_match` wire shape/semantics incl. present-empty + `present_match: false`; the `safe_regex` RBAC verdicts + regex-dialect parity; the non-string-Value config-validity dispositions) and fires **ADR-0088** (reserved) with the locked facts. **ADR-0089 is reserved** for the §6.1 split (projected NOT to fire). The new ROADMAP row `36` lands `in-progress` (depends-on `06 07 10 33 34 35`). M35-1 is scheduled CONSUMED at phase-36 close; the older carry-forwards (M34-1/M34-2/M34-3 + M33-1/M33-2 + the empty-`metadata_match`→fallback doc-comment + M29-1/M29-2 + M30-1/M30-2 + the phase-31 cosmetics + the HTTP-filters-family (1)-(4)) remain live. No code changes this state-1 session (SPEC + ADR + ROADMAP + STATE only). `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` holds; no new crate/dependency/fuzz-target/`HttpFilterInstance` variant projected. **DECISIONS.md ledger head: ADR-0087** (this ADR; project-cumulative count 87; next-available **ADR-0088**, reserved for the §6.2 reconciliation). **ADR-0014 REMAINS IN FORCE; ADR-0028 REMAINS OPEN; ADR-0049 governs** the config-validity all-fatal posture. The state-2 PLAN-write is the next session.

## ADR-0088: Phase-36 §6.2 empirical-verification reconciliation (run LOCALLY at the state-2 PLAN-write against `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` — an H1 `direct_response` listener + a `[header_to_metadata, rbac, router]` chain, `action: ALLOW` single-policy `metadata`/`header` matchers, `curl` probes with/without/empty `X-Tier`, bytes via `od -c`, config round-tripped through `/config_dump`, malformed + non-string-`Value` variants via `--mode validate`) — TWO MATERIAL divergences from the SPEC projection (the `present_match` semantics are **`match = key_present && want`** — `present_match: false` NEVER matches — NOT the SPEC's projected `present == want` and NOT the divergent `HeaderMatcherMode::PresentMatch` `want ? present : true` precedent; Envoy `safe_regex` is **RE2 FULL match (anchored)** whereas envoy-rust's `StringMatcher::matches` SafeRegex uses `regex::is_match` = PARTIAL, a pre-existing cross-cutting gap masked by anchored fixtures → the fixture-0044 pattern is LOCKED anchored so partial==full, and the unanchored partial-vs-full gap is recorded as new carry-forward **M36-1**, explicitly OUT of phase-36 scope), plus the headline confirmations (`present_match: true`/`false` BOTH accepted + round-trip verbatim through `/config_dump`; `present_match: true` ALLOWS any present `X-Tier` → `200`+`ok\n` / DENIES absent+present-empty → `403`+`RBAC: access denied` 19B; present-but-empty header → metadata UNSET → absent, consistent with ADR-0084; a `safe_regex` value on the `metadata` `string_match` AND on a `Permission::Header` `safe_regex_match` behave IDENTICALLY byte-exact; the non-`string_match` oneof keys `null_match`/`bool_match`/`double_match`/`or_match`/`list_match` accepted by Envoy → envoy-rust stays STRICTER boot-fatal; a malformed RBAC `safe_regex` pattern BOOT-FATAL on Envoy, ADR-0049) so the **STRONG differential target FIRES** (cross-proxy byte-identical `200`/`403`+body verdict for both F1 `present_match` and F2 `safe_regex`); this ADR LOCKS the open SPEC §3 PLAN-write calls

**Status:** Accepted (phase-36 state-2 PLAN-write; `superpowers:writing-plans`). Reconciles SPEC §3 / §6.2 for phase `36-rbac-matcher-value-enrichment`. Supersedes nothing. Builds on ADR-0087 (the pick + scope), ADR-0086 (§A6 `present_match` Envoy-accepted; the §A3 verdict ground truth + producer chain order), ADR-0084 (present-but-empty header → metadata unset; the default producer namespace), ADR-0034 (the 19-byte `RBAC: access denied` body), ADR-0021 (`regex` permitted foundation), ADR-0049 (config-validity all-fatal).

**Method.** Stood up live `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` (Docker, the ENVOY_TARGET pin `sha256:56da5afd…`) with an H1 `direct_response` (200 `ok\n`) listener whose `http_filters` chain is `[header_to_metadata, rbac, router]`: `header_to_metadata` extracts `x-tier`→`tier` (default namespace `envoy.filters.http.header_to_metadata`). Ran 9 RBAC `rules:` variants — runtime probes (port-mapped `curl`, `od -c` on the body) for `present_match: true`, `present_match: false`, a `metadata` `string_match.safe_regex` (`prod|staging`), a `Permission::Header` `safe_regex_match` (`prod|staging`); `--mode validate` for `null_match`/`bool_match`/`double_match`/`or_match` and a malformed `safe_regex` (`(`); anchoring-boundary probes (`staging-2`/`xstaging`/`production`) to determine full-vs-partial; `/config_dump` round-trip for `present_match`. All containers cleaned up. The phase-33 store, the phase-34 producer, the decode-pipeline threading, and the phase-10 RBAC decision matrix / local reply were NOT re-verified (reused unchanged; their byte form is the ADR-0034/0084/0086 ground truth).

**LOCKED FACTS (the ground truth `PLAN.md §A` carries inline; the task encodings derive from these — do NOT re-derive):**
1. **F1 `present_match` semantics (§A1) — MATERIAL DIVERGENCE.** Empirical truth table (`present` = the `filter:key` resolves to a stored value): `(want=true, present=true) → MATCH`; `(want=true, present=false) → NO match`; `(want=false, present=true) → NO match`; `(want=false, present=false) → NO match`. ⇒ **`match = present && want`**. `present_match: false` NEVER matches (a degenerate-but-Envoy-faithful config). This DIVERGES from the SPEC §2.1.2 projection (`present == want`, which would match-when-absent for `want=false`) AND from the existing `HeaderMatcherMode::PresentMatch` (`matcher.rs:42-47`, `want ? value.is_some() : true` — always-true for `want=false`). The new `ValueMatcher::PresentMatch(want)` MUST implement `present && want`, NOT copy the header precedent (the SPEC §2.1.2 / spec-review I-1 foot-gun, now resolved empirically).
2. **F1 present-empty + verdicts (§A2) — CONFIRMED byte-exact.** `present_match: true`: any non-empty `X-Tier` → `tier` stored → present → `200` + `ok\n` (3 bytes); `X-Tier;` (present-but-empty) → `header_to_metadata` writes nothing (ADR-0084) → key UNSET → present=false → `403` + `RBAC: access denied` (19 bytes, no newline, `od -c`); absent `X-Tier` → `403`+19B. So present-but-empty is treated as ABSENT (the SPEC's "may be moot" projection CONFIRMED). `/config_dump` round-trips `"present_match": true` verbatim (snake_case).
3. **F2 `safe_regex` verdicts (§A3) — CONFIRMED byte-exact; the metadata + header paths are IDENTICAL.** With pattern `prod|staging`: `staging`/`prod` → `200`+`ok\n`; `dev` → `403`+19B; present-empty/absent → `403`+19B. A `safe_regex` value on the `metadata` `string_match` AND on a `Permission::Header` `safe_regex_match` produced byte-identical verdicts. F2 must compile BOTH paths.
4. **F2 anchoring (§A3b) — MATERIAL DIVERGENCE (cross-cutting, pre-existing).** Envoy `safe_regex` is **RE2 FULL match (anchored)**: with `prod|staging`, `staging-2`/`xstaging`/`production` → `403` (NO match — the whole string must match). envoy-rust's `StringMatcher::matches` SafeRegex (`matcher.rs:87-91`) uses `regex::Regex::is_match` = **PARTIAL** (substring), so `is_match("prod|staging", "staging-2") == true` — a DIVERGENCE for UNANCHORED patterns. This is PRE-EXISTING (phase 04.2) and cross-cutting (the route-config header `safe_regex` shares the code path), masked because every existing fixture uses an anchored pattern (`^v[0-9]+$`). **Disposition:** fixture 0044 + every phase-36 backstop LOCK an ANCHORED pattern (`^(prod|staging)$` — Envoy accepts the redundant anchors; envoy-rust `is_match` of an `^…$` pattern is whole-string-equivalent), so partial==full and the differential is byte-identical WITHOUT a SafeRegex-semantics change. The unanchored partial-vs-full gap is **new carry-forward M36-1** — explicitly OUT of phase-36 scope (it is NOT RBAC-specific; a proper full-match fix touches the shared route-config SafeRegex and warrants its own phase). NOTE: this is DISTINCT from M35-1 (the latent panic), which F2 DOES close.
5. **F2 mechanism + malformed-regex disposition (§A4) — boot-fatal, ADR-0049.** A malformed RBAC `safe_regex` (`(`) is BOOT-FATAL on Envoy (`--mode validate` exit 1, "missing ): ("). envoy-rust must reject at BOOT, not at first-request panic. **Mechanism (the SPEC §3.4 call, LOCKED):** compile every RBAC-reachable `SafeRegex` at `rbac.rs` lowering time on the owned clone, making `lower_permission`/`lower_principal` **fallible** (`-> Result<_, FilterError>`) and threading the `Result` up to the already-fallible `RbacFilter::build_from_config` → `FilterPipeline::build_from_config`, which runs at listener-build (server startup) → a returned `Err` fails the boot. Expose a focused public envoy-config compile helper (e.g. `HeaderMatcher::compile_safe_regexes(&mut self) -> Result<(), ConfigError>` + `ValueMatcher::compile_safe_regexes(&mut self) -> Result<(), ConfigError>`, reusing the existing private `compile_safe_regex(&mut SafeRegex)` and `ConfigError::InvalidRegex`); `lower_*` clone the matcher, call the helper, map `ConfigError::InvalidRegex → FilterError::InvalidConfig`. A naïve in-`lower` `Regex::new().unwrap()` is NOT acceptable (re-introduces a boot panic). REJECTED alternative: making the immutable RBAC config-validation path (`validate_http_filters` → `validate_rbac_config` → tree validators) mutable to compile at parse time — too invasive (the whole `&[HttpFilter]` validation chain up to the bootstrap would become `&mut`); the lowering-time compile is the SPEC's named M35-1 fix home and surgical. (Boot-fatal at pipeline-build is a slightly later boot STAGE than the route walk's parse-time rejection, but both are pre-traffic startup → differentially both proxies fail to boot → equivalent.)
6. **Config-validity for non-`string_match`/`present_match` keys (§A5) — CONFIRMED stricter.** Envoy ACCEPTS `null_match`/`bool_match`/`double_match`/`or_match`/`list_match` (the full `ValueMatcher` oneof). envoy-rust ADDS ONLY `present_match` to the hand-rolled "exactly one key" `ValueMatcher` visitor (`KEYS = ["string_match", "present_match"]`); every other oneof key stays `unknown_field` → BOOT-FATAL (the ADR-0086 §A6 stricter-than-Envoy posture, unchanged). The existing in-code test `rbac_metadata_rejects_present_match_value` (`bootstrap.rs:12186`), which today asserts `present_match` is REJECTED, MUST be FLIPPED by F1 to assert ACCEPTANCE (a second test to repurpose, alongside the SPEC-named M-1 `rbac_metadata_value_safe_regex_is_parse_accepted` at `bootstrap.rs:~12514`).

**Disposition of the SPEC §3 open PLAN-write calls (now LOCKED in `PLAN.md §A`):** §3.1 → `value: { present_match: true|false }` accepted inside the RBAC `metadata` condition, round-trips verbatim; §3.2 → semantics `present && want` (`false` never matches), present-empty→absent, `200`+`ok\n` / `403`+19B byte-exact; §3.3 → `safe_regex` on `metadata` AND `Permission::Header` identical, anchored pattern `^(prod|staging)$` for portable full==partial parity; §3.4 → other oneof keys boot-fatal (stricter), malformed RBAC `safe_regex` boot-fatal via the fallible-lowering mechanism (§A4/§A5 above), reuse `ConfigError::InvalidRegex` + `FilterError::InvalidConfig` (NO new error variant); §3.5 → fixture 0044 = `direct_response` + `header_to_metadata` producer + ONE `action: ALLOW` policy per probe family; F1 present/absent probe pair + F2 regex-match/miss probe pair; the header-`safe_regex_match` case lives in the in-process BACKSTOP (the panic-regression guard) — the fixture's F2 uses the `metadata` value to keep metadata-vein continuity; no `%DYNAMIC_METADATA%` log line; §3.6 → reuse the fixture-`0017`/`0043` status+body comparator + the `extra_headers` probe (no new comparator); §3.7 → existing `parse_bootstrap` covers it, NO new fuzz target + 2 seeds (`present_match` + RBAC `safe_regex`); §3.8 → split NOT fired (~8 tasks).

**Material divergences from the SPEC:** TWO — (i) `present_match` semantics `present && want` (NOT `present == want`); `present_match: false` never matches — F1 implements `present && want`; (ii) Envoy `safe_regex` = RE2 full match vs envoy-rust `is_match` partial — fixture LOCKS anchored patterns so the differential is byte-identical, the unanchored gap deferred as M36-1. Both are encoded in `PLAN.md §A` and the Task code. Neither changes the §6.1 split projection (still NOT fired, ~8 tasks) nor the strong differential target (still FIRES — the fixture exercises only the byte-identical surfaces).

**Consequences.** `PLAN.md` lands with these facts inline (no `[§6.2-PENDING]`) + ~8 TDD tasks (F1 config `present_match` variant + visitor/serializer/`KEYS` + flip `rbac_metadata_rejects_present_match_value` / F1 `eval_metadata` presence restructure `present && want` / F2 public compile helper + fallible `lower_*` + `build_from_config` thread + repurpose `rbac_metadata_value_safe_regex_is_parse_accepted` / in-process backstop incl. the header-`safe_regex` panic-regression guard + `present_match: false` never-matches + composition/Principal/DENY / fixture 0044 (F1 + F2 metadata probe pairs) / `parse_bootstrap` seeds / BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT "Phase 36" extension). `crates/envoy-config` gains the `present_match` `ValueMatcher` arm + the public compile helper; `crates/envoy-filter/src/rbac.rs` gains the presence-aware `eval_metadata` + fallible lowering with SafeRegex compilation; the RBAC decision matrix, local reply, stats, store, producers, and pipeline are UNCHANGED. No new `HttpFilterInstance` variant, no new crate, no new dependency, no new fuzz target, no new `ConfigError`/`FilterError` variant. `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` holds. Carry-forward **M35-1 is CONSUMED** by F2 (the panic is fixed + guarded); **M36-1 is NEW** (unanchored SafeRegex partial-vs-full, deferred). **DECISIONS.md ledger head: ADR-0088** (this ADR; project-cumulative count 88; next-available **ADR-0089**, reserved for the §6.1 split — projected NOT to fire). **ADR-0014 REMAINS IN FORCE; ADR-0028 REMAINS OPEN; ADR-0049 governs** the config-validity all-fatal posture. The state-3 implementation is the next session (`superpowers:subagent-driven-development`).

## ADR-0089: Phase-37 pick + scope — **widen the RBAC condition-TYPE surface** with the `url_path` Permission/Principal condition (Envoy's `type.matcher.v3.PathMatcher` — `url_path: { path: { <StringMatcher> } }` — matching the request path with the `?query` stripped) on the EXISTING phase-10 `envoy.filters.http.rbac` filter + fixture `0045` — a byte-exact, DETERMINISTIC, LOCALLY-observable differential (the probe controls the request-line path → the RBAC verdict, so `200`+`direct_response`-body vs `403`+`RBAC: access denied` 19B is byte-identical cross-proxy; the query-strip semantic is the load-bearing distinction — a `/allowed?x=1` probe matches `url_path: { exact: "/allowed" }` because Envoy strips the query, whereas envoy-rust's existing route matcher compares the raw request-target byte-for-byte); the **thin reuse-slice MVP** (NO new `HttpFilterInstance` variant, NO new infrastructure, NO metadata store, NO producer chain — reuses the phase-10 RBAC engine + decision matrix + local reply, the 04.x `StringMatcher`/`SafeRegex` + the `regex` foundation (ADR-0021), and the phase-36 compile-RBAC-SafeRegex-at-lowering fallible-lowering path UNCHANGED); choose `url_path` over the rejected alternatives below

**Status:** Accepted (phase-37 state-1 brainstorm; `superpowers:brainstorming`). Locks the pick + minimum-viable scope for phase `37-rbac-url-path-condition`. Supersedes nothing. Builds on ADR-0087/0088 (the phase-36 pick + the §6.2 ground truth — the M35-1 SafeRegex fix at `rbac.rs` fallible lowering, and the new carry-forward M36-1 unanchored-SafeRegex partial-vs-full gap this phase weighs but does NOT consume), ADR-0034 (the 19-byte `RBAC: access denied` body), ADR-0021 (`regex` permitted foundation), ADR-0049 (config-validity all-fatal).

**Context.** Phases 35/36 deepened the RBAC matcher-VALUE axis (the `metadata` condition; then `present_match` + `safe_regex` on it). The phase-10 RBAC filter supports the condition TYPES `any`/`header`/`and_*`/`or_*`/`not_*`/`metadata` on both `Permission` and `Principal` (`crates/envoy-config/src/bootstrap.rs:1409-1504`). Envoy's RBAC also has `url_path`, `destination_ip`/`destination_port`, `source_ip`/`direct_remote_ip`/`remote_ip`, and `requested_server_name`/SNI — all named phase-10/35/36 deferrals. ROADMAP rows `00`–`36` are all `done`; `36` was the highest defined row; the remaining family headings (`Runtime + hot restart`, `WASM host`, `Deprecated/edge`) are headings-only with no concrete pending row → this is a free new-phase pick. The standing instruction is to fold carry-forward Minors into whichever surface the next phase touches; `url_path`'s SafeRegex shares the M36-1 surface (weighed, anchored-locked, NOT consumed — folding M36-1 would touch the cross-cutting route-config SafeRegex path).

**Options considered (the pick rationale + rejected alternatives):**
- **(CHOSEN) the `url_path` RBAC condition type.** The ONLY not-yet-shipped RBAC condition that reads a request attribute the filter ALREADY holds — `FilterRequest.path` (`crates/envoy-filter/src/types.rs:28-30`) — so it needs NO new connection-context plumbing. Byte-exact + deterministic + locally observable; genuine differential richness via the query-strip semantic (not a thin `:path`-header alias); reuses the entire RBAC engine + the 04.x `StringMatcher` + the phase-36 SafeRegex-at-lowering fix; NO new crate/dependency/`HttpFilterInstance` variant/metadata store/producer chain. ~350–700 LoC / ~6–9 tasks — the cheapest-strong leaf.
- **(rejected) the connection-context RBAC conditions** — `destination_ip`/`destination_port` (Permission), `source_ip`/`direct_remote_ip`/`remote_ip` (Principal), `requested_server_name`/SNI (Permission). Each needs the downstream socket address (and, for SNI, the TLS handshake server-name) threaded into the filter — infrastructure `FilterRequest` does NOT carry today. Their own future RBAC-condition phase(s) once a connection-context plumbing slice lands; `url_path` is chosen precisely because it alone needs none of this.
- **(rejected) the remaining non-string `ValueMatcher` variants** (`null_match`/`double_match`/`bool_match`/`list_match`/`or_match`) + multi-segment metadata `path` + `MetadataMatcher.invert` — the matcher-VALUE axis the non-string-Value generalization gates (the flat string-only store has no typed values); best deferred until a consumer needs a typed value. This phase widens the orthogonal condition-TYPE axis instead.
- **(rejected) jwt_authn `payload_in_metadata`** — a metadata PRODUCER (would feed an RBAC `metadata` principal with JWT claims), not a condition-type increment; a natural strong follow-up but it adds producer plumbing and JWT claims are non-string (riding the deferred non-string-Value generalization).
- **(rejected) `json_format` / `typed_json_format` access log** — a self-contained Observability leaf reusing the phase-32 engine, but bigger (~700–1100 LoC) with a real §6.2 JSON key-ordering/typing risk and no filter-family continuity. A fine FUTURE Observability pick; not the cheapest-strong increment now.

**Decision.** Land `url_path` as a single phase `37-rbac-url-path-condition` per the SPEC at `docs/envoy-rust/phases/37-rbac-url-path-condition/SPEC.md`. Add a `UrlPath(PathMatcher)` variant to BOTH the `Permission` and `Principal` enums (config `Deserialize`/`Serialize` + `KEYS`), a thin `PathMatcher { path: StringMatcher }` config struct, the two runtime `eval` arms (resolve the query-stripped `req.path`, then `StringMatcher::matches`), the two `lower` arms (reusing the phase-36 fallible SafeRegex-at-lowering compile so a `safe_regex` `url_path` value is boot-fatal on a bad pattern, not a first-request panic), and the query-strip helper. Fixture `0045` exercises match / miss / query-strip (the query-bearing probe is the load-bearing cross-proxy witness); the in-process backstop carries the richer cases (Principal, composition, DENY-inversion, an anchored `safe_regex` `url_path`, malformed-regex/empty-`PathMatcher` boot-fatal). Minimum-viable per §2 — defers the connection-context conditions, path-normalization beyond query-strip, the non-string-Value/metadata-vein items, `shadow_rules`, per-route `typed_per_filter_config`, and the rest of the Observability family.

**Rationale.** It is the cheapest pick that (a) broadens the RBAC condition-TYPE surface (the first request-attribute condition beyond `header`), (b) needs ZERO new infrastructure (reads `req.path`, the one not-yet-shipped condition that does), (c) is byte-exact + deterministic + locally observable with genuine differential richness (the query-strip distinction), (d) reuses the entire RBAC engine + the 04.x `StringMatcher` + the fixture-0017/0043/0044 harness + the phase-36 SafeRegex-at-lowering fix, (e) needs no new crate/dependency/`HttpFilterInstance` variant. One strong differential for ~6–9 tasks.

**Consequences.** The state-2 PLAN-write (`superpowers:writing-plans`) runs the §6.2 LOCAL reconnaissance against live `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` (the `url_path`/`PathMatcher` wire shape + `Principal`-`url_path` acceptance; THE key risk — the EXACT path Envoy matches against: query-strip only vs also fragment-strip / percent-decode / path-normalization, swept via `/allowed?x=1`, `/allowed#frag`, `/al%6Cowed`, `/allowed/../allowed`, `//allowed`, `/allowed/`; the `safe_regex` `url_path` verdicts with an anchored portable pattern; the config-validity dispositions) and fires **ADR-0090** (reserved) with the locked facts. **ADR-0091 is reserved** for the §6.1 split (projected NOT to fire). The new ROADMAP row `37` lands `in-progress` (depends-on `06 07 10`). Carry-forward **M36-1** (unanchored SafeRegex partial-vs-full) is weighed but NOT consumed (the fixture/backstop lock anchored patterns; the cross-cutting full-match fix stays deferred); the older carry-forwards (M36-2/M36-3 + M34-1/M34-2/M34-3 + M33-1/M33-2 + the empty-`metadata_match`→fallback doc-comment + M29-1/M29-2 + M30-1/M30-2 + the phase-31 cosmetics + the HTTP-filters-family (1)-(4)) remain live. No code changes this state-1 session (SPEC + ADR + ROADMAP + STATE only). `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` holds; no new crate/dependency/fuzz-target/`HttpFilterInstance` variant projected (a small new `ConfigError` variant for an invalid `PathMatcher` is a §3 PLAN-write call). **DECISIONS.md ledger head: ADR-0089** (this ADR; project-cumulative count 89; next-available **ADR-0090**, reserved for the §6.2 reconciliation). **ADR-0014 REMAINS IN FORCE; ADR-0028 REMAINS OPEN; ADR-0049 governs** the config-validity all-fatal posture. The state-2 PLAN-write is the next session.
