## ADR-0097: Phase-41 pick + scope — **add the `%REQ_WITHOUT_QUERY(NAME[?ALT])[:N]%` access-log command operator** (like `%REQ%` but with the `?query` string stripped from the resolved value) over the EXISTING command-operator engine + the text/json encoders + the harness — a new `Op` variant + one parse keyword + one render arm + one `encode_single_op` arm + a one-line query-strip, with ZERO new `AccessLogRecord` field / connection plumbing / crate / dependency, and projected NO new `ConfigError` variant; choose `%REQ_WITHOUT_QUERY%` over the rejected alternatives below + fixture `0049`

**Status:** Accepted (phase-41 state-1 brainstorm; `superpowers:brainstorming`). Locks the pick + minimum-viable scope for phase `41-accesslog-req-without-query`. **Consumes the ADR-0097 number** that ADR-0096 reserved for the phase-40 §6.1 split — that split did NOT fire and phase 40 is closed, so the reservation lapsed and `0097` is the next-free number (the same reclaim-a-lapsed-reservation convention by which ADR-0095 reclaimed the phase-39 split slot, ADR-0093 the phase-38, and ADR-0091 the phase-37). Supersedes nothing. Builds on ADR-0078/0079 (the phase-32 command-operator engine + the `(NAME[?ALT])[:N]` grammar + the `-` sentinel + `:N` truncation), ADR-0092/0094 (the phase-38/39 json encoder + `encode_single_op` typed classifier), ADR-0090 §B (the phase-37 `strip_query` query-strip precedent), ADR-0049 (config-validity all-fatal).

**Context.** Phases 32/38/39/40 ran the Observability file-sink access-log-encoder vein: the text command-operator engine, the `json_format` JSON-object encoder, the recursive nested `json_format`, and the `omit_empty_values` knob — over a FIXED operator set. That vein's remaining `SubstitutionFormatString` knobs (`sort_properties`, `content_type`) are weak/uncertain, and the deferred CF-39-1 numeric-literal formatting is a protobuf-`double` rabbit hole. ROADMAP rows `00`-`40` are all `done`; `40` was the highest defined row → a free new-phase pick. Envoy's access-log command-operator vocabulary still has many unimplemented operators; `REQ_WITHOUT_QUERY` is the cheapest of them — its data (`record.path`, the `:path`/request-target, which INCLUDES the query — confirmed at `crates/envoy-accesslog/src/record.rs:36-38`) is already in the record, so it needs ZERO new plumbing.

**Options considered (the pick rationale + rejected alternatives):**
- **(CHOSEN) `%REQ_WITHOUT_QUERY%`.** A new `Op::ReqWithoutQuery { name, alt, truncate }` (mirroring `Op::Req`, `command_operator.rs:40`) parsed by the EXISTING `parse_header_op` grammar + a new keyword dispatch (`:231`), resolved by the EXISTING `resolve_req` (`:549`) with the `?ALT` fallback, then the query stripped (substring before the first `?` — the trivial `strip_query` logic from `crates/envoy-filter/src/rbac.rs:96`, ADR-0090 §B, re-implemented in-crate — NO cross-crate dep) and the `:N` truncation applied; plus a `ReqWithoutQuery` arm on `encode_single_op` (`json_format.rs:224`, mirroring the `Req` arm at `:253-262`). ZERO new `AccessLogRecord` field, connection plumbing, request attribute, crate, dependency, `HttpFilterInstance` variant; projected NO new `ConfigError` variant. Byte-exact + deterministic + locally observable (a `GET /p?x=1&y=2` probe → `%REQ_WITHOUT_QUERY(:PATH)%`→`/p` beside `%REQ(:PATH)%`→`/p?x=1&y=2`, byte-identical cross-proxy). ~120–250 LoC / ~5–6 tasks — the cheapest-strong leaf.
- **(rejected) `json_format_options.sort_properties`** — the per-object key-sort toggle. The observed v1.33.0 default IS sorted (ADR-0092 §A, hardcoded in phases 38/39), so the knob RISKS being an empty/no-op differential (whether it observably toggles anything at this pin is itself uncertain — a weak, possibly-empty pick). Its own future phase, pending a §6.2 confirmation it is observable.
- **(rejected) the RBAC connection-context conditions** (`destination_ip`/`source_ip`/…) — each needs the downstream socket address threaded into `FilterRequest` (NEW plumbing) AND produces an ENVIRONMENT-FRAGILE differential (the source/destination IP the two proxies observe differs by harness topology — the `192.168.65.2` bridge-IP / consistent-hash-endpoint divergence class), so the byte-exact cross-proxy compare is hard to make stable. Heavier + fragile; its own future RBAC phase once a connection-context plumbing slice lands.
- **(rejected) the gRPC-ALS / OTLP access-log sinks** — a new access-log SINK needs new gRPC-streaming / OTLP-export transport infrastructure. Higher differential value but much heavier; each its own future Observability phase.
- **(rejected) CF-39-1 numeric-literal `json_format` leaves** — the protobuf-`double` JSON formatting (`1e+06`/`1.5`→string) is a fiddly rabbit hole with low differential-strength-per-LoC. Stays a carry-forward.

**Decision.** Land `%REQ_WITHOUT_QUERY%` as a single phase `41-accesslog-req-without-query` per the SPEC at `docs/envoy-rust/phases/41-accesslog-req-without-query/SPEC.md`. Add `Op::ReqWithoutQuery { name, alt, truncate }` + a `"REQ_WITHOUT_QUERY"` keyword dispatch reusing `parse_header_op` + a render arm (resolve via `resolve_req` with `?ALT` → strip the query → `:N` truncate) + a `ReqWithoutQuery` arm on `encode_single_op` (string→quoted, absent→`null`). Fixture `0049-accesslog-req-without-query` exercises a byte-exact line showing the query-stripped path beside the full path; the in-process backstop carries the strip/no-`?`/truncate-order/`?ALT`/absent/json-typed cases. Minimum-viable per §2 — defers `%RESP_WITHOUT_QUERY%` (N/A), `sort_properties`/`content_type`, CF-39-1, the other operators (each needs a new record field), and the gRPC-ALS/OTLP/tracing/tap surfaces.

**Rationale.** The cheapest pick that (a) continues the byte-exact Observability access-log vein with a NEW operator (after the encoder-knob vein mined out), (b) needs ZERO new infrastructure (the value it strips is already in the record; the strip is a one-liner), (c) is byte-exact + deterministic + locally observable, (d) reuses the entire phase-32/38/39/40 stack (`parse_header_op`/`resolve_req`/`truncate_bytes`/the encoders/the harness), (e) needs no new crate/dependency/record-field/`ConfigError` variant. One strong differential for ~5–6 tasks. It avoids the maybe-empty `sort_properties` and the IP-fragile RBAC conditions.

**Consequences.** No code changes this state-1 session (SPEC + ADR + ROADMAP + STATE only). The state-2 PLAN-write (`superpowers:writing-plans`) runs the §6.2 LOCAL reconnaissance against live `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` (an H1 listener + a file logger using `%REQ_WITHOUT_QUERY(:PATH)%` + a `:N` variant + a non-`:path` variant) and fires **ADR-0098** (reserved) with the locked facts. The KEY §6.2 risks: (1) the **strip point + strip-vs-truncate ORDER** (a `%REQ_WITHOUT_QUERY(:PATH):3%` on `/p?x=1` → `/p` [strip-then-truncate] vs `/p?` [truncate-raw]); (2) the **header scope / `REQ_ALLOW_LIST`** (is a non-`:path` name accepted?); (3) the **`?ALT`** strip; (4) the **absent + json-typed** rendering. **ADR-0099 is reserved** for the §6.1 split (projected NOT to fire — ~120–250 LoC / ~5–6 tasks). The new ROADMAP row `41` lands `in-progress` (depends-on `06 32 38`). Carry-forwards: `%REQ_WITHOUT_QUERY%` touches `command_operator.rs`/`json_format.rs` (the encoder surface), so the phase-39 **M39-1** (mirror-enum sync) / **M39-2** (recursion depth) and the phase-38 **M38-1/M38-2** are ADJACENT and MAY be folded if cheap; **M40-1** (fixture-`0048` README doc-accuracy) and the RBAC/older Minors stay live (this phase does not touch `rbac.rs`). No code changes this state-1 session. `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` holds; no new crate/dependency/fuzz-target/record-field/`HttpFilterInstance` variant projected (NO new `ConfigError` variant projected). **DECISIONS.md ledger head: ADR-0097** (this ADR; project-cumulative count 97; next-available **ADR-0098**, reserved for the §6.2 reconciliation). **ADR-0014 REMAINS IN FORCE; ADR-0028 REMAINS OPEN; ADR-0049 governs.** The state-2 PLAN-write is the next session.

## ADR-0098: Phase-41 §6.2 reconciliation — **FIRES with a MATERIAL PIVOT**: the state-1 pick `%REQ_WITHOUT_QUERY%` is NOT a valid v1.33.0 access-log operator (`Not supported field in StreamInfo: REQ_WITHOUT_QUERY` — VOID, like phase-38's non-existent `typed_json_format`), so phase 41 pivots to **`%ROUTE_NAME%`** (recon-confirmed VALID — the matched route's config `name`, an `Option<String>` rendered exactly like `%UPSTREAM_HOST%`); the phase dir is renamed `41-accesslog-req-without-query` → `41-accesslog-route-name`; NO new `ConfigError` variant; **ADR-0099 (the §6.1 split) does NOT fire**

**Status:** Accepted (phase-41 state-2 PLAN-write; `superpowers:writing-plans`). Consumes the **ADR-0098** number ADR-0097 reserved for the §6.2 reconciliation. **Amends** ADR-0097 (the phase-41 pick): the operator choice `%REQ_WITHOUT_QUERY%` is VOID; the cheapest-strong pick within phase 41 becomes `%ROUTE_NAME%`. Builds on ADR-0078/0079 (the command-operator engine), ADR-0092/0094 (the json `encode_single_op` typed classifier), ADR-0049. **This ADR FIRES** — the reconnaissance overturns the state-1 pick itself; the SPEC is re-scoped + the PLAN authored against the locked facts below.

**Context.** ADR-0097/SPEC picked `%REQ_WITHOUT_QUERY%` (a `%REQ%`-with-the-query-stripped operator) on the assumption it is a real Envoy access-log operator. The state-2 §6.2 reconnaissance stood up the pinned image `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` in Docker with a file logger configured `json_format: { stripped: "%REQ_WITHOUT_QUERY(:PATH)%" }` and drove `GET /p?…`. (NOTE: a stray leftover `envoy-bin` host process from a prior differential test was holding port 10000, masking the result as a "Created"-state container until the recon moved to fresh host ports — a leftover-process lesson akin to ADR-0090's leftover-container.)

**Findings (each EMPIRICALLY OBSERVED against live v1.33.0; D-3.3).**

**§A — `%REQ_WITHOUT_QUERY%` is NOT a v1.33.0 access-log operator. [VOIDS the ADR-0097 pick.]** The config boot-fatals: `error initializing config: Not supported field in StreamInfo: REQ_WITHOUT_QUERY`. This is the same "Not supported field in StreamInfo" error class Envoy emits for any UNKNOWN command operator (cf. phase-38 ADR-0092 §E `%NOPE%`). So `REQ_WITHOUT_QUERY` is not in v1.33.0's access-log command-operator vocabulary (it may exist in a later Envoy, or under a different spelling — irrelevant at the pin). → The phase-41 pick is VOID; the SPEC's `%REQ_WITHOUT_QUERY%` design is discarded. This is the verify-at-PLAN-write discipline catching a bad pick BEFORE any implementation (mirrors phase-38 ADR-0092 §C, where the §6.2 recon found `typed_json_format` non-existent).

**§B — the pivot: a batch recon of candidate operators found these VALID + DETERMINISTIC at v1.33.0** (each rendered for `GET /p?x=1` → a `direct_response` route named `route1`): `%ROUTE_NAME%`→`"route1"`; `%RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS%`→`"direct_response"`; `%ACCESS_LOG_TYPE%`→`"DownstreamEnd"`; `%REQUEST_HEADERS_BYTES%`→`155`; `%UPSTREAM_CLUSTER%`/`%REQUESTED_SERVER_NAME%`/`%VIRTUAL_CLUSTER_NAME%`/`%CONNECTION_TERMINATION_DETAILS%`→`null` (absent on this plaintext/direct_response setup). → **`%ROUTE_NAME%` is the cheapest-strong DETERMINISTIC pivot**: it reads the matched route's static config `name` (config-deterministic, byte-exact), needs ONE new `Option<String>` record field, and renders EXACTLY like the existing `%UPSTREAM_HOST%`. `%RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS%` (a rabbit hole of detail strings), `%ACCESS_LOG_TYPE%` (a near-constant — weak), and `%REQUEST_HEADERS_BYTES%` (header-byte counting — needs new data + fragile) were rejected as gnarlier/weaker; the `null`-rendering operators need TLS/upstream setup. The other valid operators are deferred to their own future phases.

**§C — `%ROUTE_NAME%` semantics LOCKED.** A NAMED route (`name: myroute`) → `%ROUTE_NAME%` renders `myroute`: as a json single-operator value → quoted `"myroute"`; in a mixed/multi-segment value (`r=%ROUTE_NAME%`) → `r=myroute`. An UNNAMED route → ABSENT: json single-op → `null`; mixed/text → the `-` sentinel (`r=-`). → `%ROUTE_NAME%` is an `Option<String>` whose `Some`→the route name, `None`→absent — IDENTICAL to `Op::UpstreamHost` (`record.upstream_host: Option<String>`, `render_op` `unwrap_or("-")`, `encode_single_op` `quote_opt`). The implementation copies that pattern with a new `record.route_name` field.

**Decision.** PIVOT phase 41 to `%ROUTE_NAME%`; rename the phase dir to `41-accesslog-route-name`; re-scope the SPEC. **Implementation:** add `pub route_name: Option<String>` to `AccessLogRecord` (mirroring `upstream_host`); set it at the H1 + H2 HCM record-construction sites from the matched route's config `name` (non-empty → `Some`, else `None` — PLAN-VERIFY the route struct exposes `name`, add `pub name: String` to the route struct if absent); add `Op::RouteName` (a `"ROUTE_NAME"` no-arg keyword) + its `render_op` arm (`unwrap_or("-")`) + its `encode_single_op` arm (`quote_opt`). Fixture `0049-accesslog-route-name` (a named route → the byte-exact route-name line); the backstop carries named/unnamed × text/json-single/mixed. NO new crate/dependency/fuzz-target/`ConfigError` variant; ONE new `AccessLogRecord` field.

**§6.1 split — does NOT fire (ADR-0099 stays UNFIRED).** ONE record field + ONE `Op` variant (mirroring `Op::UpstreamHost`) + the HCM plumbing + one fixture + backstop + seed. **~120–250 LoC / ~5–6 tasks** — under the §6.1 gate.

**Consequences.** `PLAN.md` is authored THIS state-2 session against §A–§C inline (no projections survive except the PLAN-VERIFY route-`name`-exposure detail). NO new crate/dependency/fuzz-target/`HttpFilterInstance` variant; NO new `ConfigError` variant; ONE new `AccessLogRecord` field (`route_name`). `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` holds. Carry-forwards: phase 41 touches `command_operator.rs`/`json_format.rs`/`record.rs`/`hcm.rs` — the adjacent **M39-1/M39-2/M38-1/M38-2** MAY be folded if cheap; **M40-1** + the RBAC/older Minors stay live. **DECISIONS.md ledger head: ADR-0098** (this ADR; project-cumulative count 98; next-available **ADR-0099**, RESERVED for the §6.1 split which this ADR confirms does NOT fire). **ADR-0014 REMAINS IN FORCE; ADR-0028 REMAINS OPEN; ADR-0049 governs.** The state-3 implementation is the next session.

## ADR-0099: Phase-42 pick + scope — **add the `%RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS%` access-log command operator** (the response-code-details string Envoy attaches to the reply — e.g. `via_upstream` for an upstream-routed response, `direct_response` for a `direct_response` route) over the EXISTING command-operator engine + the text/json encoders + the harness — a new `Op::ResponseCodeDetails` no-arg keyword + one render arm + one `encode_single_op` arm + a new `AccessLogRecord.response_code_details: Option<String>` field set by the HCM, rendered EXACTLY like `%ROUTE_NAME%`/`%UPSTREAM_HOST%`, with the detail-string vocabulary BOUNDED to the deterministic value(s) the fixture exercises; **the leading candidate `%VIRTUAL_HOST_NAME%` was EXISTENCE-VETOED at state-1** (VOID at v1.33.0); choose `%RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS%` over the rejected alternatives below + fixture `0050`

**Status:** Accepted (phase-42 state-1 brainstorm; `superpowers:brainstorming`). Locks the pick + minimum-viable scope for phase `42-accesslog-response-code-details`. **Consumes the ADR-0099 number** that ADR-0098 reserved for the phase-41 §6.1 split — that split did NOT fire and phase 41 is closed, so the reservation lapsed and `0099` is the next-free number (the same reclaim-a-lapsed-reservation convention by which ADR-0097 reclaimed the phase-40 split slot, ADR-0095 the phase-39, and ADR-0093 the phase-38). Supersedes nothing. Builds on ADR-0078/0079 (the phase-32 command-operator engine + the `(NAME[?ALT])[:N]` grammar + the `-` sentinel), ADR-0092/0094 (the phase-38/39 json encoder + `encode_single_op` typed classifier), ADR-0098 §C (the phase-41 `%ROUTE_NAME%` `Option<String>` record-field-operator pattern + the H2 `*_for_log_h2` parameter-thread), ADR-0049 (config-validity all-fatal).

**Context.** Phase 41 closed `%ROUTE_NAME%` (the first "operator backed by a new `Option<String>` record field" leaf). The phase-41 ADR-0098 §B batch recon had confirmed several more operators VALID at v1.33.0 (incl. `%RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS%`, `%UPSTREAM_CLUSTER%`, `%REQUEST_HEADERS_BYTES%`). The next-phase pick must choose the cheapest-strong VALID leaf in that sub-vein. The leading candidate this session was `%VIRTUAL_HOST_NAME%` — the EXACT `%ROUTE_NAME%` pattern (the matched virtual-host's config `name`), even cheaper because `VirtualHost.name` ALREADY exists in `bootstrap.rs` (no new config field) — IF it is a real v1.33.0 operator. **The phase-41 lesson (verify the pick EXISTS) was applied as a LIVE existence-check at THIS state-1**, on fresh host ports, against the pinned image, BEFORE locking the SPEC.

**Findings (each EMPIRICALLY OBSERVED against live `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0`; D-3.3).**

**§A — `%VIRTUAL_HOST_NAME%` (the leading candidate) is NOT a v1.33.0 access-log operator. [VETOES it BEFORE the SPEC locks.]** A config with `json_format: { vhn: "%VIRTUAL_HOST_NAME%" }` (a named virtual_host + a direct_response route) boot-fatals: `error initializing config: Not supported field in StreamInfo: VIRTUAL_HOST_NAME` (the same error class Envoy emits for any unknown command operator — cf. ADR-0098 §A `%REQ_WITHOUT_QUERY%`, ADR-0092 §C `typed_json_format`/`%NOPE%`). So `VIRTUAL_HOST_NAME` is not in v1.33.0's access-log command-operator vocabulary at the pin. This is the verify-at-state-1 discipline catching a bad pick EARLIER than phase 41 caught its bad pick (phase 41 found `%REQ_WITHOUT_QUERY%` VOID only at the state-2 §6.2 recon, forcing a mid-state-2 pivot + a dir rename; here the veto landed at state-1, so the SPEC was authored ONLY against the valid fallback — no pivot, no rename).

**§B — the pick: `%RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS%` is VALID + DETERMINISTIC at v1.33.0.** Re-confirmed live this session (not trusting the prior-phase ADR-0098 §B recon blindly): a config with `json_format: { rcd: "%RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS%", mixed: "d=%RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS%", code: "%RESPONSE_CODE%" }` boots + serves. An **upstream-routed `200`** (a STATIC cluster pointing at Envoy's own admin as a real backend) → `%RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS%` = **`via_upstream`** (json single-op → quoted `"via_upstream"`; mixed → `d=via_upstream`); a **`direct_response` route** → **`direct_response`** (line `{"code":200,"mixed":"d=direct_response","rcd":"direct_response"}`). → `%RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS%` is an always-present-on-completion `String` that the MVP models as `Option<String>` (`Some`→the detail string, `None`→absent → `quote_opt`/`unwrap_or("-")`) — IDENTICAL to `Op::RouteName`/`Op::UpstreamHost`.

**§C — `%RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS%` scope LOCKED (the rabbit-hole bounded).** ADR-0098 §B had rejected `%RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS%` for phase 41 as "a rabbit hole of detail strings"; that risk is RESOLVED here by BOUNDING the MVP to the deterministic value(s) the §2 fixture exercises (the `via_upstream` upstream-routed-success path; possibly also `direct_response` if envoy-rust supports a `direct_response` route cheaply — PLAN-VERIFY). The OPERATOR is complete (parse + text + json single-op + the record field); only the SET of distinct detail strings envoy-rust can emit is bounded — each additional detail-string path (the local-reply details, `route_not_found`, the filter-generated details) grows naturally as envoy-rust grows the corresponding response path (§2.2 future work). This is the cheapest-strong framing: it reuses the existing upstream access-log fixture template (the natural `via_upstream` value) and the entire `%ROUTE_NAME%` machinery.

**Decision.** Phase 42 = `42-accesslog-response-code-details`: add `%RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS%`. **Implementation:** add `pub response_code_details: Option<String>` to `AccessLogRecord` (mirroring `route_name`); set it at the H1 + H2 HCM record-construction sites for the response path taken (upstream-routed success → `Some("via_upstream")`; the H2 site via a new `response_code_details_for_log_h2` emit-fn parameter, mirroring the phase-41 `route_name_for_log_h2` thread); add `Op::ResponseCodeDetails` (a `"RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS"` no-arg keyword) + its `render_op` arm (`unwrap_or("-")`) + its `encode_single_op` arm (`quote_opt`). Fixture `0050-accesslog-response-code-details` (an upstream-routed request → the byte-exact `via_upstream` line; optionally a second `direct_response` witness — PLAN-VERIFY); the backstop carries present/absent × text/json-single/mixed. NO new crate/dependency/fuzz-target/`ConfigError` variant; ONE new `AccessLogRecord` field.

**Rejected alternatives.** (1) **`%VIRTUAL_HOST_NAME%`** — VOID at v1.33.0 (§A); the existence-check vetoed it. (2) **`%UPSTREAM_CLUSTER%`** — VALID but rendered `null` on the plaintext/direct_response recon (ADR-0098 §B); needs a routed-upstream fixture to witness a non-null value (achievable, but `%RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS%` is at least as cheap and the `via_upstream` value is more universal). (3) **`%REQUEST_HEADERS_BYTES%`** — VALID (rendered `155`) but header-byte counting is new data + fragile across header-set differences (ADR-0098 §B rejected it as gnarlier). (4) **`%ACCESS_LOG_TYPE%`** — VALID but a near-constant (`DownstreamEnd`) — weak differential. (5) **CF-39-1 numeric-literal `json_format` leaves / `sort_properties`** — risk of an empty differential (observability unverified). (6) **the gRPC-ALS/OTLP/tracing/tap surfaces** — new sink/transport infrastructure, far heavier than a one-operator leaf. `%RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS%` is the cheapest-strong VALID pick.

**§6.1 split — does NOT fire (ADR-0100 stays UNFIRED).** ONE record field + ONE `Op` variant (mirroring `Op::RouteName`) + the HCM plumbing (H1 + the H2 parameter-thread) + one fixture + backstop + seed + a BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT note. **~120–250 LoC / ~5–6 tasks** — under the §6.1 gate. **ADR-0100 reserved** for the split (projected NOT to fire).

**Consequences.** No code changes this state-1 session (SPEC + ADR + ROADMAP + STATE only). The state-2 PLAN-write (`superpowers:writing-plans`) runs the §6.2 recon against live `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` (the suffix grammar [no-arg / `:N`]; the exact HCM-path → detail-string mapping for the fixture(s); whether a `direct_response` second witness is cheap) and authors `PLAN.md` against the §A–§C facts + the locked details; **ADR-0099 does NOT need a §6.2 reconciliation ADR** unless that recon overturns a §A–§C fact (the pick is already existence-verified — the phase-41-style pivot risk is retired at state-1). The new ROADMAP row `42` lands `in-progress` (depends-on `06 32 38 41`). Carry-forwards: `%RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS%` touches `command_operator.rs`/`json_format.rs`/`record.rs`/`hcm.rs` — the adjacent **M39-1/M39-2/M38-1/M38-2** MAY be folded if cheap; **M40-1** + the RBAC/older Minors (it does not touch `rbac.rs`) stay live. No code changes this state-1 session. `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` holds; no new crate/dependency/fuzz-target/`HttpFilterInstance` variant projected (NO new `ConfigError` variant projected). **DECISIONS.md ledger head: ADR-0099** (this ADR; project-cumulative count 99; next-available **ADR-0100**, reserved for the §6.1 split which this ADR projects does NOT fire). **ADR-0014 REMAINS IN FORCE; ADR-0028 REMAINS OPEN; ADR-0049 governs** the config-validity all-fatal posture. The state-2 PLAN-write is the next session.

## ADR-0100: Phase-43 pick + scope — **add the `%UPSTREAM_CLUSTER%` access-log command operator (the matched cluster's config `name`) + stand up the FIRST proxy (upstream-routed) access-log differential fixture** — a new `Op::UpstreamCluster` no-arg keyword + a new `AccessLogRecord.upstream_cluster: Option<String>` field set by the HCM at the proxy-success arm (the cluster name is ALREADY in hand as `BuildOutcome::Proxy { cluster }`), rendered EXACTLY like `%UPSTREAM_HOST%`; the enabling work is extending the access-log differential driver to route to a real backend (the access-log fixture family `0040`-`0050` is `direct_response`-only / `clusters: []`), which ALSO witnesses, near-free on the proxy path, the already-implemented `%UPSTREAM_HOST%` + `%RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS%`→`via_upstream` (advancing carry-forward M42-1); the §6.1 split is projected to LIKELY fire; choose `%UPSTREAM_CLUSTER%` over the rejected alternatives below + fixture `0051`

**Status:** Accepted (phase-43 state-1 brainstorm; `superpowers:brainstorming`). Locks the pick + minimum-viable scope for phase `43-accesslog-upstream-cluster`. **Consumes the ADR-0100 number** that ADR-0099 reserved for the phase-42 §6.1 split — that split did NOT fire and phase 42 is closed, so the reservation lapsed and `0100` is the next-free number (the same reclaim-a-lapsed-reservation convention by which ADR-0099 reclaimed the phase-41 split slot, ADR-0097 the phase-40, ADR-0095 the phase-39). Supersedes nothing. Builds on ADR-0078/0079 (the phase-32 command-operator engine + the `-` sentinel), ADR-0092/0094 (the phase-38/39 json encoder + `encode_single_op` typed classifier), ADR-0098 §C / ADR-0099 (the phase-41/42 `Option<String>` record-field-operator pattern + the H2 `*_for_log_h2` parameter-thread), ADR-0049 (config-validity all-fatal).

**Context.** Phases 41/42 closed `%ROUTE_NAME%`/`%RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS%` (the "operator backed by a new `Option<String>` record field" sub-vein). EVERY access-log differential fixture to date (`0040`-`0050`) drives a `direct_response` route (`clusters: []`, no backend) — so the upstream-routed access-log path has NEVER been differentially exercised, and operators whose value is `null`/absent without an upstream (`%UPSTREAM_CLUSTER%`, and the already-implemented-but-never-witnessed `%UPSTREAM_HOST%`) cannot be tested. The phase-42 state-5 review opened carry-forward **M42-1** (`%RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS%`'s `via_upstream` is set on endpoint-PICK not response-success, unobservable without a proxy fixture). The next-phase pick must weigh the cheapest-strong leaf; the project's own breadcrumbs (the phase-42 STATE close-out candidate menu) led with `%UPSTREAM_CLUSTER%` + the proxy-fixture + the M42-1 synergy.

**Findings (each EMPIRICALLY OBSERVED against live `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0`; D-3.3; the phases-41/42 "verify the pick EXISTS" lesson applied at state-1).**

**§A — `%UPSTREAM_CLUSTER%` is VALID + config-DETERMINISTIC at v1.33.0.** A config with a `route: { cluster: my_backend_cluster }` (a STATIC cluster pointing at Envoy's own admin as a real backend) + `json_format: { uc: "%UPSTREAM_CLUSTER%", mixed: "c=%UPSTREAM_CLUSTER%", rcd: "%RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS%" }` boots + serves a routed `200`; the line is `{"mixed":"c=my_backend_cluster","rcd":"via_upstream","uc":"my_backend_cluster"}`. → `%UPSTREAM_CLUSTER%` renders the matched cluster's static config `name` (json single-op → quoted `"my_backend_cluster"`; mixed → `c=my_backend_cluster`); on a `direct_response`/local-reply path it is ABSENT (→ `null` / `-` sentinel — it was `null` on the phase-42 direct_response recons). It is an `Option<String>` IDENTICAL in shape to `Op::UpstreamHost` — a STATIC STRING, NO formula to match.

**§B — the same proxy line witnesses `%RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS%`→`via_upstream` (M42-1 synergy).** The routed `200` rendered `rcd: "via_upstream"` — confirming that the first proxy access-log fixture witnesses, for the first time on a real upstream-success path, both `%RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS%`'s `via_upstream` value (advancing M42-1 — the success path becomes differentially covered) and the already-implemented-but-never-differentially-tested `%UPSTREAM_HOST%` (phase 06). These are near-free regression bonuses on the SAME fixture (the operators already exist; only `%UPSTREAM_CLUSTER%` is new).

**§C — the cost is the ENABLING harness infra (the first proxy access-log fixture).** Confirmed by code-read: ALL access-log fixtures `0040`-`0050` use `clusters: []`; the `Driver::Http1WithAccessLog` driver drives a `direct_response` listener + scrapes the file log — it does NOT start a backend. The harness DOES have backend/upstream machinery (`tests/differential/src/backend.rs`/`upstream.rs`) used by other (non-access-log) drivers. So phase 43's genuinely-new work is WIRING a backend into the access-log driver (extend `Http1WithAccessLog` or add a driver variant — PLAN-VERIFY the seam). The OPERATOR itself is trivial: the cluster name is already in hand at the HCM proxy-success arm as `BuildOutcome::Proxy { cluster }` (where `upstream_host_for_log` + `response_code_details = via_upstream` are already set), so `upstream_cluster = Some(cluster_name)` is a one-line addition there; the `Op::UpstreamCluster` is an exact `Op::UpstreamHost` mirror.

**Decision.** Phase 43 = `43-accesslog-upstream-cluster`: add `%UPSTREAM_CLUSTER%` + the first proxy access-log fixture. **Implementation:** add `pub upstream_cluster: Option<String>` to `AccessLogRecord` (mirror `upstream_host`); set it at the H1 + H2 HCM proxy-success arm from `BuildOutcome::Proxy { cluster }` (non-proxy → `None`; the H2 side via a new `finalize_h2_stream` parameter); add `Op::UpstreamCluster` (a `"UPSTREAM_CLUSTER"` no-arg keyword) + its `render_op` arm (`unwrap_or`) + its `encode_single_op` arm (`quote_opt`). Extend the access-log differential driver to route to a real backend; fixture `0051-accesslog-upstream-cluster` (a routed request → the byte-exact cluster-name + `via_upstream` line; `%UPSTREAM_HOST%` witnessed loosely if its ephemeral ip:port is non-deterministic — PLAN-VERIFY pin/normalize/exclude); the backstop carries present/absent × text/json-single/mixed. NO new crate/dependency/fuzz-target/`ConfigError` variant; ONE new `AccessLogRecord` field; ONE new `Op` variant.

**Rejected alternatives.** (1) **`%REQUEST_HEADERS_BYTES%`** — VALID (rendered `155`) but a header-byte COUNT whose exact value requires reverse-engineering Envoy's accounting formula (which headers / pseudo-headers / per-header overhead) — a formula-match rabbit hole (ADR-0098 §B flagged it "fragile"); `%UPSTREAM_CLUSTER%` is a pass-through static string with no formula. (2) **`%ACCESS_LOG_TYPE%`** — VALID but a near-constant (`DownstreamEnd` for envoy-rust's single end-of-stream log) — weak differential (indistinguishable from a hard-coded constant). (3) **`%VIRTUAL_HOST_NAME%`** — VOID at v1.33.0 (phase-42 ADR-0099 §A). (4) **`%RESPONSE_HEADERS_BYTES%`** — varies with date/server response headers — fragile. (5) **CF-39-1 numeric-literal leaves / `sort_properties`** — empty-differential risk. (6) **gRPC ALS / OTLP / tracing / tap** — new sink/transport infrastructure, far heavier. `%UPSTREAM_CLUSTER%` is the cheapest-STRONG VALID pick AND its enabling proxy access-log fixture is foundational (it unlocks `%UPSTREAM_HOST%`, the M42-1 `via_upstream` correctness, and future upstream-only operators).

**§6.1 split — projected to LIKELY fire (ADR-0101 reserved).** Unlike phases 41/42 (which cloned an existing direct_response fixture), this phase stands up NEW harness infra (a backend wired into the access-log driver) on top of the one-operator leaf. The operator is ~6 tasks (~120-250 LoC, the proven pattern); the harness extension may add materially more. The state-2 PLAN-write decides whether to SPLIT (`43.1` proxy-access-log harness + `43.2` the operator) or keep it whole; **ADR-0101 is reserved** for that split.

**Consequences.** No code changes this state-1 session (SPEC + ADR + ROADMAP + STATE only). The state-2 PLAN-write (`superpowers:writing-plans`) runs the §6.2 recon (the suffix grammar; the `%UPSTREAM_HOST%` determinism on the fixture; the proxy access-log driver seam; the H2 path) and authors `PLAN.md` (deciding the §6.1 split). The new ROADMAP row `43` lands `in-progress` (depends-on `06 32 38 42`). Carry-forwards: this phase ADVANCES **M42-1** (witnesses `via_upstream` on the upstream-success path) but does NOT close it (the failure-path detail vocabulary still needs failure-injection fixtures); **M39-1/M39-2/M38-1/M38-2 + CF-39-1 + M40-1** + the RBAC/older Minors stay live. No code changes this state-1 session. `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` holds; no new crate/dependency/fuzz-target/`HttpFilterInstance` variant projected (NO new `ConfigError` variant projected). **DECISIONS.md ledger head: ADR-0100** (this ADR; project-cumulative count 100; next-available **ADR-0101**, reserved for the §6.1 split). **ADR-0014 REMAINS IN FORCE; ADR-0028 REMAINS OPEN; ADR-0049 governs** the config-validity all-fatal posture. The state-2 PLAN-write is the next session.

## ADR-0152: Phase-73 §5 state-0/1 brainstorm — pick the access-log FILTER arms #4 & #5, the recursive `and_filter` / `or_filter` composition, over `duration_filter`/`grpc_status_filter`/`metadata_filter`/`runtime_filter`, the H2 differential, and the §9 family openers

- Date: 2026-07-21
- Status: accepted
- Context: Phase 72 closed (ROADMAP rows `00`-`72` all `done` [`59`/`60`/`62` intentional gaps], STATE "awaiting next planning"), so this is the §5 state-0/1 next-phase pick (`superpowers:brainstorming`; memory `closeout-and-pick-are-separate-sessions` — its OWN session). The access-log FILTER subsystem (`envoy.config.accesslog.v3.AccessLogFilter`, the per-record log-emission oneof) now has THREE leaf arms — `status_code_filter` (phase 70), `response_flag_filter` (phase 71), `header_filter` (phase 72) — plus a runtime `should_log(status, response_flags, headers)` seam (twice-widened) threaded through both HCM emit loops, and a byte-exact `Http1AccessLogByteExact` differential driver whose `expect_logged` + `extra_headers` + `expected_logged_count` probe fields already exist. A next unit of progress must clear the cheapest-strong-differential bar (the phase-66/68/69/70/71/72 precedent). The phase-72 SPEC §4 pre-identified `and_filter`/`or_filter` as "a natural NEXT leaf once ≥3 leaf arms exist … deferred, not rejected on merit." Two state-0 recon fan-outs ran this session against the pinned `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` (digest `sha256:56da5afd…770c2`): an in-tree change-surface survey and a live `--mode validate` + port-mapped runtime probe (graceful-stop flush).
- Options considered:
  - **`and_filter` / `or_filter`** — the recursive composition arms (`{ filters: repeated AccessLogFilter }`, MEASURED PGV `min_items = 2`, mutually-exclusive oneof arms, arbitrary-depth nesting): gate a sink on the boolean AND/OR of its nested child predicates.
  - **`duration_filter`** — timing-based (`op(request_duration_ms, threshold)`); the differential needs latency bounds and is flaky.
  - **`grpc_status_filter` / `metadata_filter` / `runtime_filter`** — each needs a new data axis (gRPC trailer status / dynamic-metadata plumbing / RTDS).
  - **The standalone H2 access-log-filter differential** (the deferred M71-6).
  - **Each §9 family opener** (network-filter payload codecs, `sni_cluster`, non-deterministic LB, HTTP/3+QUIC, gRPC bridge/transcoding, observability SINKS, runtime/RTDS, hot-restart, WASM host).
- Decision: Phase 73 = `73-accesslog-and-or-filter`: land BOTH recursive composition arms `AccessLogFilter.and_filter` / `or_filter` (arms #4 & #5) end-to-end in one phase, behaviorally equivalent to `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0`. Add `AndFilter { filters: Vec<AccessLogFilter> }` + `OrFilter { filters: Vec<AccessLogFilter> }` config structs (NO `Box` — the `Vec` breaks the recursion; MEASURED R-0.1/R-0.6) + the two oneof arms; extend the compiler-forced `set_arms` cardinality destructuring + the `compile_access_log_filter` match from 3 to 5 arms; add `filters.len() >= 2` fail-loud validation (MEASURED PGV `min_items = 2`, R-0.2) + **recursive** per-child validation by extracting the currently-inline per-filter body into a `&mut`-taking helper (so nested `header_filter` SafeRegex still compiles in place). Add `LogFilter::And(Vec<LogFilter>)` / `LogFilter::Or(Vec<LogFilter>)` runtime variants whose `should_log` evaluates `.all()` / `.any()` — the phase-72 widened signature already carries everything a composition needs (NO further widening); NO new `Eq`/`PartialEq`, NO `envoy-config` dependency (ADR-0150 holds). Witness byte-exact by TWO NEW backend-free fixtures: `0079-accesslog-and-filter` (`and_filter { [header_filter{x-a=1}, header_filter{x-b=1}] }` → only the both-match probe KEPT, MEASURED R-0.3) + `0080-accesslog-or-filter` (`or_filter { [and_filter{[x-a,x-b]}, header_filter{x-c=1}] }`, depth-2 — witnesses the recursion differentially, MEASURED R-0.5). Full scope, PLAN-VERIFY items (PV-1..PV-8), and rejected-alternative detail live in `docs/envoy-rust/phases/73-accesslog-and-or-filter/SPEC.md`.
- Rationale: `and_filter`/`or_filter` are the cheapest arms #4/#5 — they compose the THREE already-covered leaf predicates with ZERO new request-data plumbing (the twice-widened `should_log(status, response_flags, headers)` already carries everything, MEASURED R-0.1) and reuse the ENTIRE byte-exact differential driver UNCHANGED (MEASURED R-0.1: the `extra_headers`/`expect_logged`/`expected_logged_count` fields cover both fixtures), so each fixture is pure config + probes + a ~10-line test. The only new machinery is one recursive config type + one recursive validation helper + two `LogFilter` variants (`.all()`/`.any()`). They light up a genuinely NEW observable axis (boolean COMPOSITION), yield deterministic BACKEND-FREE byte-exact single-line observables (MEASURED R-0.3/R-0.4), and witness recursion depth-2 cross-proxy (MEASURED R-0.5). The two arms are STRUCTURALLY IDENTICAL (differ only by `.all()` vs `.any()`), so one phase pays the single expensive item — the validator recursion refactor — ONCE and serves both; splitting would duplicate the entire scaffolding for a one-line delta (§4). `duration_filter` is timing-flaky; `grpc_status_filter`/`metadata_filter`/`runtime_filter` each need a new data axis far above the near-zero-new-logic bar; the standalone H2 differential is weak (codec-agnostic gate, already byte-identical); each §9 opener is a large new subsystem. Rust recursion is hazard-free (MEASURED R-0.6: both the config `AccessLogFilter` and the runtime `LogFilter` recurse through `Vec<_>`, a fixed-size pointer → no `Box`; serde derive + `Debug/Default/Serialize/Deserialize/PartialEq` compose over recursive types; no `Eq`/`PartialEq` introduced).
- Consequences: No code changes this state-0/1 session (SPEC + ADR + ROADMAP row `73` `in-progress` + STATE advance only). The state-2 PLAN-write (`superpowers:writing-plans`) runs the §6.2 empirical reconciliation (PV-1..PV-8 — the `AndFilter`/`OrFilter` serde model, the validator recursion refactor + `filters.len() >= 2`, the two `LogFilter` variants + the recursive compile, the driver-reuse confirmation, the fuzz disposition, the split-gate re-derive) and authors `PLAN.md`. New ROADMAP row `73` lands `in-progress` (depends-on `06 32 70 71 72`). **ADR-0153 reserved** for the §6.2 reconciliation; **ADR-0154 reserved** for the §6.1 split (very unlikely — both arms share ALL scaffolding, ~670-LoC single phase). CHEAPLY FOLDS the candidate M71-3 (all-suppressed `expected_logged_count == 0` shape — weigh at state-2). OPENS **CF-73-1** (the recursive arms accept arbitrary nesting depth with NO stack guard — parity with upstream, R-0.6; a documented deferred non-goal owned by a future stack-safety phase). NOT consumed (still live): CF-72-1/CF-72-2 (`HeaderMatcher`-parity — a composition arm does not touch the match engine), M71-6/7/8, M70-R4/R9, M69-A..I, CF-69-1/2/3/5, M68-1, M-1, CF-67-3/5/6/7, the older Minors + the HTTP-filters-family (1)–(4). **ADR-0028 REMAINS OPEN** (`runtime_key` + the 23 inert `response_flag_filter` tokens stay RTDS-inert); ADR-0049 governs the config-validity fail-loud posture; ADR-0016/0124/0131/0133/0136/0137/0139/0140-0151 preserved (esp. ADR-0150: `LogFilter` has NO `Eq`/`PartialEq`, `envoy-accesslog` MUST NOT depend on `envoy-config`; ADR-0147: kept-LAST suppression-fixture authoring). **DECISIONS.md ledger head: ADR-0152** (next-available **ADR-0153**, reserved). `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` holds. The state-2 PLAN-write is the next session.

## ADR-0151: Phase-72 §5.2 state-3 re-implementation — the PV-4 `invert_match` + ABSENT divergence is **MODE-DEPENDENT**: value-matcher+invert+absent DIVERGES (upstream DROPS), but `present_match`+invert+absent is PARITY (upstream KEEPS); CF-72-1 is re-scoped to the **value-matcher** case

- Date: 2026-07-20
- Status: accepted (does NOT supersede ADR-0149 — its state-2 decision to scope PV-4 OUT and open CF-72-1 stands; this ADR CORRECTS the *characterization* of that boundary)
- Context: The phase-72 §5 state-5 code-review (`REVIEW.md`, F-1, Important MUST-FIX) LIVE-PROBED the headline PV-4 divergence on BOTH proxies (envoy-rust DEBUG `envoy-bin` vs. `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0`, port-mapped, graceful-stop flush) and MEASURED that the interaction is **mode-dependent**, not the blanket "absent+invert = divergence" that ADR-0149 (PV-4 note) and SPEC §0/R-0.6 recorded:
  - `present_match: true` + `invert_match` + ABSENT header → **KEEP on BOTH** proxies (**PARITY**).
  - a VALUE-based matcher (`exact`/`prefix`/`suffix`/`safe_regex`/`range`/`string_match`) + `invert_match` + ABSENT header → envoy-rust **KEEP** vs. upstream **DROP** (**DIVERGENCE**).
  Upstream special-cases a missing header: for a value matcher a missing header is an unconditional value no-match that `invert_match` does NOT resurrect (→ DROP); for `present_match` the present-check is `false` and `invert_match` DOES flip it (→ KEEP). envoy-rust's shared engine (`matcher.rs:51`) applies `mode_result ^ invert_match` UNIFORMLY, so absent (`mode_result = false`) → `false ^ true` = KEEP in BOTH modes — coincidentally matching upstream for `present_match` but diverging for value matchers. The state-4 in-tree pin `pv4_absent_plus_invert_is_kept_inherited_shared_engine_boundary` (`matcher.rs:397`) exercised `PresentMatch(true)` — the ONE mode that does NOT diverge — and labeled that PARITY case "diverges from upstream — CF-72-1"; the genuinely-divergent value-matcher case was pinned by NO test.
- Options considered:
  - (a) Leave the pin as-is. REJECTED — it documents parity as divergence and actively misleads: a future CF-72-1 fixer reading it would "fix" the shared engine to DROP `absent+invert` UNIFORMLY and thereby BREAK `present_match+invert+absent` (which upstream KEEPS), introducing a NEW divergence.
  - (b) Change runtime behavior now (special-case value-matcher absent+invert to DROP). REJECTED — that IS CF-72-1, a cross-cutting route+access-log change with a route-differential blast radius, out of arm-#3 scope; ADR-0149's deferral stands.
  - (c) Correct the pins + docs to the measured mode-scope and re-scope CF-72-1. CHOSEN.
- Decision: NO runtime code change. Correct the test surface and docs to the MEASURED mode-scope:
  - `matcher.rs` — replace the mislabeled pin with two mode-scoped pins: `pv4_value_matcher_absent_plus_invert_kept_diverges_from_upstream` (value matcher `exact`+invert+absent → KEEP, MEASURED-divergent from upstream DROP = CF-72-1) and `pv4_present_match_absent_plus_invert_kept_is_parity_with_upstream` (`present_match`+invert+absent → KEEP = PARITY; a future CF-72-1 fixer MUST preserve this KEEP). The `header_match_trait_delegates_to_inherent_engine` invert leg now exercises the value-matcher divergence through the `HeaderMatch` seam.
  - **CF-72-1 is re-scoped** from the blanket "shared-engine absent+invert fix" to the **value-based-matcher absent+invert fix** (the `present_match` mode is parity and must stay KEEP). Reflected in `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md` §C and the §5.2 re-implementation log.
- Rationale: characterization tests on a phase's HEADLINE divergence must pin the actual divergent behavior and correctly separate it from parity; the two mode-scoped pins are non-vacuous (a mutation applying the naive uniform-DROP "fix" turns BOTH RED, and the parity pin is precisely the guard that catches that mode-breaking fix). ADR-0149's *decision* (scope PV-4 out, reuse the engine verbatim, open CF-72-1) was correct and stands; only its *characterization* of the boundary was too broad.
- Consequences: NO behavior change; fixture `0078` (non-inverted) is unaffected; the §7.5 gate re-verification (state-4) is a separate later session. **CF-72-1** now reads "value-matcher `matcher.rs:51` absent+invert fix (a cross-cutting route+access-log change); the `present_match` mode is upstream-parity and must remain KEEP." Also addressed this state-3 re-entry: **F-2** (a cheap H2 `header_filter` keep/drop unit test — `h2_header_filter_keeps_match_drops_mismatch_and_absent` — closing the unasserted `&envoy_req.headers` threading; the H2 differential stays deferred = M71-6) and **F-3** (an in-process two-sink mixed-filter test — `two_sinks_with_mixed_filters_gate_independently` — closing **M71-5**, MEASURED byte-exact parity at state-5). **DECISIONS.md ledger head: ADR-0151** (next-available **ADR-0152**). ADR-0149/0150 REMAIN IN FORCE; ADR-0028 REMAINS OPEN; ADR-0049 governs the config-validity all-fatal posture.

## ADR-0150: Phase-72 §5 state-3 implementation — the `LogFilter::Header` runtime seam is an injected **`HeaderMatch` trait object**, NOT a carried `envoy_config::HeaderMatcher` (the ADR-0149 default was a dependency CYCLE); `LogFilter` drops `PartialEq` as well as `Eq`

**Context.** ADR-0149 (PV-3) deferred the `envoy-accesslog`↔`envoy-config`
dependency posture to implementation time, with the stated DEFAULT: "add
`envoy-config` to `envoy-accesslog` if absent" so `LogFilter::Header` could carry
an `envoy_config::HeaderMatcher` directly. At implementation the ACTUAL
dependency direction was measured: **`envoy-config` already depends on
`envoy-accesslog`** (`crates/envoy-config/Cargo.toml:14`; load-bearing —
`envoy_accesslog::parse_format` compiles access-log format strings at
config-validation time, the ADR-0141 compiled-config posture). Therefore the
ADR-0149 default is a **dependency CYCLE** (`envoy-config → envoy-accesslog →
envoy-config`) and Cargo rejects it. ADR-0149 assumed the reverse edge.

**Decision — a trait-object seam (the PLAN's "Preferred" accesslog-owned type,
realized as a trait object, not a concrete re-model).**
- `envoy-accesslog` defines `pub trait HeaderMatch: Debug + Send + Sync { fn
  matches(&self, headers: &[(String, String)]) -> bool; }` and the arm
  `LogFilter::Header { matcher: Arc<dyn HeaderMatch> }`.
- `envoy-config` (which already depends on `envoy-accesslog`) provides `impl
  envoy_accesslog::HeaderMatch for HeaderMatcher` in `matcher.rs`, delegating to
  the inherent phase-04.2 `HeaderMatcher::matches` VERBATIM (method-call syntax
  gives the inherent method priority over the trait method — no recursion). This
  reuses the 7-mode engine with **ZERO matching duplication** and preserves PV-4
  (`mode_result ^ invert_match`, incl. absent+invert = KEEP) identically across
  the route and access-log paths.
- `envoy-http1`'s `compile_access_log_filter` boxes it: `LogFilter::Header {
  matcher: Arc::new(hf.header.clone()) }` (the matcher is cloned AFTER validate()
  compiled its SafeRegex, so `matches` never hits its `.expect()`).
- **`LogFilter` drops BOTH `Eq` AND `PartialEq`** (ADR-0149 PV-3 dropped only
  `Eq`). A trait object is not `PartialEq`-derivable, and NOTHING compares
  `LogFilter` values (grep-confirmed: no `==`/`assert_eq!`/set/map consumer;
  `FileSink`, the sole container, derives only `Debug`).

**Rejected alternatives.** (a) Add the reverse dep — a cycle, impossible. (b) A
concrete accesslog-owned `HeaderPredicate` re-modeling all 7 modes + StringMatcher
+ SafeRegex — adds a `regex` dep to `envoy-accesslog` and ~80 lines of matcher
duplication that must faithfully replicate the PV-4 XOR bug; strictly worse than
the trait seam (more code, more risk, no behavioral gain). (c) A closure/`Arc<dyn
Fn>` — same trait-object shape but less self-documenting; the named trait is
clearer.

**Consequences.** No new crate dependency (the trait seam is the whole point — it
avoids the cycle without a re-model). The `HeaderMatch` trait + impl are the only
net-new abstraction vs. ADR-0149's plan; every other PV-3 mechanic (widened
`should_log`/`FileSink::should_log`, the 3-arm `compile_access_log_filter`, both
HCM emit-gate threads, `&mut validate_access_logs`) lands unchanged. The
accesslog-side `should_log` `Header` test uses a local `HeaderMatch` stub (the
crate cannot construct a real `HeaderMatcher`); the real per-mode membership +
absent-drop coverage lives in `envoy-http1` (T9) + the `HeaderMatcher::matches`
engine's own phase-04.2 tests. `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` holds. **DECISIONS.md
ledger head: ADR-0150** (next-available **ADR-0151**). **Supersedes nothing;
RESOLVES the ADR-0149 PV-3 implementation-time dependency-posture question,
replacing its infeasible "add the dep" default.** ADR-0028 REMAINS OPEN; ADR-0049
governs; ADR-0140–0149 are NOT reopened.

- Date: 2026-07-20
- Status: accepted (phase-72 §5 state-3 implementation; `superpowers:executing-plans`). Resolves the ADR-0149 PV-3 deferred dependency-posture decision.

## ADR-0149: Phase-72 §5 state-2 PLAN-write — **§6.2 empirical reconciliation (PV-1..PV-7 resolutions)**; MEASURED that upstream drops absent+`invert_match` on BOTH the route AND access-log paths (a latent SHARED-engine bug → CF-72-1), name-only/`treat_missing_header_as_empty` inherited fail-loud boundaries (CF-72-2), and two implementation blockers the SPEC did not anticipate (the `LogFilter` `Eq` derive; the `&mut` compile path for the header_filter SafeRegex)

**Context.** The state-2 PLAN-write re-confirmed SPEC §3's PLAN-VERIFY items (PV-1..PV-7) against the LIVE tree (three read-only recon fan-outs — an in-tree config/runtime/HCM survey, a live-Envoy `--mode validate` + port-mapped route/access-log measurement, a differential-driver/fuzz/docs survey) and LIVE-MEASURED the two items the state-1 recon left as open PLAN-VERIFY questions (PV-4 the invert+absent divergence on the ROUTE path; PV-5 the name-only/`treat_missing_header_as_empty` wire acceptance). Two implementation blockers the state-1 SPEC did not anticipate surfaced from the in-tree survey (recorded below). `PLAN.md` authored (`docs/envoy-rust/phases/72-accesslog-header-filter/PLAN.md`, 12 TDD tasks); no code-tree change this session.

**MEASURED facts (this session, against `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0`).**
- **PV-4 (route path, NEW measurement):** a route with a header matcher `{ name: x-test, string_match: { exact: "blocked" }, invert_match: true }` listed first, a fallback second — `GET /` with the header ABSENT → the FALLBACK route (not the inverted route). So upstream ROUTE matching DROPS absent+invert, exactly like the access-log path (re-confirmed at runtime: absent+invert → not logged). The in-tree shared engine (`matcher.rs:51`) applies `mode_result ^ invert_match` UNCONDITIONALLY → absent+invert = KEEP. **This is therefore a latent bug on BOTH the route and access-log paths, not access-log-specific** — CORRECTING the SPEC §0/R-0.6 framing that treated it as an access-log-path gap.
- **PV-5 (`--mode validate`):** upstream ACCEPTS name-only `header: { name }` (presence), `present_match`, `string_match`, and `treat_missing_header_as_empty: true` (no warning); REJECTS empty `header_filter: {}` (`HeaderFilterValidationError.Header: value is required`); accepts flat `exact_match` with a deprecation warning. The in-tree `HeaderMatcher` deserializer REJECTS name-only ("missing mode key", `bootstrap.rs:3175`) and `treat_missing_header_as_empty` (unknown field, `bootstrap.rs:3168`).

**Decisions (PV-1..PV-7).**
- **PV-1 — `HeaderFilter` model + empty-`header` rejection.** Model `HeaderFilter { header: HeaderMatcher }` mirroring `StatusCodeFilter` — `#[derive(Debug, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq)]`, `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`, NO `Default`, `header` REQUIRED. Reuse the phase-04.2 `HeaderMatcher` (`bootstrap.rs:3022`, hand-rolled Deserialize/Serialize) verbatim. Empty `header_filter: {}` → the required-field serde error → **`ConfigError::Yaml`** (fail-loud; **NO new `ConfigError` variant** — ADR-0049 waives byte-parity vs upstream's `HeaderFilterValidationError.Header`). Per-arm validation delegates to the existing `validate_header_matcher` (`bootstrap.rs:5367`), which already checks empty name (`EmptyHeaderName`), compiles the SafeRegex (`InvalidRegex`), and validates the range (`InvalidInt64Range`).
- **PV-2 — 3-arm `set_arms` destructuring + M71-1/M71-4 folds.** Extend the compiler-forcing destructure `let AccessLogFilter { status_code_filter, response_flag_filter, header_filter } = filter;` (no `..`) and the `set_arms` array to 3 entries (`bootstrap.rs:5146`). Both `> 1` and `== 0` stay `AmbiguousAccessLogFilter { detail }`. **M71-1:** `rejects_access_log_filter_with_both_arms` now asserts `detail.contains("more than one")`; a NEW test pins cardinality-BEFORE-per-arm precedence (a both-arms + empty-name-header config fails on cardinality, not `EmptyHeaderName`). **M71-4:** refresh the `validate_access_logs` docstring (item 3 no longer calls the `>1` branch "unreachable"; add items for the `UnknownResponseFlag` token check and the header_filter matcher validation).
- **PV-3 — widen `should_log` (2nd time) + drop `Eq` + both HCM emit loops.** Widen to `should_log(&self, status: u16, response_flags: &str, headers: &[(String, String)]) -> bool` (+ the `FileSink::should_log` wrapper); the `Header` arm is `matcher.matches(headers)`. **BLOCKER #1 (SPEC did not anticipate):** `LogFilter` derives `Eq` (`filter.rs:23`) but `HeaderMatcher` is only `PartialEq` (it holds `SafeRegex`/`StringMatcher`), so a `HeaderMatcher`-carrying arm BREAKS the `Eq` derive → **DROP `Eq` from `LogFilter`** (grep-confirmed: no `LogFilter: Eq` consumer). Extend `compile_access_log_filter` (`hcm.rs:1735`) to a 3-tuple match adding `(None, None, Some(hf)) => LogFilter::Header { matcher: hf.header.clone() }` (the matcher is cloned AFTER validate() compiled its SafeRegex, so `matches` never hits its `.expect()`). Thread the in-scope downstream request headers: H1 `sink.should_log(record.response_code, &record.response_flags, &req.headers)` (`hcm.rs:1512`), H2 `&envoy_req.headers` (`crates/envoy-http2/src/hcm.rs:1135`); `compile_access_log_filter` has ONE definition (H2 shares it via `config.inner`). ~45 test call sites of `should_log` widen in lockstep (mechanical). The gate sees the downstream request headers as received; the opener's `x-log` is not a route-mutated header, so it is inert (confirm on both proxies at state-4). **BLOCKER #2 (SPEC did not anticipate):** `validate_access_logs` takes `&[AccessLog]` (immutable) but `validate_header_matcher` needs `&mut` to compile the SafeRegex → change `validate_access_logs` to `&mut [AccessLog]`; its SOLE caller `validate_hcm` (`bootstrap.rs:3822`) already holds `&mut hcm`, so the call becomes `validate_access_logs(&mut hcm.access_log)?`.
- **PV-4 — the `invert_match` + ABSENT divergence (HEADLINE) — MEASURED on BOTH paths; scope OUT + document + carry-forward.** Given the measurement (upstream drops absent+invert on route AND access-log; the in-tree shared engine keeps it on both), option (b) "model the access-log path's absent-under-invert explicitly" is REJECTED — it would fork the two paths' semantics while leaving route matching still buggy (worse). Option (c) "fix the shared engine now" is DEFERRED — it is a cross-cutting route+access-log change with a route-differential blast radius, outside arm #3's cheapest-strong scope. **CHOSEN: option (a)** — reuse `HeaderMatcher::matches` verbatim (the opener fixture `0078` uses a NON-inverted explicit-mode matcher), scope invert-under-absent OUT of the differential surface, document the shared-engine boundary in `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md` §C, pin the CURRENT (divergent) behavior in-process, and OPEN carry-forward **CF-72-1** (the shared-engine `matcher.rs:51` absent+invert fix; owner = a future phase touching `matcher.rs` with a route+access-log differential; touches the existing `invert_match_inverts_present_match_result` pin at `matcher.rs:373`).
- **PV-5 — name-only + `treat_missing_header_as_empty` load-parity — inherited fail-loud boundaries + carry-forward.** DECISION: inherit the phase-04.2 boundary for BOTH — keep them fail-loud (the shared `HeaderMatcher` deserializer rejects them; a route `HeaderMatcher` rejects them identically today) per the ADR-0049 posture (a config upstream accepts may be boot-fatal here — it never SILENTLY diverges). Do NOT touch the shared deserializer (route-parity blast radius; arm #3's scope is `header_filter`, not `HeaderMatcher` load-parity). The opener uses explicit `string_match: { exact }`. Pin the current rejection in-process (explicit tested decisions, not silent divergences); OPEN carry-forward **CF-72-2** (accept name-only → `PresentMatch(true)` + `treat_missing_header_as_empty`; owner = a future `HeaderMatcher`-parity phase).
- **PV-6 — §6.1 size re-derivation + §7.4.** Re-derived against the live tree at **~725 net LoC / 12 TDD tasks** (the ~45-call-site `should_log` widening is mechanical breadth folded into one task) → well under the ~1500 LoC / ~25 task gate → **NO SPLIT** (ADR-0150 stays UNFIRED). §7.4 = a NEW `parse_bootstrap` corpus seed `header_filter.yaml` + one `!`-un-ignore line in `crates/envoy-config/fuzz/.gitignore` — **NO new fuzz target, NO `ci.yml` edit** (ADR-0137 config-only-sub-message precedent; `parse_bootstrap` is the sole config fuzz target, CONFIRMED).
- **PV-7 — CF-71-1 sound closure + M71-2.** Land an ORDERING-AWARE settle in the byte-exact driver: a `suppression_settle(&[probes]) -> Duration` returning a long `CF71_1_SETTLE` (12s ≥ the ~10s FileAccessLog flush interval) when the LAST probe is DROPPED (fixture 0076's dropped-LAST shape — a bug-leaked line for the last record flushes only on Envoy's periodic timer, past the 2s `CF70_3_SETTLE`), else the cheap `CF70_3_SETTLE`; applied in both `run_http1_access_log_byte_exact_arm` and `run_http2_access_log_byte_exact_arm`. The `0078` opener orders kept-LAST (the already-sound short-settle case), so CF-71-1's long settle protects the pre-existing dropped-LAST `0076`. **M71-2:** fix the three stale "ordering witness" doc phrases — the `CF70_3_SETTLE` doc comment (`tests/differential/src/lib.rs:1679`), the `0077` integration-test module doc (`tests/differential/tests/access_log_response_flag_filter.rs:10`), and the `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md` §F phrase (line 2319). The `0077` README §"Ordering witness" already explains the retirement correctly and is NOT a target (per ADR-0147's enumeration). Surgical — do NOT disturb the 31 existing access-log fixtures.

**Carry-forward disposition.** CONSUMES **CF-71-1** (PV-7) + **M71-2** (three doc phrases); FOLDS **M71-1** (detail assert + precedence) + **M71-4** (docstring). **OPENS CF-72-1** (shared-engine absent+invert fix) + **CF-72-2** (name-only/treat-missing load-parity). NOT folded (weighed and deferred to keep scope surgical): **M71-3** (all-suppressed `expected_logged_count == 0` untested — needs a dedicated empty-log fixture, not cheap), **M71-5** (multi-sink mixed-filter composition untested — the 3-arm change makes it more relevant but it stays a carry-forward), **M70-R4/R9**, **M71-6/7/8**, **M69-A..I**, **CF-69-1/2/3/5**, **M68-1**, **M-1**, **CF-67-3/5/6/7**, the older Minors + the HTTP-filters-family (1)–(4).

**Consequences.** No code-tree change this state-2 session — `PLAN.md` authored (12 TDD tasks); this ADR fired; STATE advanced to state-3; ROADMAP row `72` UNCHANGED (no split → status stays `in-progress`; per invariant #2 the append-only summary cell is not rewritten). The state-3 implementation (`superpowers:subagent-driven-development`/`executing-plans`) is the NEXT session. `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` holds; NO new crate projected (the `envoy-accesslog`→`envoy-config` dependency posture is confirmed at implementation time — default: add the dep if absent, since re-modeling the 7-mode matcher would be pure duplication); NO new dependency beyond that, NO new fuzz target; **NO new `ConfigError` variant** (empty-`header` rides serde `Yaml`); ONE new config type (`HeaderFilter`); ONE new `LogFilter` variant (`Header`); the `should_log`/`FileSink::should_log` signatures widen by one `&[(String,String)]` param; `LogFilter` loses its `Eq` derive; `validate_access_logs` becomes `&mut`. **DECISIONS.md ledger head: ADR-0149** (next-available **ADR-0150**, reserved for the §6.1 split — NOT fired). **ADR-0028 REMAINS OPEN; ADR-0049 governs the config-validity fail-loud posture; ADR-0140/0141/0142/0143 (phase 70) + ADR-0144/0145/0146/0147 (phase 71) + ADR-0148 (the phase-72 pick) are NOT reopened.** The state-3 implementation is the next session.

- Date: 2026-07-20
- Status: accepted (phase-72 §5 state-2 PLAN-write; `superpowers:writing-plans`). Reserved by ADR-0148. **Supersedes NOTHING**; CORRECTS SPEC §0/R-0.6's "access-log-path-only" framing of the invert-absent gap with the MEASURED both-paths fact.

## ADR-0148: Phase-72 §5 state-1 brainstorm — pick the access-log FILTER arm #3, `header_filter`, over `and_filter`/`or_filter` and the §9 family openers

- Date: 2026-07-19
- Status: accepted
- Context: Phase 71 closed (ROADMAP rows `00`-`71` all `done`, STATE "awaiting next planning"), so this is the §5 state-0/1 next-phase pick (`superpowers:brainstorming`). The access-log FILTER subsystem (`envoy.config.accesslog.v3.AccessLogFilter`, the per-record log-emission oneof) now has TWO arms — `status_code_filter` (phase 70) and `response_flag_filter` (phase 71) — plus a runtime `should_log(status, response_flags)` seam threaded through both HCM emit loops, and a byte-exact `Http1AccessLogByteExact` differential driver whose `expect_logged` + `extra_headers` probe fields already exist. A next unit of progress must clear the cheapest-strong-differential bar (the phase-66/68/69/70/71 precedent). Two state-0 recon fan-outs ran this session against the pinned `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` (digest `sha256:56da5afd…770c2`): an in-tree feasibility survey and a live `--mode validate` + port-mapped runtime probe (graceful-stop flush).
- Options considered:
  - **`header_filter`** — the 3rd `AccessLogFilter` oneof arm (`HeaderFilter { header: envoy.config.route.v3.HeaderMatcher }`): gate a sink on whether a named REQUEST HEADER matches.
  - **`and_filter` / `or_filter`** — the recursive composition arms (`{ filters: repeated AccessLogFilter }`, MEASURED PGV `min_items = 2`).
  - **`duration_filter`** — timing-based; the differential needs latency bounds and is flaky.
  - **The standalone H2 access-log-filter differential** (the deferred M71-6).
  - **Each §9 family opener** (network-filter payload codecs, `sni_cluster`, non-deterministic LB, HTTP/3+QUIC, gRPC bridge/transcoding, observability SINKS, runtime/RTDS, hot-restart, WASM host).
- Decision: Phase 72 = `72-accesslog-header-filter`: land `AccessLogFilter.header_filter` (arm #3) end-to-end, behaviorally equivalent to `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0`. Add a `HeaderFilter { header: HeaderMatcher }` config type REUSING the existing phase-04.2 `HeaderMatcher` (`bootstrap.rs:3025`) + its 7-mode `matches(&[(String,String)])` engine (`matcher.rs:21`) verbatim; `header` is PGV-required (empty `header_filter: {}` fail-loud, MEASURED R-0.2). Extend the `set_arms` cardinality destructuring (`bootstrap.rs:5148`) + the `compile_access_log_filter` match (`hcm.rs:1742`) from 2 to 3 arms (compiler-forced). Add a `LogFilter::Header { matcher }` runtime variant and WIDEN `should_log` a SECOND time to also carry the request-header slice (the one new seam — the same class of change phase 71 performed once); thread the already-in-scope `req.headers` / `envoy_req.headers` at BOTH HCM emit gates. Witness byte-exact by NEW fixture `0078` (an H1 HCM with a `header_filter { header: { name: "x-log", string_match: { exact: "yes" } } }` file access log + one `direct_response` route → `GET /x` with `x-log: yes` KEPT, mismatch/absent DROPPED → a single byte-identical `STATUS=200 PATH=/x H=yes` line, NO backend). CONSUME CF-71-1 (ordering-aware settle ≥ the ~10s flush interval for dropped-LAST suppression fixtures) + M71-2 (the three stale "ordering witness" doc phrases); cheaply FOLD M71-1 (assert `detail` on the cardinality test + precedence) + M71-4 (validator docstring). Full scope, PLAN-VERIFY items, and rejected-alternative detail live in `docs/envoy-rust/phases/72-accesslog-header-filter/SPEC.md`.
- Rationale: `header_filter` is the cheapest arm-#3 leaf that also lights up a genuinely NEW observable axis (request-header membership). The two expensive pieces already exist and are reusable verbatim — the `HeaderMatcher` type + its full matching engine (MEASURED in-tree: zero new matching logic) and the request headers in scope at both emit gates (MEASURED: no new `AccessLogRecord` field, no new capture plumbing) — and the differential probe already carries `extra_headers` + `expect_logged`, so the fixture is pure YAML. It yields a deterministic BACKEND-FREE byte-exact single-line observable, and this phase (touching both the differential driver and the access-log-filter surface) is the designated owner of CF-71-1 + M71-2. `and_filter`/`or_filter` add a RECURSIVE config type for a composition of already-covered predicates — a natural NEXT leaf now that 3 arms exist, but less new observable value; `duration_filter` is timing-flaky; the standalone H2 differential is weak; each §9 opener is a large new subsystem far above the cheapest-strong bar. The state-0 recon also surfaced load-bearing PLAN-VERIFY subtleties that make this a substantive (not rubber-stamp) pick: the shared engine's `mode_result ^ invert_match` gives absent+invert = KEEP but upstream access-log = DROP (MEASURED R-0.4/R-0.6), and the existing `HeaderMatcher` deserializer rejects name-only `{name}` and `treat_missing_header_as_empty` that upstream accepts — each an explicit PV-4/PV-5 decision at state-2.
- Consequences: No code changes this state-1 session (SPEC + ADR + ROADMAP row `72` `in-progress` + STATE advance only). The state-2 PLAN-write (`superpowers:writing-plans`) runs the §6.2 empirical reconciliation (PV-1..PV-7 — the `HeaderFilter` serde model + empty-`header` rejection, the 3-arm destructuring + M71-1/M71-4, the 2nd `should_log` widening + the 3-arm compile match + both emit loops, the invert-absent divergence decision, the name-only / treat-missing parity decision, the CF-71-1 sound closure) and authors `PLAN.md`. New ROADMAP row `72` lands `in-progress` (depends-on `06 32 70 71`). **ADR-0149 reserved** for the §6.2 reconciliation; **ADR-0150 reserved** for the §6.1 split (very unlikely — a ~640-LoC single-phase leaf). CONSUMES CF-71-1 + M71-2; FOLDS M71-1 + M71-4; OPENS the PV-4 invert-absent + PV-5 name-only/treat-missing parity questions. NOT consumed (still live): M71-3/5/6/7/8, M70-R4/R9, M69-A..I, CF-69-1/2/3/5, M68-1, M-1, CF-67-3/5/6/7, the older Minors + the HTTP-filters-family (1)–(4). **ADR-0028 REMAINS OPEN** (`runtime_key` + the 23 inert `response_flag_filter` tokens stay RTDS-inert); ADR-0049 governs the config-validity fail-loud posture; ADR-0016/0124/0131/0133/0136/0137/0139/0140-0147 preserved. **DECISIONS.md ledger head: ADR-0148** (next-available **ADR-0149**, reserved). `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` holds. The state-2 PLAN-write is the next session.

## ADR-0147: Phase-71 §5 state-5 code-review — **ADR-0146's settle-soundness rationale is MEASURED-FALSE for the REFERENCE side of dropped-LAST suppression fixtures** (live `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` flushes two back-to-back records in DIFFERENT batches ~10s apart — line 1 at t≈0.01s, line 2 at t≈10.05s — NOT "the SAME flush"); the CF-70-3 closure is RE-SCOPED, not reopened: **SOUND for the SUBJECT side on ALL orderings** (envoy-rust writes per-record immediately, so any leaked line is on disk before `wait_file_lines` returns and the exact count-equality catches it) **and for the REFERENCE side on kept-LAST orderings** (fixture 0077 — a leaked line would be the FIRST record, flushed near-instantly, so the byte-compare mismatches); the residual reference-side window on dropped-last shapes (fixture 0076) bites ONLY at fixture-authoring / pin-refresh time (the reference is the ORACLE whose suppression was live-verified at authoring via graceful-stop); future suppression fixtures SHOULD order kept-last AND authors MUST verify reference-side suppression via graceful-stop or a ≥flush-interval wait; an ordering-aware driver hardening (settle ≥ the ~10s flush interval for dropped-last suppression fixtures) is **carry-forward CF-71-1**; **NO code change owed**

- **Date:** 2026-07-19.
- **Status:** accepted (phase-71 §5 state-5 code-review; `superpowers:requesting-code-review`). **Supersedes the SOUNDNESS-CLAIM of ADR-0146 only** ("The settle is sound for BOTH probe orderings") — the retirement of the hard ordering-witness assertion, the settle mechanism itself, and CF-70-3's closure for the subject-under-test all STAND. ADR-0127 governs why this review is a separate context from the implementing one.

**Context.** The state-5 review's live measurement (this session, port-mapped `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0`, an unfiltered file sink, two back-to-back HTTP requests, per-second file polling) observed: line 1 on disk at **t≈0.012s**, line 2 at **t≈10.05s**. Upstream's FileAccessLog therefore does NOT batch two back-to-back records into one flush — the first write flushes near-immediately and the second waits the full ~10s `file_flush_interval` tick. ADR-0146's rationale — "upstream Envoy flushes its whole buffer atomically, so a leaked line lands in the SAME flush as the kept lines (both probes are driven back-to-back before any `wait_file_lines`)" — is measured-false: back-to-back records land in DIFFERENT flushes as the DEFAULT behavior, not a rare timer-split race. (This also retro-explains SPEC R-0.5's own control: "the 2nd line only at ~t+12s".)

**Consequence analysis (what the 2s settle actually guarantees).** The differential's job is detecting SUBJECT (envoy-rust) divergence. (a) **Subject side, all orderings: SOUND.** envoy-rust writes per-record immediately (no flush batching — the very fact ADR-0146 already relied on), so an envoy-rust-leaked line is on disk before `wait_file_lines(expected)` returns and the exact count-equality (`lib.rs:6395`/`6403` region) rejects it; the settle is not even needed for this class. (b) **Reference side, kept-LAST orderings (0077): SOUND.** A reference-side extra line would be the FIRST record, flushed near-instantly; `wait_file_lines` sees it and the byte-compare mismatches. (c) **Reference side, dropped-LAST orderings (0076): NOT closed by the 2s settle.** A reference-side extra line would be the SECOND record, flushing at ~t+10s — after the 2s settle expires. This window matters only when the reference's behavior differs from what the fixture author measured — i.e. at fixture-AUTHORING time or a D-3.7 pin-refresh re-baselining — because within a pinned CI, the oracle's suppression behavior is a constant that was live-verified when the fixture landed (0076: phase-70 ADR-0140 recon; 0077: this phase's R-0.4 graceful-stop witness).

**Decision.** (1) ADR-0146's "sound for BOTH probe orderings" claim is NARROWED as titled; the settle mechanism, the assertion retirement, and the subject-side CF-70-3 closure stand unchanged — **no code change owed**, the phase is NOT reopened. (2) **Authoring convention (binding on future suppression fixtures):** order kept probes LAST where the scenario permits, and in ALL cases verify the reference side's suppression at authoring via graceful-stop (`docker stop`, SIGTERM drain) or a ≥flush-interval wait — never trust a short-budget read for the reference's dropped half. (3) **CF-71-1 (carry-forward, owner = the next phase touching the differential driver or adding a suppression fixture):** optionally harden the driver with an ordering-aware settle — when `has_suppression` and the LAST probe is NOT `expect_logged`, extend the settle past the ~10s flush interval (≈12s) so the reference side is settle-covered on dropped-last shapes too; cost ≈ +12s per such fixture run (today: 0076 only).

**Consequences.** Docs-only (this ADR + `REVIEW.md`); the stale "ordering witness (primary soundness guarantee)" doc comment on `CF70_3_SETTLE` (`tests/differential/src/lib.rs:1677-1680`) and its two echoes (the 0077 integration-test doc comment; the `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md` §F "as the CF-70-3 ordering witness" phrase) are Minor doc corrections folded into CF-71-1's owner (M71-2). **DECISIONS.md ledger head: ADR-0147** (this ADR; next-available **ADR-0148**). ADR-0028 REMAINS OPEN; ADR-0049 governs config-validity; ADR-0144/0145/0146 otherwise stand. `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` holds.

## ADR-0146: Phase-71 §5 state-3 implementation — **RETIRE the ADR-0145 PV-7 hard "last probe must be KEPT" ordering-witness assertion (incompatible with the pre-existing dropped-last fixture 0076); the bounded settle is the ordering-agnostic CF-70-3 closure**

**Context.** ADR-0145 PV-7 specified closing CF-70-3 (the FileAccessLog ~10s async-flush false-pass window) with TWO mechanisms in the byte-exact differential driver: (1) a "primary" ordering-witness — a hard `assert!` that a suppression fixture's LAST probe has `expect_logged == true` (the rationale: FileAccessLog flushes in request order, so once the kept LAST line is on disk, every earlier record — including any leaked one — has ALSO flushed, making the exact count-equality sound WITHOUT a settle); and (2) a "defense-in-depth" bounded settle (re-read both files after `CF70_3_SETTLE` and reject any growth past the kept-line count). The T7 implementation (commit `9bf5a41`) added BOTH to both arms, gated on `has_suppression = expected_lines < probes.len()`. The plan asserted "the 30 existing all-kept fixtures see ZERO change."

**Problem (CI-caught, state-3 head `c2efbd0`, run `29668532521`).** That premise was FALSE: the phase-70 fixture **0076** (`0076-accesslog-status-code-filter`) is itself a SUPPRESSION fixture — probe 1 `GET /log` → 503 KEPT (`expect_logged: true`), probe 2 `GET /nolog` → 200 DROPPED (`expect_logged: false`) — with the DROPPED probe LAST. So `has_suppression` is true for 0076, and the hard ordering-witness `assert!` (LAST probe must be kept) PANICS on it (`tests/differential/src/lib.rs:6275`). The state-3 T12 dry-run ran `cargo test --workspace --lib --bins`, which EXCLUDES the differential integration-test binaries, so the regression surfaced only at the state-3 CI push, not locally. Reproduced deterministically locally (`cargo test -p differential --test access_log_status_code_filter` → the same panic).

**Options.** (a) REORDER 0076 to kept-last — REJECTED: 0076 is a landed phase-70 fixture; the standing traps forbid disturbing the access-log fixtures, and reordering changes a witnessed byte-exact artifact. (b) Keep the assert but exempt 0076 — REJECTED: a special-case allowlist is fragile and the assert adds nothing 0076 needs. (c) **RETIRE the hard ordering-witness assertion; keep the bounded settle as the sole, ordering-AGNOSTIC CF-70-3 closure — CHOSEN.**

**Decision.** Remove the `assert!(probes.last()…expect_logged…)` precondition from BOTH `run_http1_access_log_byte_exact_arm` and `run_http2_access_log_byte_exact_arm`; retain the `has_suppression`-gated bounded settle (both proxies still live: sleep `CF70_3_SETTLE`, re-read both files, `bail!` if either grew past `expected_lines`). The settle is sound for BOTH probe orderings: envoy-rust writes per-record immediately, so a leaked line is present before the settle even starts; upstream Envoy flushes its whole buffer atomically, so a leaked line lands in the SAME flush as the kept lines (both probes are driven back-to-back before any `wait_file_lines`), which the settle observes. This is a STRICT improvement over phase 70 (which had NO settle and passed 0076 anyway). Fixtures MAY still author kept-last (0077 does) but it is no longer ENFORCED. This SUPERSEDES ADR-0145 PV-7's ordering-witness-assertion mechanism ONLY; CF-70-3's closure (now via the settle) and every other ADR-0145 resolution stand.

**Consequences.** Both `0076` (regression fixed) and `0077` (new) differentials green locally after the fix. No schema/runtime/config change — driver-only. `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` holds. This is a state-3 correction (the implementation was defective; §5.2 in spirit — the fix stays within the state-3 session that authored the defect, re-verified before advancing). **DECISIONS.md ledger head: ADR-0146** (this ADR; next-available **ADR-0147**). ADR-0028 REMAINS OPEN; ADR-0049 governs config-validity. `CF-70-1` + `M70-R1` + `CF-70-3` + `M70-R2` remain discharged by phase 71.
