## ADR-0145: Phase-71 §5 state-2 PLAN-write — **§6.2 empirical reconciliation (PV-1..PV-7 resolutions) + a MEASURED token-count correction to ADR-0144**

**Context.** The state-2 PLAN-write re-confirmed SPEC §3's PLAN-VERIFY items (PV-1..PV-7) against the LIVE tree (three read-only recon fan-outs — config surface, runtime/HCM surface, differential-driver+fuzz surface) and LIVE-MEASURED the two items the state-0/1 recon left open (PV-6 empty-`flags` runtime semantics; the exact accepted-token set). One load-bearing correction to ADR-0144 emerged (the token COUNT), and PV-6 resolved a previously-unmeasured runtime behavior.

**MEASURED CORRECTION to ADR-0144 (the token set).** ADR-0144 / ROADMAP row `71` / STATE.md all state the `response_flag_filter.flags` PGV `in`-list has **30 tokens** (23-of-which... "24 parsed-but-inert"). That is an off-by-one transcription error in the state-1 brainstorm. This session RE-MEASURED the authoritative rejection message from `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` (`--mode validate` on a `flags: ["ZZZ_BOGUS"]`): `value must be in list [LH UH UT LR UR UF UC UO NR DI FI RL UAEX RLSE DC URX SI IH DPE UMSDR RFCF NFCF DT UPE NC OM DF DO DR]` — **exactly 29 tokens** (verified by `wc -w`). Of those, envoy-rust produces **6** (`NR UH UO UC UF URX` — all present in the list), leaving **23 parsed-but-inert** (NOT 24). **The validator, PLAN.md, and `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md` use 29 / 6 / 23.** ADR-0144's pick + scope decision is otherwise UNAFFECTED — only its "30-token" / "24-inert" count is corrected here (append-only: ADR-0144 is not edited; this ADR narrows the fact).

**Decisions (PV-1..PV-7).**
- **PV-1 — `ResponseFlagFilter` model + token validator.** Model as `ResponseFlagFilter { flags: Vec<String> }` (`#[serde(default, deny_unknown_fields)]`, derive `Default`) — a VALIDATED string membership set, NOT a 29-variant `ResponseFlag` enum. The `ComparisonOp` type-safe-enum precedent is deliberately NOT mirrored: 23 of 29 tokens are inert, so a per-variant enum buys almost no type-safety while adding 29 renamed variants; a validated `Vec<String>` matches the "parsed-but-inert" posture and keeps membership a direct string compare. The new arm `pub response_flag_filter: Option<ResponseFlagFilter>` is added to `AccessLogFilter` (`bootstrap.rs:713-723`). A new `ConfigError::UnknownResponseFlag { token: String }` (message `"response_flag_filter flags must be a known response-flag token: {token}"`, the `AmbiguousLogFormat`/`{detail}` interpolation convention) is raised by a token-membership check against a `const RESPONSE_FLAG_TOKENS: [&str; 29]`, attached in `validate_access_logs` (`bootstrap.rs:5109`+) as a sibling to the phase-70 `runtime_key` check (`bootstrap.rs:5131-5135`).
- **PV-2 — `set_arms` destructuring (M70-R1).** Replace the one-element array (`bootstrap.rs:5118-5121`) with a compiler-forcing struct destructuring `let AccessLogFilter { status_code_filter, response_flag_filter } = filter;` (no `..` — a future 3rd arm fails to compile until the count is updated), then `let set_arms = [status_code_filter.is_some(), response_flag_filter.is_some()].iter().filter(|s| **s).count();`. The `== 0` branch (`"no filter variant is set"`) is unchanged; the `else` branch (`"more than one filter variant is set"`) is now REACHABLE (R-0.3: upstream rejects a `filter` carrying both arms). The over-claiming doc comment is fixed. The `runtime_key` check and the new `response_flag_filter` token check both consume the destructured bindings.
- **PV-3 — widen `should_log` + 2-arm compile match (CF-70-1) + both HCM loops.** Widen the signature to **`should_log(&self, status: u16, response_flags: &str) -> bool`** — NOT `&AccessLogRecord`. Rationale: both current arms need only these two scalars; passing `&AccessLogRecord` (owned by `envoy-accesslog`, so accessible) would force every unit-test call site to construct a full record for no present benefit; a future arm needing a 3rd field re-widens cheaply (internal crate API). `FileSink::should_log` (`file_sink.rs:99-106`) widens in lockstep. `compile_access_log_filter` (`envoy-http1/src/hcm.rs:1736-1757`) drops the zero-arm `expect()` for a full `match (&f.status_code_filter, &f.response_flag_filter)` with two real arms + an `unreachable!("validated: exactly one filter arm is set")` for the validated-away 0/2 cases. Both emit-loop call sites thread the token: H1 `hcm.rs:1512` and H2 `hcm.rs:1135` change `sink.should_log(record.response_code)` → `sink.should_log(record.response_code, &record.response_flags)` (the record already carries the FINAL single token at both gates — H1 builds it at `hcm.rs:1649-1661`, H2 at `hcm.rs:1084-1104`; 7 outcomes `URX UF NR UH UO UC` + `-`). Test-only call sites updated in lockstep (`envoy-http1/src/hcm.rs` ~4619/4820-4925; `file_sink.rs` ~352-361).
- **PV-4 — membership + `-` sentinel.** For a non-empty `flags`, match = `flags.iter().any(|f| f == response_flags)` over the SINGLE rendered token (CONFIRMED single/brace-free). The `-` no-flag sentinel ∉ the 29-token set, so a non-empty `flags` never matches a `-` record (R-0.4). The `LogFilter::ResponseFlag { flags: Vec<String> }` runtime variant is added (`filter.rs:21-26`).
- **PV-5 — size + §7.4.** §6.1 re-derived at **~645 net LoC / ~13 TDD tasks** → well under the ~1500 LoC / ~25 task gate → **NO SPLIT** (ADR-0146 stays UNFIRED). §7.4 = a NEW `parse_bootstrap` corpus seed `response_flag_filter.yaml` + one `!`-un-ignore line in `crates/envoy-config/fuzz/.gitignore` — **NO new fuzz target, NO `ci.yml` edit** (`parse_bootstrap` is the sole config fuzz target; CONFIRMED).
- **PV-6 — empty-`flags` semantics (LIVE-MEASURED this session, port-mapped against v1.33.0, graceful-stop flush).** `flags: []` (empty list) AND `response_flag_filter: {}` (absent `flags`) BOTH parse, BOTH are ACTIVE, and BOTH have IDENTICAL runtime semantics: **a record matches iff it has ANY response flag set** — the no-route 404 `NR` is KEPT, the clean `direct_response` 503 `-` is DROPPED (the no-`filter` control kept BOTH lines; the `flags: ["NR"]` control kept only `NR`). This is upstream's documented "if empty, matches any response flag set." Modeled at runtime as: `if flags.is_empty() { response_flags != "-" } else { flags.iter().any(|f| f == response_flags) }`. LOAD-PARITY requires envoy-rust to ACCEPT empty/absent `flags` (never reject) and honor the "any flag set" semantics. In `serde` the empty/absent case both deserialize to an empty `Vec` (via `#[serde(default)]`), so the runtime handles them uniformly.
- **PV-7 — CF-70-3 sound closure (ordering witness).** The FileAccessLog ~10s async-flush batch (R-0.5) makes a naive short-budget check false-pass a merely-un-flushed record as "suppressed." SOUND closure = an **ordering witness** in the differential driver, applied ONLY when suppression is present (`expected_logged_count(probes) < probes.len()`): (a) assert the LAST probe is `expect_logged: true` (bail otherwise); because FileAccessLog flushes in REQUEST ORDER, once the final (kept) record's line is on disk — which the existing `wait_file_lines(expected_lines)` (`lib.rs:6311`/`6328`, budget `ACCESS_LOG_FLUSH_WAIT`=15s) already waits for — every earlier record that was NOT suppressed has ALSO flushed, so the EXISTING exact count-equality (`envoy_lines.len() == expected_lines`, `lib.rs:6355`/`6363`) SOUNDLY rejects a bug-emitted un-suppressed line instead of false-passing on an un-flushed one; (b) a bounded suppression-only "no extra line appears within a short settle" re-check is added as defense-in-depth. Both guards are gated on `has_suppression`, so the 30 existing byte-exact access-log fixtures (all `expect_logged: true` → no suppression) see ZERO timing/behavior change. Fixture `0077` drives the dropped `/direct` 503 FIRST and the kept `/nowhere` 404 LAST (satisfying the ordering witness). Applied to BOTH `run_http1_access_log_byte_exact_arm` and `run_http2_access_log_byte_exact_arm`. **M70-R2** (the `expected_logged_count` helper has no in-process witness) is cheaply FOLDED IN here (a unit test on the helper); **M70-R4** (`"filter": null` serialization) and **M70-R9** are NOT folded (carry forward).

**Consequences.** No code-tree change this state-2 session — `PLAN.md` authored (`docs/envoy-rust/phases/71-accesslog-response-flag-filter/PLAN.md`, ~13 TDD tasks); this ADR fired; STATE advanced; ROADMAP row `71` UNCHANGED (no split → status stays `in-progress`, and per invariant #2 the append-only summary cell is not rewritten — the "30-token"/"24-inert" wording there is a landed narrative superseded on that narrow fact by this ADR's MEASURED 29/6/23). The state-3 implementation (`superpowers:subagent-driven-development`/`executing-plans`) is the NEXT session. `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` holds; NO new crate/dependency/fuzz-target projected; ONE new `ConfigError` variant (`UnknownResponseFlag`); ONE new `LogFilter` variant (`ResponseFlag`); the `should_log`/`FileSink::should_log` signatures widen by one `&str` param. **DECISIONS.md ledger head: ADR-0145** (next-available **ADR-0146**, reserved for the §6.1 split — NOT fired). **ADR-0028 REMAINS OPEN; ADR-0049 governs the config-validity all-fatal posture; ADR-0140/0141/0142/0143 govern the phase-70 access-log-filter opener and are NOT reopened.** The state-3 implementation is the next session.

## ADR-0144: Phase-71 pick + scope — **land the SECOND `AccessLogFilter` oneof arm, `response_flag_filter`** (`envoy.config.accesslog.v3.AccessLogFilter.response_flag_filter`), the cheapest-strong-differential arm-#2 leaf of the access-log FILTER subsystem phase 70 opened: a per-`AccessLog`-sink predicate that emits a record ONLY IF the record's `%RESPONSE_FLAGS%` token ∈ the configured `flags` list, reusing the ENTIRE phase-70 `filter` seam (the `AccessLog.filter` oneof, the `should_log` per-sink gate in BOTH HCM emit loops, the byte-exact `Driver::Http1AccessLogByteExact` differential driver + its EXISTING `expect_logged` probe field — NO harness change for the positive witness) AND the mature `%RESPONSE_FLAGS%` derivation (phases 48–65, which ALREADY renders `NR` byte-exact) — adding only a `ResponseFlagFilter { flags: [<30-token PGV set>] }` schema + the `response_flag_filter: Option<ResponseFlagFilter>` oneof arm, a token-membership validator (`BOGUS`/lowercase fail-loud; all 30 upstream-accepted tokens accepted for LOAD-PARITY, of which envoy-rust produces only `{NR, UH, UO, UC, UF, URX}` — the other 24 parsed-but-inert like phase-70's `runtime_key`), a `LogFilter::ResponseFlag` runtime variant with a WIDENED `should_log` signature (the one genuinely-new seam: it must see `record.response_flags`, not just the status), and threading BOTH HCM emit loops; witnessed byte-exact by a NEW fixture `0077` (an H1 HCM with a `response_flag_filter { flags: ["NR"] }` file access log + one `direct_response` route + a no-route probe → the 404 `NR` line is KEPT, the 503 `-` line is SUPPRESSED → a single byte-identical log line, NO backend — a strictly STRONGER witness than phase 70 whose kept line carried the `-` sentinel); landing arm #2 DISCHARGES the two deferred arm-#2 obligations **CF-70-1** (the `compile_access_log_filter` zero-arm `expect()` at `envoy-http1/src/hcm.rs:1742` → a full 2-arm match) + **M70-R1** (the hand-maintained one-element `set_arms` cardinality array at `envoy-config/src/bootstrap.rs:5118` → a compiler-forcing destructuring, its over-claiming `> 1` branch now reachable) AND CLOSES **CF-70-3** (the `wait_file_lines` false-pass-only window — empirically reproduced this session as FileAccessLog's ~10s async-flush batch; phase 71 is "the next access-log-filter phase" designated to harden the suppression assertion); choose `response_flag_filter` over `header_filter` (needs the full `HeaderMatcher` config surface — larger schema) / `duration_filter` (timing-flaky) / `and_filter`+`or_filter` (recursive, heavier) / the standalone H2 access-log-filter differential (codec-agnostic, weak alone) / the re-weighed phase-70 rejects (outlier `consecutive_local_origin_failure`, CB `max_pending_requests>0`, the `upstream_rq_overflow` rename, retry `retriable_headers`) / every §9 family opener (network-filter codecs, `sni_cluster`, non-deterministic LB, HTTP/3+QUIC, gRPC bridge/transcoding, observability SINKS, runtime/RTDS, hot-restart, WASM host — each a large new subsystem far above the cheapest-strong bar)

- **Date:** 2026-07-18.
- **Status:** accepted (phase-71 §5 state-0/1 next-phase PICK; `superpowers:brainstorming`). Reclaims the UNRESERVED ledger-head slot (previous head ADR-0143). **Supersedes NOTHING.**

**Context.** ROADMAP rows `00`-`70` were all `done` (`59`/`60`/`62` intentional gaps), STATE `awaiting next planning` — the §5 state-0/1 pick session (memory `closeout-and-pick-are-separate-sessions`). Phase 70 opened the access-log FILTER subsystem (`AccessLogFilter` oneof) with arm #1 `status_code_filter`, and its `REVIEW.md` §9.5 attached two arm-#2 obligations (CF-70-1 + M70-R1) to WHICHEVER future phase lands the second oneof arm, plus CF-70-3 (the flush false-pass window) to "the next access-log-filter phase." The state-0 recon (two read-only fan-outs — one in-tree code survey, one live-Envoy `--mode validate` + port-mapped runtime probe against `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0`) MEASURED: (R-0.1) the greenfield seam — `AccessLogFilter` is an Option-per-variant struct whose doc comment invites arm #2; the zero-arm `expect()` at `hcm.rs:1742`; the `should_log(status: u16)` at `envoy-accesslog/src/filter.rs:32` that takes ONLY the status (must widen); the `set_arms` array at `bootstrap.rs:5118`; the `expect_logged` driver already present; and the exact 6-token `%RESPONSE_FLAGS%` vocabulary envoy-rust emits (`NR, UH, UO, UC, UF, URX`, single token, brace-free); (R-0.2) the wire shape — `response_flag_filter { flags: [...] }` accepted, the PGV `in`-list is exactly 30 tokens, `BOGUS`/lowercase rejected, `flags: []`/absent-`flags` accepted, multiple/duplicate accepted; (R-0.3) `response_flag_filter` + `status_code_filter` together REJECTED (mutually-exclusive oneof arms); (R-0.4) the backend-free runtime witness — `flags:["NR"]` keeps the no-route 404 `NR`, drops the clean `direct_response` 503 `-`; `flags:["UH"]` empties the log; no-filter logs both; (R-0.5) the FileAccessLog ~10s async-flush batch confound (the CF-70-3 mechanism). Full evidence in `docs/envoy-rust/phases/71-accesslog-response-flag-filter/SPEC.md` §0.

**Decision.** Phase 71 = `71-accesslog-response-flag-filter`: land the `response_flag_filter` oneof arm end-to-end (schema + token validator + `LogFilter::ResponseFlag` + widened `should_log` + both HCM emit loops + fixture `0077` + in-process coverage + `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md` subsection), discharging CF-70-1 + M70-R1 and closing CF-70-3. The match is a token-membership test (`flags.contains(record.response_flags)`); the 24 unproduced tokens are parsed-but-inert (load-parity); the empty-`flags` semantics is a PLAN-write live-measurement (PV-6). NO new crate/dependency; NO new fuzz TARGET (a `parse_bootstrap` corpus-seed edit, ADR-0137 precedent); ONE new `ConfigError::UnknownResponseFlag`; the `AmbiguousAccessLogFilter` cardinality variant REUSED across 2 arms.

**Rejected alternatives.** `header_filter` (reuses the phase-04.2 header matcher but needs the full `HeaderMatcher` config surface — materially larger schema, and no cheaper on the arm-#2 obligations); `duration_filter` (timing-based → flaky differential); `and_filter`/`or_filter` (recursive `AccessLogFilter` — heavier; a natural phase now that arm #2 makes 2 leaf arms); the standalone H2 access-log-filter differential (codec-agnostic gate, byte-identical composition — weak alone; fold into a future H2 fixture set); and the re-weighed phase-70 rejects + every §9 family opener (each a large new subsystem). `response_flag_filter` is the cheapest arm-#2 leaf: it reuses the phase-70 seam + the already-byte-exact `NR` derivation, needs the driver UNCHANGED for its positive witness, yields a deterministic backend-free byte-exact single line whose KEPT record carries a NON-trivial flag (`NR`), and clears three carry-forwards.

**§6.1 split — NOT projected to fire (ADR-0146 reserved as a formality).** §8 re-estimate ~630 net LoC / ~10–13 tasks (lighter than phase 70 ~670 — the `expect_logged` driver field already exists and there is no new codec/primitive). PV-5 re-derives at the state-2 PLAN-write; **ADR-0146 reserved** for the (unlikely) split.

**Consequences.** No code changes this state-0/1 session (SPEC + ADR + ROADMAP row `71` `in-progress` + STATE only). The state-2 PLAN-write (`superpowers:writing-plans`) runs the §6.2 recon (PV-1..PV-7: the serde model + token validator, the `set_arms` destructuring, the widened `should_log` + the 2-arm compile match + both emit loops, the membership/`-` semantics, the empty-`flags` live-measurement, the CF-70-3 sound closure) and authors `PLAN.md`. New ROADMAP row `71` lands `in-progress` (depends-on `06 32 70`). This pick CONSUMES CF-70-1 + M70-R1 (arm-#2 obligations) and CLOSES CF-70-3; M70-R2/R4/R9 + M69-A..I + CF-69-1/2/3/5 + M68-1 + M-1 + CF-67-3/5/6/7 + the older Minors + HTTP-filters-family (1)–(4) stay live. `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` holds. **DECISIONS.md ledger head: ADR-0144** (this ADR; next-available **ADR-0145**, reserved for the §6.2 reconciliation; **ADR-0146** reserved for the §6.1 split). **ADR-0014 REMAINS IN FORCE; ADR-0028 REMAINS OPEN; ADR-0049 governs** the config-validity all-fatal posture; ADR-0140/0141/0142/0143 (phase 70) unmodified. The state-2 PLAN-write is the next session.

## ADR-0143: Phase-70 §5 state-4 re-verification (2nd) — **the gate-(b) decisive numeric cross-check (`local passed+failed == CI passed`) is unobtainable while the host's GitHub credential is invalid** (GitHub serves Actions run/job logs ONLY to authenticated users — the run-level API, the job-level API, and the web UI's per-step AJAX endpoints all refuse anonymous access on this public repo); for THIS verification an equivalent-strength substitute is accepted: CI `success` on the SAME full SHA (both jobs healthy, steps 15/13 — not runner starvation) **+** a diff-counted test-set reconciliation (**exactly +1 / −0 test functions** vs the parent tree whose identity was twice measured at 2022, with `tests/` carrying ZERO diff) **+** the local enumeration `2017 passed + 6 failed = 2023` matching the predicted total exactly; **the numeric log-derived identity remains the standard protocol** whenever a valid credential exists, and the human must restore it (`gh auth login`)

- **Date:** 2026-07-17.
- **Status:** accepted (phase-70 §5 state-4 RE-VERIFICATION (2nd); `superpowers:verification-before-completion`). **Supersedes NOTHING**; scoped to the evidence protocol of THIS state-4 verdict (and any future verification facing the same credential outage), NOT a weakening of the identity protocol itself.

**Context.** The §7.5 gate-(b) adjudication protocol (in force since the phase-70 §V sweep and prescribed by the session handoff) ends with a decisive numeric cross-check: `local passed + failed == CI passed` on the same SHA, derived by grepping the CI run log's `test result:` lines. This session measured every other leg of the gate over `60a5272e0bb55ee06fa39e35e6069d8d3e234dfe` (CI run `29596323921`, `completed`/`success`, confirmed on the FULL 40-char SHA), but the log grep failed: `gh run view --log` and `gh api …/runs/<id>/logs` and `gh api …/jobs/<id>/logs` all return **HTTP 403 "Must have admin rights to Repository"**, because `gh auth status` reports **"The token in default is invalid"** (expired/revoked; `GITHUB_TOKEN` in the environment is empty). Public READ endpoints (`gh run list`, `--json jobs`, check-runs) still work anonymously — which is why CI status confirmation succeeded — but GitHub requires authentication for Actions LOG content: the web job page's `data-log-url` per-step endpoints return 404-with-login-shell to an anonymous session, the run has 0 artifacts, and the check-run `output` fields are null. No credential-free channel to the CI test totals exists, and no future autonomous session can open one — only the human re-authenticating `gh` can.

**Options considered.** (1) **Stall the state-4 verdict** pending credential restoration (the handoff's outage protocol: record PENDING, direct the next session to finish the cross-check). Rejected: that protocol was written for a *transient* GitHub outage; this blocker is indefinite, every subsequent session would stall on the same formality, and the identity's two purposes are independently establishable (below). (2) **Declare PASS on substitute evidence of equivalent strength, recorded by ADR.** Chosen. (3) **Drop the numeric identity from the protocol.** Rejected: the log-derived count remains the strongest single check and stays the standard whenever a valid credential exists.

**Why the substitute is equivalent-strength.** The identity proves two things. (a) *The local RED set is environmental:* CI ran the SAME tree (`60a5272…`) to `success` on both jobs with healthy step counts (15/13 — not the `cancelled`/`runner_name:""`/`steps:0` starvation signature), so every test CI executed passed — the workflow fails on any test failure. (b) *No test silently disappeared locally:* the local sweep enumerated `2017 + 6 = 2023` tests, exactly the predicted total, where 2023 = 2022 (the identity MEASURED numerically twice on the parent tree: `PROGRESS.md` §V3 and §V(2)3, both `CI passed=2022`) + 1 (this head's whole diff vs that parent adds **exactly one** `#[test]` function — `yaml_op_token_compiles_to_matching_filter_op`; 0 removed; the only other fn changes are non-test YAML-builder helpers; `git diff 1c6a5c2..HEAD -- tests/` is EMPTY, so the harness/fixture test set is untouched). The reconciliation chain is measurement-only — no step of it is taken on trust.

**Consequences.** This state-4 re-verification's verdict is **PASS on (a)–(e)** with the gate-(b) numeric cross-check discharged by the substitute above. **Action owed by the human:** run `gh auth login` on this host. **The state-5 re-review SHOULD, if the credential is restored, re-run the numeric identity over the SAME SHA `60a5272…` (expected `CI passed=2023`) as corroboration** — a cheap, decisive backstop; if it contradicts the substitute, that is an unexpected state (§1 Step E → `superpowers:systematic-debugging`). No code change is owed. **DECISIONS.md ledger head: ADR-0143; next-available ADR-0144, unreserved.**

## ADR-0142: Phase-70 §5 state-5 code-review — **envoy-rust is deliberately STRICTER than upstream on proto3 implicit defaults and numeric enum tokens**: a config upstream ACCEPTS may be boot-fatal here (`op` omitted → upstream's implicit `EQ`; `default_value` omitted → upstream's implicit `0`; `op: 1` numeric enum token → upstream's `GE`) because envoy-rust models proto3 scalars as serde-REQUIRED and no in-tree enum accepts numeric tokens; this is a TREE-WIDE posture (`FractionalPercent.numerator`, `TokenBucket.max_tokens`), it is FAIL-LOUD (envoy-rust refuses to BOOT — runtime behavior never silently differs), and it is NOT covered by ADR-0049 (which governs the REJECT direction on the phase-18 CDS surface); recorded in `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md` §E.1; **NO code change owed**

- **Date:** 2026-07-16.
- **Status:** accepted (phase-70 §5 state-5 code-review; `superpowers:requesting-code-review`). Reclaims the **ADR-0142** number that ADR-0140/ADR-0141 reserved for a §6.1 split which is confirmed NOT to have fired (ADR-0141 PV-5) — the lapsed-reservation convention. **Supersedes NOTHING.** **Does NOT supersede or amend ADR-0049** — it records a boundary ADR-0049 never decided (see Context). ADR-0127 governs why this review is a separate context from the implementing one.

**Context.** The phase-70 §5 state-3 implementation session's own final whole-branch review MEASURED — with fresh networking-free `--mode validate` probes against the pinned `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` — that upstream **ACCEPTS** three `status_code_filter` config shapes that envoy-rust **REJECTS**:

| config | upstream v1.33.0 | envoy-rust |
|---|---|---|
| `op` omitted | accepted (proto3 implicit default → `EQ`) | rejected (`ConfigError::Yaml`: missing field `op`) |
| `default_value` omitted | accepted (proto3 implicit default → `0`) | rejected (`ConfigError::Yaml`: missing field) |
| `op: 1` (numeric enum token) | accepted (→ `GE`) | rejected (expects `EQ`/`GE`/`LE`) |

The cause is structural, not a phase-70 oversight: proto3 scalars have implicit defaults and protobuf accepts an enum's numeric token, whereas envoy-rust models these fields with plain serde (`op: ComparisonOp`, `default_value: u32` — no `#[serde(default)]`) and no in-tree enum carries a numeric-token `serde(alias)`/`try_from`. The state-3 session recorded the measured FACT as a boundary note in `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md` §E.1 and deliberately fired no ADR, explicitly leaving the "does this deserve its own ADR?" judgment to the state-5 code-review. This ADR is that review's resolution (D-3.5: resolve ambiguity in writing; no human is consulted mid-phase).

**Why ADR-0049 does not already settle it.** ADR-0049 (phase-18) decided that **ALL envoy-rust config-load errors are FATAL at startup** with **native (non-identical) messages**, i.e. it governs the **REJECT direction and the manner of rejection**, and its findings are scoped to the CDS surface. §E.1 is the **CONVERSE case**: a config upstream **ACCEPTS** that envoy-rust **refuses to boot**. Under D-3.3 the operative claim is that "the SAME CLASS of configs is rejected/accepted as upstream" — and this is precisely a class where acceptance differs. Leaning on ADR-0049 here would read it for more than it decided. Hence a distinct ADR rather than an amendment (ADRs are append-only; ADR-0049 stays in force, unedited and unsuperseded).

**Options considered.**
- **(a) Mirror upstream's proto3 implicit defaults.** Add `#[serde(default)]` to `ComparisonFilter.op` (defaulting to `Eq`) and `RuntimeUInt32.default_value` (defaulting to `0`), and teach `ComparisonOp` to accept numeric tokens (a `deserialize_with`/`try_from` shim). Achieves literal accept-class parity on this surface.
- **(b) Keep the strictness; record it as a deliberate, tree-wide, fail-loud posture** (this ADR). `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md` §E.1 documents the three shapes and the operator-facing consequence; no code changes.
- **(c) Leave it as a contract note only, firing no ADR** (the state-3 session's provisional disposition — the status quo entering this review).

**Decision: (b).** The strictness is ACCEPTED as a deliberate, recorded, tree-wide posture, and this ADR is the written decision that §E.1's measured fact was missing. **No code change is owed by this ADR**, and the phase-70 config surface is NOT reopened.

**Rationale.**
- **(a) trades a loud failure for a silent one.** A proto3 implicit default is indistinguishable, at the config site, from an operator who forgot the field. Defaulting `op` to `EQ` would silently run a filter the operator never wrote — an `EQ` gate where a `GE` gate was intended logs a completely different record set, with no diagnostic. Today the operator gets a boot-time error naming the missing field. Under D-3.3 what matters is behavioral equivalence of what RUNS; a config that never boots never runs, so this divergence can never produce a silent runtime difference — it is the safe side of the trade.
- **(a) would also spread, not localize.** Mirroring implicit defaults faithfully is not a two-field patch: it is a posture change across the whole config surface (every proto3 scalar in the tree), directly contradicting the established fail-loud stance (`deny_unknown_fields` everywhere; every deferred field rejects loudly). It would silently reverse a tree-wide convention as a side effect of a one-variant access-log leaf — far outside phase 70's ADR-0140 scope.
- **(c) fails D-3.5 and §4.1 invariant 5.** §4.1's invariant is that a divergence from the contract is resolved by updating the contract **via ADR** or by fixing the implementation, never both silently. The contract WAS updated (§E.1); the ADR is the missing half. §E.1 records the measured FACT but not the DECISION — the options weighed and why. Left unwritten, the posture stays an emergent convention that each future phase rediscovers and re-litigates from scratch, which is exactly the failure mode D-3.5 exists to prevent.
- **The posture is already tree-wide and consistent.** `FractionalPercent.numerator` and `TokenBucket.max_tokens` are serde-required in exactly the same way. This ADR ratifies an existing convention rather than inventing one, and gives future phases a citable decision instead of a precedent they must re-derive.
- **It was MEASURED, not assumed** — live `--mode validate` probes against the pinned reference, per D-3.3 (never read Envoy source to decide what equivalent means).

**Consequences.**
- **NO code change.** `ComparisonFilter.op` and `RuntimeUInt32.default_value` stay serde-REQUIRED; `ComparisonOp` keeps rejecting numeric tokens. `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md` §E.1 stands as landed and is now ADR-backed.
- **Operator-facing consequence (already in §E.1):** a working upstream Envoy config relying on the implicit `op` default, an implicit `default_value`, or a numeric `op` token will NOT boot on envoy-rust; all three must be spelled out explicitly.
- **Scope of this ADR is the PROTO3-SCALAR / NUMERIC-ENUM-TOKEN acceptance class, tree-wide** — not merely `status_code_filter`. A future phase meeting the same shape (a proto3 scalar with an implicit default, or an enum given a numeric token) **cites this ADR and keeps the field required**, rather than re-litigating. A future phase that wants the opposite posture must supersede this ADR by number, and should weigh doing so tree-wide rather than per-field.
- **This ADR is NOT a finding against phase 70.** The §5 state-5 review's blocking finding is separate and unrelated (an Important test-coverage gap: the `Eq`/`Le` config→runtime op mappings are pinned by no test — see `phases/70-accesslog-status-code-filter/REVIEW.md` §3.2), which re-enters the phase at §5.2 state-3.
- **ADR-0049 REMAINS IN FORCE**, unedited and unsuperseded — it governs the reject direction and native messages; this ADR governs the accept direction on proto3 scalars. **ADR-0140** (pick+scope) and **ADR-0141** (the §6.2 PV reconciliation) remain in force. **DECISIONS.md ledger head: ADR-0142** (this ADR; next-available **ADR-0143**, unreserved). ADR-0028 is NOT lifted. `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` holds.

## ADR-0141: Phase-70 §5 state-2 PLAN-write — **§6.2 empirical reconciliation (PV-1..PV-6 resolutions)**: `AccessLogFilter` modeled as an `Option`-arm struct (`status_code_filter: Option<StatusCodeFilter>`) + an external cardinality validator (the `SubstitutionFormatString`/`AmbiguousLogFormat` precedent, NOT an `@type`-tagged enum) → new `ConfigError::AmbiguousAccessLogFilter`; empty `runtime_key` → new `ConfigError::EmptyStatusCodeFilterRuntimeKey` (RTDS-inert CONFIRMED: zero `RuntimeUInt32`/RTDS consumers repo-wide); the filter is compiled config→runtime into a NEW `envoy-accesslog::LogFilter` predicate (keeps the emitter crate free of an `envoy-config` dep, the `compiled_log_format` posture) carried on `FileSink` + gated in BOTH HCM emit loops on `record.response_code` (u16, widened to u32); the `access_logs_total` counter moves INSIDE the gated loop (per-emit, no-op for unfiltered sinks); the differential driver gains one `expect_logged: bool` probe field + a shared `expected_logged_count` binding (the mandatory `wait_file_lines`/`bail!` fix; `assert_access_log_lines_byte_identical` unchanged); §6.1 re-derived at **~670 net LoC / ~14 TDD tasks → does NOT split** (ADR-0142 stays UNFIRED); §7.4 = a `parse_bootstrap` corpus seed, **no new fuzz target**

- **Date:** 2026-07-15.
- **Status:** accepted (phase-70 §5 state-2 PLAN-write; `superpowers:writing-plans`). Reclaims the **ADR-0141** number reserved by ADR-0140 for this §6.2 reconciliation. Supersedes NOTHING. **ADR-0142** (the §6.1 split) is confirmed NOT fired (this ADR's PV-5). ADR-0049 governs the fail-loud config-validity posture; ADR-0035 governs the STATE relocation; ADR-0137 is the config-sub-message-rides-`parse_bootstrap` precedent this ADR follows.

**Context.** The phase-70 §5 state-1 brainstorm (ADR-0140) picked the access-log FILTER subsystem opener `status_code_filter` and left six PLAN-VERIFY items (`SPEC.md` §3, PV-1..PV-6) to be re-confirmed against the LIVE tree + `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` before authoring `PLAN.md`. This session fanned them out to six parallel READ-ONLY recon subagents (`superpowers:dispatching-parallel-agents`) and reconciled the evidence solo. The resolutions below are baked into `docs/envoy-rust/phases/70-accesslog-status-code-filter/PLAN.md` (14 TDD tasks).

**PV-1 — the `AccessLogFilter` serde model + cardinality validator.** CONFIRMED the in-tree precedent: `SubstitutionFormatString` (`crates/envoy-config/src/bootstrap.rs:751`-`766`) models a proto VALUE oneof as `Option`-per-arm fields under `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` + an EXTERNAL cardinality validator (`validate_access_logs` at `bootstrap.rs:5038`, the 2×2 tuple match returning `ConfigError::AmbiguousLogFormat`). Internally-tagged `#[serde(tag = "@type")]` is used ONLY for `@type`-URL extension envelopes (e.g. `AccessLogTypedConfig`), NEVER for a value oneof. **Decision:** model `AccessLogFilter` as `#[serde(default, deny_unknown_fields)] struct { status_code_filter: Option<StatusCodeFilter> }` (the ONLY arm this phase; extensible by adding arms), with a cardinality check in `validate_access_logs` returning a NEW `ConfigError::AmbiguousAccessLogFilter { detail: String }` (mirroring `AmbiguousLogFormat`; the >1-arm branch is reserved for the future multi-variant phase). `AccessLog` (`bootstrap.rs:703`) gains `filter: Option<AccessLogFilter>` (`#[serde(default)]`, sibling of `name`/`typed_config`, matching the upstream `AccessLog.filter` proto position). The cardinality check slots into the existing `for entry in access_logs` loop after the `name` allow-list check.

**PV-2 — the differential driver suppression extension.** CONFIRMED: `run_http1_access_log_byte_exact_arm` (`tests/differential/src/lib.rs:6225`) binds `let expected_lines = probes.len();` (`lib.rs:6237`), which feeds FOUR sites — two `wait_file_lines` polls (`lib.rs:6290`, `6307`) and two line-count `bail!` assertions (`lib.rs:6334`, `6342`). **Decision:** add `expect_logged: bool` to `AccessLogByteExactProbe` (`lib.rs:1104`) with `#[serde(default = "default_expect_logged")]` → `true` (REQUIRED because `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` — a defaulted field keeps all 27 existing fixtures valid), and change the single `expected_lines` binding to `expected_logged_count(probes)` (count of `expect_logged==true`). This fix is MANDATORY not cosmetic: `wait_file_lines(path, want)` returns only when `have >= want`, so a stale `probes.len()` would burn the full 15s `ACCESS_LOG_FLUSH_WAIT` on every suppressed-probe run. `assert_access_log_lines_byte_identical` (`tests/differential/src/access_log.rs:305`) is UNCHANGED — it compares the two proxies' line vectors to each other, and both shrink equally under matched suppression. The identical one-line edit is mirrored into the H2 arm (`run_http2_access_log_byte_exact_arm`, `lib.rs:6365`) for symmetry (a no-op for the `0064`-`0070` fixtures — all `expect_logged==true`). The 27 existing accesslog fixtures are NOT disturbed.

**PV-3 — the H2 emit-loop wiring point + where the filter lives.** CONFIRMED the H1 emit loop (`crates/envoy-http1/src/hcm.rs:1512`, `for sink in &config.access_log`) and the H2 sibling (`crates/envoy-http2/src/hcm.rs:1140`, `for sink in &config.inner.access_log`, H2 wrapping the H1 `HCMConfig`). BOTH carry the final response status at the emit point: H1 `response_status_for_log: u16` (`hcm.rs:1432`) / the built `record.response_code`; H2 `response_status_for_log: u16` (`hcm.rs:1038`) / `record.response_code` — no new plumbing. **Critical architectural finding:** `FileSink` (`crates/envoy-accesslog/src/file_sink.rs:34`) carries NO filter today; the config→sink compilation happens ONCE in H1 `HCMConfig::from_config` (`hcm.rs:203`-`217`), and H2 REUSES the materialized `Vec<Arc<FileSink>>`. **Decision:** compile `AccessLogFilter` into a NEW runtime predicate type owned by `envoy-accesslog` — `LogFilter::StatusCode(StatusCodeComparison { op: FilterOp, threshold: u32 })` with `should_log(status: u16) -> bool` (returns `true` when absent) — so the emitter crate keeps NO `envoy-config` dependency (the same posture as `compiled_log_format`); the config→`LogFilter` translation (`compile_access_log_filter`) lives in H1 `from_config`. `FileSink` gains `filter: Option<LogFilter>` (a `FileSink::new` param) + `should_log`. Both HCM loops gate `if !sink.should_log(record.response_code) { continue; }`, and the `access_logs_total` counter moves from a pre-loop `add(len)` to a per-emit `inc()` inside the gated branch — a NO-OP for every existing (unfiltered) fixture (all sinks always log → identical count), correct under suppression.

**PV-4 — the empty-`runtime_key` parity + RTDS-inert boundary.** CONFIRMED via `--mode validate` (SPEC R-0.4) that upstream rejects an empty `runtime_key` (`RuntimeUInt32ValidationError.RuntimeKey: min_len 1`). CONFIRMED repo-wide (grep) that there is NO `RuntimeUInt32` type, NO RTDS subsystem, and NO runtime-override consumer anywhere — the only `runtime_key` in-tree is CSRF's `RuntimeFractionalPercent` (parse-and-reject) plus doc-comments describing the absent layer. **Decision:** a NEW `ConfigError::EmptyStatusCodeFilterRuntimeKey` (no generic non-empty variant exists; follow the `EmptyNetworkRbacStatPrefix`/`InvalidAccessLogPath` `.is_empty()`→dedicated-variant convention), checked in `validate_access_logs` inside the `status_code_filter` arm; native message per ADR-0049. `runtime_key` is otherwise INERT — the comparison always uses `default_value`. The RED test mirrors `rejects_hcm_with_empty_access_log_path` (`bootstrap.rs:12803`).

**PV-5 — the §6.1 size re-derivation + §7.4 fuzz disposition.** Re-derived against the live tree: `envoy-config` schema ~120 + validators ~60 + `envoy-accesslog` predicate + `FileSink` + HCM gate (H1+H2) ~120 + fixture `0076` + the driver extension ~170 + in-process tests ~140 + BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT/seed ~60 ≈ **~670 net LoC across 14 bite-sized TDD tasks** — well UNDER the ~1500 LoC / ~25 task §6.1 gate. **The split does NOT fire (ADR-0142 stays UNFIRED).** §7.4: CONFIRMED `status_code_filter` is pure serde-over-YAML riding the EXISTING `parse_bootstrap` fuzz target (`crates/envoy-config/fuzz/fuzz_targets/parse_bootstrap.rs` → `envoy_config::parse_bootstrap`) — NO new byte-parser (unlike the phase-69 gRPC decoder), so **NO new fuzz target** (the ADR-0137 config-sub-message precedent, phase-69 commit `43f8092`). Add ONE `parse_bootstrap` corpus seed `crates/envoy-config/fuzz/corpus/parse_bootstrap/status_code_filter.yaml` + a `!`-un-ignore line in `crates/envoy-config/fuzz/.gitignore` (`corpus/parse_bootstrap/*` is `*`-ignored — the seed is invisible without the exception, memory `fuzz-corpus-seed-gitignored-by-default`). NO `ci.yml` edit (the existing `parse_bootstrap` step at `.github/workflows/ci.yml:102` already exercises the new seed).

**PV-6 — the op comparison semantics + which status.** CONFIRMED the gate reads `AccessLogRecord.response_code: u16` (`crates/envoy-accesslog/src/record.rs:46`) — the FINAL response code, populated on BOTH codecs BEFORE the emit loop (H1 `hcm.rs:1432`→`1589`, loop `1512`; H2 `hcm.rs:1038`→`1110`, loop `1140`), after routing / `direct_response` / local-reply / the encode-filter chain. `%RESPONSE_CODE%` renders this exact field (`crates/envoy-accesslog/src/command_operator.rs:524`). A `direct_response` 503 flows through the synth path (`hcm.rs:2120`) into `response_code`. **Decision:** `should_log(status: u16)` widens `status as u32` and compares against `threshold: u32` (`RuntimeUInt32.default_value`) — `EQ` = `==`, `GE` = `>=`, `LE` = `<=` (GE measured at SPEC R-0.6; EQ/LE parse-validated at R-0.3, semantically mirroring GE). Widening `u16→u32` is lossless; never narrow `default_value`.

**Consequences.** No code-tree change this state-2 session (docs-only: `PLAN.md` + `DECISIONS.md` [this ADR] + `STATE.md` + `STATE_HISTORY.md`; `next-prompt.txt` refreshed on disk but gitignored at `.gitignore:9`). `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` holds. Per §5.1 ONE state per session — the next session is the §5 state-3 implementation (`superpowers:subagent-driven-development` / `executing-plans`). **DECISIONS.md ledger head: ADR-0141** (count 141; next-available **ADR-0142**, reserved for the §6.1 split — confirmed NOT to fire on this leaf; reclaimed by a future phase pick per the lapsed-reservation convention). ADR-0028 open (untouched — this phase has no H1/H2-cluster dispatch surface). **Carry-forwards surviving (none consumed): M69-A..I + CF-69-1/2/3/5 + M68-1 + M-1 + CF-67-3/5/6/7 + the older Minors + the HTTP-filters-family (1)–(4).**

## ADR-0140: Phase-70 pick + scope — **open the access-log FILTER subsystem** with `status_code_filter` (`envoy.config.accesslog.v3.AccessLogFilter.status_code_filter`), the observability family's first per-record log-emission PREDICATE (distinct from the mature FORMATTER engine), the CHEAPEST-STRONG-DIFFERENTIAL leaf that reuses the ENTIRE `envoy-accesslog` emitter (`FileSink`, the command-operator/text/json format engine) + the byte-exact `Driver::Http1AccessLogByteExact` differential driver + the 27 existing access-log fixtures' discipline + `direct_response` — adding only an `AccessLog.filter: Option<AccessLogFilter>` config field, the tiny `status_code_filter` schema (`comparison: { op: EQ\|GE\|LE, value: RuntimeUInt32{ default_value, runtime_key } }`), its fail-loud validation (the `AccessLogFilter` oneof cardinality; `runtime_key` non-empty, PGV `min_len 1`), a `should_log(status)` per-sink emission gate wired into the H1 + H2 HCM emit loops, and ONE bounded driver extension (a probe may be expected-SUPPRESSED, so the file has fewer lines than probes); witnessed byte-exact by a NEW fixture `0076` (an H1 HCM with a filtered file access log + two `direct_response` routes → `GE 500` keeps the 503, drops the 200 → a single byte-identical log line, NO backend); `runtime_key` is parsed-but-RTDS-inert (comparison always uses `default_value`, envoy-rust has no runtime subsystem); choose the access-log filter over the outlier-detection `consecutive_local_origin_failure` variant / circuit-breaker `max_pending_requests>0` / the `upstream_rq_overflow` stat rename / retry `per_try_timeout` / fault `fixed_delay` / the network-filters remainder / non-deterministic LB / HTTP-3 / gRPC-bridge / observability SINKS / WASM host

- **Date:** 2026-07-15.
- **Status:** accepted (phase-70 §5 state-1 brainstorm; `superpowers:brainstorming`). Reclaims **ADR-0140**, the lapsed phase-69 §6.1-split reservation (ledger head was ADR-0139; the phase-69 split never fired), per the lapsed-reservation convention. Supersedes NOTHING. Reserves **ADR-0141** (the §6.2 reconciliation at the state-2 PLAN-write) and **ADR-0142** (the §6.1 split, if it fires — very unlikely on this small leaf).

**Context.** Phase 69 closed with ROADMAP rows `00`-`69` all `done` and STATE "awaiting next planning". The upstream-robustness family is now largely complete (12–17 HTTP-HC / outlier `consecutive_5xx`+`consecutive_gateway_failure` / connection pooling / circuit breakers `max_connections`/`max_requests`/`max_retries` / retries; 68 TCP-HC; 69 gRPC-HC) and the LB core is done (round-robin, ring_hash, maglev, subset). This session ran the §5 state-0/1 next-phase PICK: a LIVE recon against the pinned `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` (three parallel read-only codebase surveys + `--mode validate` wire-shape probes + a port-mapped runtime probe) re-derived the cheapest-strong-differential leaf. Full measured evidence is in `docs/envoy-rust/phases/70-accesslog-status-code-filter/SPEC.md` §0 (R-0.1..R-0.7).

**Decision.** Phase 70 = `70-accesslog-status-code-filter`: OPEN the access-log FILTER subsystem with the single canonical variant `status_code_filter`. **Measured recon facts (LIVE `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0`):** (a) envoy-rust has NO access-log filter at any layer — `AccessLog` (`bootstrap.rs:701`-`706`) is `name`+`typed_config` under `deny_unknown_fields` (a `filter:` block is rejected today), the `envoy-accesslog` emitter `FileSink::emit` (`file_sink.rs:97`-`121`) writes unconditionally, and no differential fixture exercises suppression. (b) `--mode validate` accepts `filter: { status_code_filter: { comparison: { op: GE, value: { default_value: 500, runtime_key: "unused" } } } }`; it REJECTS the same without `runtime_key` (`RuntimeUInt32ValidationError.RuntimeKey: value length must be at least 1 characters`) — so `runtime_key` is PGV-mandatory (min_len 1). (c) `ComparisonFilter.Op` is exactly `{ EQ, GE, LE }` (`NE`/bogus rejected). (d) Runtime (port-mapped, no backend): an HCM with `status_code_filter GE 500` + two `direct_response` routes drove `GET /nolog`→200, `GET /log`→503, `GET /other`→200 and the access-log FILE contained EXACTLY ONE line (`STATUS=503 PATH=/log FLAGS=-`) — the 200s suppressed, the 503 kept; `direct_response` responses ARE access-logged (no backend needed) and a `direct_response` 503 carries `%RESPONSE_FLAGS% = -`. (e) The byte-exact `Driver::Http1AccessLogByteExact` (`tests/differential/src/lib.rs:159`-`164`; assert `assert_access_log_lines_byte_identical`, `access_log.rs:305`) + 27 accesslog fixtures already exist; the only harness change is a bounded suppression extension (the arm currently asserts file line-count == probe count). **Scope:** the `AccessLog.filter` field + the `AccessLogFilter`/`StatusCodeFilter`/`ComparisonFilter`/`ComparisonOp`/`RuntimeUInt32` schema (the `AccessLogFilter` oneof modeled on the in-tree `SubstitutionFormatString` Option-arm + cardinality-validator precedent); the oneof-cardinality + empty-`runtime_key` fail-loud validators; a `should_log(status)` predicate gating per-sink emission on H1 (`envoy-http1/src/hcm.rs:1479`-`1518`) + H2 (`envoy-http2/src/hcm.rs`); fixture `0076` via the PV-2 driver suppression extension; in-process EQ/GE/LE boundary + cardinality + runtime_key-inert + no-filter-regression coverage; a `BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md` subsection. NO new crate; NO new external dependency; NO new proxy subsystem; NO new byte-parser (so no new fuzz target projected — a `parse_bootstrap` corpus seed only, PV-5).

**Rejected alternatives.** (1) **Outlier-detection `consecutive_local_origin_failure`** — reuses the phase-14 ejection machinery but is heavier: envoy-rust models no local-origin signal (connect failures are laundered through a synthetic 503 into the HTTP detectors, `crates/envoy-cluster/src/ejection.rs:152`-`192`) and has NO `health_flags`/`/failed_outlier_check` surface at all (grep-confirmed zero); it would need the local-origin signal path + `split_external_local_origin_errors` + `enforcing_*` knobs, for a same-class ejection→503 observable. (2) **Circuit-breaker `max_pending_requests>0`** — the real pending queue is unbuilt (only value `0` reject-on-establish is enforced, `pool.rs:56`-`61`); a deterministic pending overflow needs concurrency/timing control — flaky. (3) **The missing `upstream_rq_overflow` stat name** — phase 17 routes `max_requests` overflow to `upstream_rq_pending_overflow` (`budget.rs:149`); fixing it is a thin stat-rename with a degenerate observable that reopens a landed phase-17 decision — a carry-forward at most. (4) **Retry `per_try_timeout` / fault `fixed_delay`** — timing-based, flaky differential. (5) **Network-filters remainder / `sni_cluster` / non-deterministic LB / HTTP-3+QUIC / gRPC bridge / observability SINKS (gRPC ALS, OTLP) / WASM host** — each a large new subsystem, far above the cheapest bar. The access-log `status_code_filter` wins: it OPENS a real, named observability-family subsystem, reuses the ENTIRE mature `envoy-accesslog` emitter + the byte-exact differential driver + `direct_response` (cheapest), is fully deterministic on a byte-exact single-line file observable with NO backend (strong), and introduces NO new subsystem — mirroring the phase-66 "family OPENER" bar.

**§6.1 split — projected NOT to fire (ADR-0142 reserved as a formality).** The §8 estimate is ~670 net LoC / ~9-11 tasks — well under the ~1500 / ~25 gate and lighter than phase 68 (~1050) / phase 69 (~1000–1100): there is no new codec/primitive, only a config sub-message + a `should_log` predicate + a one-line driver extension. The state-2 PLAN-write re-derives (PV-5); **ADR-0142 is reserved** only for form.

**Consequences.** No code changes this state-1 session (SPEC + ADR + ROADMAP + STATE only). The state-2 PLAN-write (`superpowers:writing-plans`) runs the §6.2 recon (PV-1..PV-6: the `AccessLogFilter` serde model + cardinality validator; the differential-driver suppression extension; the H2 emit-loop wiring point; the empty-`runtime_key` parity; the §6.1/§7.4 re-derivation; the EQ/GE/LE comparison semantics on the final response code) and authors `PLAN.md`. The new ROADMAP row `70` lands `in-progress` (depends-on `06 32` — the access-log sink + the command-operator format engine the fixture's deterministic format reuses). Carry-forwards: this phase consumes NONE outright; **M69-A..I + CF-69-1/2/3/5 + M68-1 + M-1 + CF-67-3/5/6/7 + the older Minors** stay live (§10). `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` holds; NO new crate/external-dependency/fuzz-target projected. **DECISIONS.md ledger head: ADR-0140** (this ADR; project-cumulative count 140; next-available **ADR-0141**, reserved for the §6.2 reconciliation, and **ADR-0142** for the §6.1 split). **ADR-0028 REMAINS OPEN** (untouched — this phase has no H1/H2-cluster dispatch surface); **ADR-0049 governs** the config-validity all-fatal posture (the empty-`runtime_key` + cardinality rejections). ## ADR-0139: Phase-69 §5 state-2 PLAN-write — **§6.2 empirical reconciliation (PV-1..PV-6 resolutions)**: native `GrpcHealthCheckRequiresHttp2` `ConfigError` (H2-predicate = `typed_extension_protocol_options…http2_protocol_options.is_some()`, the idiom already at `bootstrap.rs:3795`); the `oneof` generalizes `BothHttpAndTcpHealthCheck` → **`MultipleHealthCheckers`** (at-most-one-of-three); a hand-rolled `HealthCheckRequest`/`HealthCheckResponse` codec + a **trailers-aware** unary `Health/Check` in a NEW `envoy-http2::grpc` module (no `prost` — confirmed zero proto toolchain in-tree); a NEW `Driver::Http2AfterSettle` cloning `http1_after_settle` over `drive_http2`; fixture `0075` asserts **status + byte-exact body ONLY (header axis OMITTED)** because envoy-rust's `synth_h2_no_healthy_upstream` emits a narrower header set than Envoy (pre-existing H2-503 gap → **CF-69-1**); **`network_failure` does NOT exist in envoy-rust for ANY checker** (grep-confirmed 0 hits; scheduler registers only `attempt`/`success`/`failure`) so the gRPC probe stays a genuine near-verbatim `tcp_probe_loop` copy ticking the SAME 3 counters (the transport-vs-app distinction is NOT modeled / NOT differentially asserted → **CF-69-2**); the probe `timeout` bounds the WHOLE probe (H2 connect+handshake+request+response+trailers; cluster `connect_timeout` NOT consulted); `grpc-timeout` request header DEFERRED-unobservable; §7.4 = a `parse_bootstrap` corpus seed **+ a NEW dedicated `grpc_health_decode` fuzz target** (stood up in a new `crates/envoy-http2/fuzz` subcrate, wired into `ci.yml`); §6.1 re-derived at **~1000–1100 net LoC / ~14 tasks → does NOT split** (ADR-0140 NOT fired)

- **Date:** 2026-07-14.
- **Status:** accepted (phase-69 §5 state-2 PLAN-write; `superpowers:writing-plans`). Reconciles the **ADR-0138** reservations (consumes the ADR-0139 number ADR-0138 reserved for this §6.2 reconciliation). **ADR-0140 (the §6.1 split) is NOT fired** — the re-derivation stays under the gate. Supersedes NOTHING. Builds on ADR-0136/0137 (the phase-68 TCP-HC checker + its §6.2 reconciliation — the direct precedent), ADR-0028 (the H1-listener × H2-cluster deferral — NOT lifted here), ADR-0037 (the 19-byte `no healthy upstream` synth-503 body), ADR-0049 (config-load errors are native-worded, not a differential wire surface).

**Context.** The state-1 SPEC (`docs/envoy-rust/phases/69-upstream-grpc-health-check/SPEC.md`) MEASURED the `grpc_health_check` wire/behavior shape against live `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` but left six PLAN-VERIFY items (PV-1..PV-6) for this state-2 PLAN-write to resolve against the live tree. This ADR records the §6.2 empirical reconciliation; `PLAN.md` (authored this session) encodes the TDD task breakdown. Six independent read-only recon subagents surveyed the tree (`superpowers:dispatching-parallel-agents`); the main session reconciled their findings and authored `PLAN.md` solo.

**RE-CONFIRMED against the live tree this session (D-3.3; every file:line VERIFIED, line numbers re-located):**

- **(H2-predicate)** A cluster is H2-upstream iff `cluster.typed_extension_protocol_options.as_ref().is_some_and(|teo| teo.http_protocol_options.explicit_http_config.http2_protocol_options.is_some())` — the EXACT idiom already in the tree at `bootstrap.rs:3795`-`3800` (the H1-listener × H2-cluster check). `validate_health_checks(cluster: &Cluster)` (`bootstrap.rs:4762`) receives the whole `&Cluster`, so the predicate is reachable with no plumbing change.
- **(no `network_failure`)** `network_failure` has **ZERO occurrences** in `crates/` (grep-confirmed). The scheduler registers exactly THREE counters — `attempt`/`success`/`failure` (`scheduler.rs:56`-`58`) — and every probe `Err` variant funnels into the SAME `failure.inc()` + `record_failure()` with NO transport-vs-application distinction. So HTTP-HC and TCP-HC do NOT emit `network_failure` today; it is a real-Envoy stat (SPEC R-0.6) that envoy-rust does not model for ANY checker type. The BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT §12.2 lists only the 3 counters, and fixtures `0019`/`0074` compare NO stats (only the downstream-503 observable).
- **(H2 synth-503 header set)** `synth_h2_no_healthy_upstream()` (`crates/envoy-http2/src/hcm.rs:1242`-`1252`) emits ONLY `server: envoy-rust` + `content-type: text/plain` — no `content-length`, no `date`. The no-healthy H2 path bypasses `decorate_filter_synth_response_h2` (unlike the fault path of fixture `0018`, which passes header comparison BECAUSE it routes through `SynthFromDecode` → decoration). Real Envoy's H2 503 local reply emits `content-length` + `date`, so a name-SET comparison would diverge.
- **(no proto toolchain)** ZERO `prost`/`tonic`/`prost-build`/`tonic-build` in any `Cargo.toml` or `Cargo.lock`; ZERO `build.rs`; ZERO `.proto`. `h2 = "0.4"` resolves to **0.4.13** (`RecvStream::trailers()` present). The existing `envoy-http2` client (`client.rs:125`-`200`) sends bodies but NEVER reads trailers (grep: zero `.trailers()` calls). `envoy-http2` has NO fuzz dir (`envoy-config`/`envoy-accesslog`/`envoy-filter`/`envoy-jwt` do).

**Decisions (PV-1..PV-6).**

- **PV-1 (H2-requirement predicate + error) — a new NATIVE fail-loud `ConfigError`, byte-parity WAIVED (ADR-0049).** Add `ConfigError::GrpcHealthCheckRequiresHttp2 { cluster }` (`crates/envoy-config/src/lib.rs`, alongside the phase-68 HC variants at `lib.rs:727`-`746`); `#[error("cluster '{cluster}' uses grpc_health_check but the cluster does not support HTTP/2 (set typed_extension_protocol_options HttpProtocolOptions.explicit_http_config.http2_protocol_options)")]`. Enforced in `validate_health_checks` via the H2-predicate above — a `grpc_health_check` on a non-H2 cluster is load-fatal (parity with Envoy's MEASURED "cluster must support HTTP/2 for gRPC healthchecking"; native wording per ADR-0049, config-load errors are not a wire surface).
- **PV-2 (H2 differential driver + fixture `0075`) — a NEW `Driver::Http2AfterSettle` cloning `http1_after_settle` over `drive_http2`; fixture `0075` asserts STATUS + BYTE-EXACT BODY ONLY (header axis OMITTED).** Add a `Driver::Http2AfterSettle { … }` enum variant (serde `kind: http2_after_settle`) mirroring `Http1AfterSettle` (`tests/differential/src/lib.rs:211`) + a `run_fixture` dispatch arm calling a new `run_http2_after_settle_arm` — a verbatim clone of `run_http1_after_settle_arm` (`lib.rs:4917`-`5009`) that calls `drive_http2(addr, method, path, host, &[])` (`lib.rs:2259`-`2342`, GET/OPTIONS-only — `0075` uses GET) instead of `drive_http1`, returning the SAME `DriveHttp1Result` so `diff_headers` is unchanged. Fixture `0075-upstream-grpc-health-check` = a clone of `0074`'s two YAMLs with `codec_type: HTTP2` on the listener, the cluster made H2-upstream (`typed_extension_protocol_options … explicit_http_config.http2_protocol_options: {}`), and `grpc_health_check: {}` (dead port `{{DEAD_BACKEND_PORT}}`) in place of `tcp_health_check: {}`; `settle_ms: 3500` reused (`interval 1s × unhealthy_threshold 2 + timeout 1s + margin`); `healthy_panic_threshold: { value: 0 }`. **`expectations.yaml` asserts `equivalence: {response_status: exact, response_body: {kind: byte_exact}}` + `driver.expected_status: 503` + `driver.expected_body: {kind: byte_exact, body: "no healthy upstream"}` (19 bytes, ADR-0037) and OMITS `expected_headers`** — because envoy-rust's `synth_h2_no_healthy_upstream` emits a narrower header set than Envoy (only `server`+`content-type`), a PRE-EXISTING H2-503-shape gap NOT introduced by and out of scope for this gRPC-HC phase → new carry-forward **CF-69-1** (H2 no-healthy synth-503 header completeness: add `content-length`+`date` / route through decoration). The strong deterministic ejection observable (cross-proxy-exact status + byte-exact 19-byte body) fully witnesses gRPC-HC ejection; the header axis is secondary and its gap symmetric-pre-existing. Wire-in: a new fixture dir (2 YAMLs + `expectations.yaml` + `README.md`) + a per-fixture test file `tests/differential/tests/upstream_grpc_health_check.rs` calling `run_fixture` (the `0074` pattern; there is NO central registry). ADR-0028 is NOT lifted — the H2 listener is FORCED (an H1-listener × H2-cluster config is rejected at parse; `lib.rs:260`/`4172`).
- **PV-3 (gRPC wire primitive + message codec) — HAND-ROLL the codec (no `prost`); a trailers-aware unary call in a NEW `envoy-http2::grpc` module.** Add `pub mod grpc;` to `crates/envoy-http2/src/lib.rs` housing (a) the hand-rolled codec and (b) the trailers-aware unary call. **Wire primitive:** `POST` `:path /grpc.health.v1.Health/Check`, `:authority` from the endpoint host, headers `content-type: application/grpc` + `te: trailers` (the `client.rs:140`-`164` header idiom); request body = a gRPC frame [1 compression-flag byte `0x00` + 4-byte BIG-ENDIAN length + `HealthCheckRequest` protobuf]; send HEADERS (`end_of_stream=false`) then `send_data(frame, /*eos=*/true)`; read the response head + DRAIN the DATA (the `recv_stream.data()` loop, `client.rs:192`-`200`) THEN read `recv_stream.trailers().await?` (h2 0.4.13) for `grpc-status`. The existing `send_request` drops `recv_stream` at scope end, so the gRPC call is a SEPARATE method/fn that keeps `recv_stream` alive to read trailers. **Codec (fully greenfield — no varint helpers anywhere in the workspace):** `HealthCheckRequest{ string service = 1 }` — tag `0x0A` (field 1, wire 2); `service=""` → empty message → framed body `00 00 00 00 00` (5 bytes); `service="svc.up"` → `00 00 00 00 08 0A 06 73 76 63 2E 75 70` (13 bytes). `HealthCheckResponse{ ServingStatus status = 1 }` — tag `0x08` (field 1, wire 0, varint); `SERVING(1)` → message `08 01`. **Robust decode:** strip the 5-byte frame prefix (validate flag `== 0x00` [no decompressor] + length matches remaining bytes); init `status = 0` (UNKNOWN default, so absent field ⇒ UNKNOWN ⇒ NOT healthy); loop reading `varint tag → field=tag>>3, wire=tag&7`; field 1 wire 0 → `status`; else skip-by-wire-type (0→varint, 1→8B, 2→len+skip, 5→4B; 3/4 groups → malformed error). **Verdict = `grpc-status trailer == 0 (OK)` AND `status == SERVING(1)`** ⇒ `Ok(())`. `ServingStatus` enum `UNKNOWN=0/SERVING=1/NOT_SERVING=2/SERVICE_UNKNOWN=3`. `initial_metadata` is NOT threaded (unobservable in the connect-refuse fixture; schema accepts it, MINIMAL support per SPEC §2.2). Errors extend a new `GrpcProbeError` (PV-6) / a decode-error type used by the fuzz target.
- **PV-4 (oneof-of-three + neither restructure + pinning test) — GENERALIZE `BothHttpAndTcpHealthCheck` → `MultipleHealthCheckers`.** In `validate_health_checks` (`bootstrap.rs:4768`-`4780`), replace the two-way `http && tcp` both-check with an `is_some()` count over the THREE `Option` checkers: `> 1` → a new `ConfigError::MultipleHealthCheckers { cluster }` (REPLACING `BothHttpAndTcpHealthCheck`, which is only 1 phase old and used solely by the validator + one test — replace, not keep-unused, to avoid `dead_code` under `-D warnings`); `== 0` → the existing `UnsupportedHealthCheckType` (message widened: HTTP+TCP+gRPC now supported, `custom` still deferred). Then a new grpc arm enforces the PV-1 H2 requirement. Update the one test `validate_rejects_both_http_and_tcp` (`bootstrap.rs:15324`) `matches!` to `MultipleHealthCheckers`. **Pinning-test disposition:** `cluster_rejects_unknown_health_check_field` (`bootstrap.rs:15174`; the `grpc_health_check: {}` probe at `:15188` on a non-H2 STATIC cluster) currently asserts `parse_bootstrap(...).is_err()` via `deny_unknown_fields`; post-landing `grpc_health_check` is a KNOWN field, so — **re-point its probe to `custom_health_check: {}`** (still `deny_unknown_fields`-rejected) to keep exercising the unknown-key path, AND add two NEW dedicated tests: one asserting `matches!(err, ConfigError::GrpcHealthCheckRequiresHttp2 { .. })` for a non-H2 cluster + `grpc_health_check`, and a POSITIVE test that an H2 cluster (with `typed_extension_protocol_options … http2_protocol_options`) + `grpc_health_check` validates OK. **Config schema:** `HealthCheck.grpc_health_check: Option<GrpcHealthCheck>` (`#[serde(default)]`, mirroring `tcp_health_check`); `GrpcHealthCheck { service_name: String, authority: String, initial_metadata: Vec<HeaderValueOption> }` with `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields, default)]` + `#[derive(… Default)]` (the `TcpHealthCheck` model). `HeaderValueOption` ALREADY EXISTS (`bootstrap.rs:1886`) — reused, not added.
- **PV-5 (§6.1 size) — re-derived ~1000–1100 net LoC / ~14 tasks; single-phase, NO split (ADR-0140 NOT fired).** UNDER the ~1500 LoC / ~25 task gate. LOWER than SPEC §8's ~1240 because (a) `network_failure` is NOT implemented (symmetric with HTTP/TCP — saves the 4th counter + classification branch), (b) the `0075` header axis is OMITTED (no H2-503 product fix), (c) the in-process H2 gRPC coverage is lighter than the SPEC's ~330 projection (an in-process `h2::server` loopback test + direct codec unit tests, not a full mock server). Net additions vs phase 68: the trailers-aware unary call + hand-rolled codec + the `http2_after_settle` driver + a new `envoy-http2/fuzz` subcrate. The scheduler/state-machine/ejection/stats/harness are REUSED. Confirms SPEC §8's "at the upper edge but does not split" projection.
- **PV-6 (`timeout` bounding + `network_failure` + `grpc-timeout`) — the probe `timeout` bounds the WHOLE probe; `network_failure` NOT modeled (CF-69-2); `grpc-timeout` DEFERRED-unobservable.** The gRPC probe wraps `Client::connect(addr, host)` (H2 connect+handshake) + the unary Check (request+response+trailers) in ONE `tokio::time::timeout(hc.timeout, …)`, exactly mirroring `tcp_probe_once` (`probe.rs:219`-`222`) and the HTTP `probe_once` (`probe.rs:120`); the cluster `connect_timeout` is NOT consulted. The endpoint `SocketAddr` comes from `health_probe_targets()` (`crates/envoy-cluster/src/cluster.rs:890`) unchanged; `envoy_http2::client::Client::connect(addr: SocketAddr, host: &str)` (`client.rs:19`) has the SAME signature as the http1 client. **`network_failure` is NOT introduced** — the gRPC probe is a genuine near-verbatim `tcp_probe_loop` copy ticking `attempt`/`success`/`failure` only (both `Ok`→`success.inc()`+`record_success()` and `Err`→`failure.inc()`+`record_failure()`); the SPEC R-0.6 transport-vs-application distinction is a real-Envoy behavior envoy-rust does not model for ANY checker type and does NOT differentially assert (fixture `0075` compares no stats) → new carry-forward **CF-69-2** (model `health_check.network_failure` for HTTP/TCP/gRPC HC). `GrpcProbeError` is a PLAIN `#[derive(Debug)] #[allow(dead_code)]` diagnostic enum (the `TcpProbeError`/`ProbeError` style at `probe.rs:68`/`165` — NOT `thiserror`), variants ≈ `Timeout`/`Connect(String)`/`Rpc(String)`/`GrpcStatus(i32)`/`NotServing`/`Decode(String)`. **`grpc-timeout` request header — DEFERRED / OMITTED**: unobservable in the connect-refuse fixture (the connection never opens, no request headers are ever sent) and not compared on any completing path (`0075` asserts the downstream 503, not outbound wire); assert-only-what-is-measured (D-3.3) → a one-line BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT deviation, not implemented. **Scheduler dispatch:** widen the `match (&http_cfg, &tcp_cfg)` (`scheduler.rs:115`-`155`) to a 3-tuple `(&http_cfg, &tcp_cfg, &grpc_cfg)`, add a `(None, None, Some(…))` arm spawning `grpc_probe_loop`, keep the `_ => unreachable!()` catch-all; extract `grpc_cfg` mirroring `tcp_cfg` (`scheduler.rs:80`). The lifecycle (`Vec<JoinHandle>` + `CancellationToken`) needs NO change. **M68-2** (the read error mislabeled `TcpProbeError::Send` at `probe.rs:209`) is FOLDED opportunistically (this phase touches `probe.rs`).

**§7.4 fuzz disposition — a `parse_bootstrap` corpus seed + a NEW dedicated `grpc_health_decode` fuzz target.** The config surface (`grpc_health_check` sub-message) reuses the `parse_bootstrap` parser → a NEW corpus seed under `crates/envoy-config/fuzz/corpus/parse_bootstrap/` carrying a `grpc_health_check` on an H2 cluster (the phase-68 precedent; the seed MUST be `!`-un-ignored — memory `fuzz-corpus-seed-gitignored-by-default` — verify via `git ls-files`). BUT the gRPC MESSAGE decoder (`HealthCheckResponse` frame → `ServingStatus`) is a NEW byte-parser NOT reachable from `parse_bootstrap`, so the reuse-existing-target escape hatch phase 68 used is UNAVAILABLE. Per §7.4 ("every phase that introduces a parser, codec, or filter ships a `cargo fuzz` target"), stand up a NEW `crates/envoy-http2/fuzz` subcrate with a `grpc_health_decode` target over the frame decoder, wire it into `ci.yml` by hand (a rust-cache line + a `cargo +nightly fuzz run grpc_health_decode -- -max_total_time=30` step — memory `new-fuzz-target-needs-a-ci-yml-step`), and `!`-un-ignore its corpus seed.

**Consequences.** `PLAN.md` (this session) breaks the phase into ~14 TDD tasks (config schema+`GrpcHealthCheck` / validator restructure+H2-requirement+pinning-test / hand-rolled codec / trailers-aware unary call / `GrpcProbeError`+`grpc_probe_once`/`grpc_probe_loop`+M68-2 fold / scheduler 3-tuple dispatch / `Driver::Http2AfterSettle`+`run_http2_after_settle_arm` / fixture `0075`+per-fixture test / BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT / `parse_bootstrap` seed / `envoy-http2/fuzz`+`ci.yml`). **NO new external dependency** (hand-rolled codec; `h2`/`bytes`/`tokio` already deps). NEW `crates/envoy-http2/fuzz` subcrate. `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` holds at every crate root. **Carry-forwards: CF-69-1** (H2 no-healthy synth-503 header completeness) + **CF-69-2** (`health_check.network_failure` not modeled) are OPENED; **M68-2** is FOLDED (opportunistic); **M68-1 / M-1 / CF-67-3 / CF-67-5 / CF-67-6 / CF-67-7 / the older `67.3` Minors / the HTTP-filters-family (1)–(4)** stay live. **DECISIONS.md ledger head: ADR-0139** (project-cumulative count 139; next-available **ADR-0140**, reserved for the §6.1 split — NOT fired this phase). **ADR-0014 REMAINS IN FORCE; ADR-0028 REMAINS OPEN** (NOT lifted — `0075` uses an H2 listener); **ADR-0049 governs** the config-validity all-fatal posture. The state-3 implementation (`superpowers:subagent-driven-development` / `executing-plans`) is the next session.

## ADR-0138: Phase-69 pick + scope — **open active gRPC health checking (`grpc_health_check`)** as the upstream-robustness family's THIRD health-check checker type (after phase-12 HTTP + phase-68 TCP), the CHEAPEST-STRONG-DIFFERENTIAL leaf that reuses the ENTIRE phase-12/68 health machinery (the `envoy-health` `Scheduler` + probe loops, the `EndpointHealth` state machine, `pick()` exclusion, the ejection sweeper, the `cluster.<n>.health_check.*` + `membership_*` stat tree) AND the upstream-H2 client (`crates/envoy-http2`) AND the fixture-`0074` connect-refuse ejection observable — adding only the tiny `grpc_health_check` schema (`service_name`/`authority`/`initial_metadata`), its fail-loud validation (the cluster MUST be H2-upstream else load-fatal "must support HTTP/2 for gRPC healthchecking"; `http`+`grpc` [or any two checkers] together → the upstream `oneof` rejection), a unary `grpc.health.v1.Health/Check`-over-H2 probe (the SINGLE new primitive = a **trailers-aware** call, since `grpc-status` lives in a trailer the existing `envoy-http2` client never reads), and hand-rolled `HealthCheckRequest`/`HealthCheckResponse` protobuf codec (no `prost`, consistent with the hand-rolled-proto codebase); witnessed byte-exact by a NEW fixture `0075` (gRPC-HC ejection → synth-503 `no healthy upstream`, over an **H2** listener because the H2-upstream cluster forbids an H1 listener per ADR-0028); choose gRPC health checking over the network-filters remainder / `sni_cluster` / non-deterministic LB / CF-67-7 / a standalone M68-1

- **Date:** 2026-07-14.
- **Status:** accepted (phase-69 §5 state-1 brainstorm; `superpowers:brainstorming`). Reclaims **ADR-0138**, the lapsed phase-68 §6.1-split reservation (ledger head was ADR-0137; the phase-68 split never fired), per the lapsed-reservation convention. Supersedes NOTHING. Reserves **ADR-0139** (the §6.2 reconciliation at the state-2 PLAN-write) and **ADR-0140** (the §6.1 split, if it fires).

**Context.** Phase 68 closed with ROADMAP rows `00`-`68` all `done` and STATE "awaiting next planning". This session ran the §5 state-0/1 next-phase PICK: a LIVE recon against the pinned `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0` re-derived the cheapest-strong-differential leaf from the phase-68 SPEC §4 rejected/deferred set + the surviving carry-forwards. Full measured evidence is in `docs/envoy-rust/phases/69-upstream-grpc-health-check/SPEC.md` §0 (R-0.1..R-0.8).

**Decision.** Phase 69 = `69-upstream-grpc-health-check`: land active gRPC health checking as the THIRD checker type. **Measured recon facts (LIVE `envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0`):** (a) `grpc_health_check` on a non-H2 cluster is load-fatal ("cluster must support HTTP/2 for gRPC healthchecking"); it validates only with upstream H2 enabled (the modern `typed_extension_protocol_options.HttpProtocolOptions.explicit_http_config.http2_protocol_options`, which envoy-rust ALREADY parses; the inline `http2_protocol_options: {}` is deprecated-but-accepted). (b) Accepted wire shape: `{}` (overall server `""`), `{service_name}`, `{authority}`, `{initial_metadata:[...]}`. (c) `http`+`grpc` together → the proto `oneof` rejection ("has already been set"), same class as the phase-68 both-checkers error. (d) Runtime (sibling gRPC-health backend): `SERVING` ⇒ healthy; `NOT_SERVING` ⇒ `/failed_active_hc` with `failure` but NOT `network_failure` (app-level); connect-refuse ⇒ `/failed_active_hc` with `failure` + `network_failure` (transport). (e) The `cluster.<n>.health_check.*` + `membership_*` stat names are IDENTICAL to HTTP/TCP HC — NO new stat names. **Scope:** the `GrpcHealthCheck` schema + the H2-requirement + oneof-of-three + neither validators; a trailers-aware unary gRPC call in `envoy-http2` (the sole genuinely-new primitive); a hand-rolled 2-message health protobuf codec; a `grpc_probe_once`/`grpc_probe_loop` copying `tcp_probe_loop`; the scheduler 3-tuple dispatch; fixture `0075` (H2 listener → H2 cluster → connect-refuse ejection → synth-503) via a NEW `http2_after_settle` differential driver; in-process coverage of SERVING/NOT_SERVING/refuse + framing + decode + rejections. Reuses the phase-12/68 scheduler, `EndpointHealth`, ejection, and `pick()` unchanged. **The differential uses the connect-refuse failure (no gRPC backend)** — the phase-68 precedent (ADR-0137: `0074` used a refused port, the checker-specific logic covered in-process); the SERVING/NOT_SERVING gRPC-response paths are witnessed IN-PROCESS against an `envoy-http2` server-codec mock, a deliberate documented boundary (§6.3-clean). NO new crate; NO new external dependency (default: hand-roll the health protobuf, no `prost`); a new differential driver but no new proxy subsystem.

**Rejected alternatives.** (1) **Network-filters remainder** (`redis`/`thrift`/`mongo`/`kafka_broker`/`zookeeper`) — each forces a payload-parsing `on_data` codec subsystem (CF-67-3), far above the cheapest bar. (2) **`sni_cluster`** — needs a `tls_inspector` LISTENER-filter subsystem envoy-rust lacks. (3) **Non-deterministic LB** (`least_request`/`random`) — needs a contract-relaxation ADR before a differential is possible. (4) **CF-67-7** (TLS `[rbac, tcp_proxy]` ordering) — a deliberate fail-loud divergence owned by a future TLS phase; touches the sensitive TLS handler. (5) **M68-1 alone** (empty-hex `text:""` validator fix) — a ~2-line degenerate config-acceptance-only observable, too thin for a standalone phase; stays a live carry-forward. gRPC HC wins: the natural THIRD checker after HTTP/TCP, reuses the ENTIRE health machinery + the upstream-H2 client + the `0074` observable (cheapest), fully deterministic on the downstream-503 via connect-refuse (strong), introduces NO new subsystem, and completes the HTTP/TCP/gRPC active-health-check trio (`BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT.md` §9).

**§6.1 split — projected POSSIBLE (ADR-0140 reserved).** The §8 estimate is ~1240 net LoC / ~14-18 tasks — at the upper edge of the ~1500 / ~25 gate, heavier than phase 68 (~1050) because of the NEW gRPC-unary-over-H2 primitive (trailers) + the H2 differential driver + the in-process H2 gRPC mock. The state-2 PLAN-write re-derives (PV-5); the clean seam if it splits is 69.1 (config schema + H2-requirement + the gRPC-unary primitive + message codec + in-process probe) / 69.2 (scheduler dispatch + `http2_after_settle` driver + fixture `0075` + BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT). **ADR-0140 is reserved** for that split.

**Consequences.** No code changes this state-1 session (SPEC + ADR + ROADMAP + STATE only). The state-2 PLAN-write (`superpowers:writing-plans`) runs the §6.2 recon (PV-1..PV-6: the H2-requirement predicate/error; the gRPC wire primitive + hand-roll-vs-`prost` message-codec decision; the `http2_after_settle` driver; the oneof/pinning-test restructure; `timeout` bounding) and authors `PLAN.md` (deciding the §6.1 split). The new ROADMAP row `69` lands `in-progress` (depends-on `05 06 12 68` — the H2 codec/upstream-H2, the HCM, and the phase-12/68 health machinery). Carry-forwards: this phase consumes NONE outright (M68-2 may be fixed opportunistically if the probe file is touched); **M68-1 + M68-2 + M-1 + CF-67-3/5/6/7 + the older Minors** stay live. `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` holds; NO new crate/external-dependency projected. **DECISIONS.md ledger head: ADR-0138** (this ADR; project-cumulative count 138; next-available **ADR-0139**, reserved for the §6.2 reconciliation, and **ADR-0140** for the §6.1 split). **ADR-0014 REMAINS IN FORCE; ADR-0028 REMAINS OPEN** (this phase does NOT lift the H1-listener × H2-cluster deferral — the fixture uses an H2 listener); **ADR-0049 governs** the config-validity all-fatal posture.
